chapters.title: Chapter 551: That’s right, I lost
paragraphs: Lian did not give her much time to react, and his left hand came down.
Corrupted Sun responded, and the world changed for a moment, light was no longer only something that illuminated the field.
It had paths, it had reflections, and millions of lines of light that reflected and bounced between different objects appeared in his eyes.
Each of these lines could be a path.
He only chose one, and a very small amount of Eclipse energy entered it.
He chose a line of light that reflected toward three other crescents and had a path, the Eclipse energy moved along that line and corrupted all three crescents.
Tss!
Black light passed through the first crescent, then the second and the third, all three stayed in their places for a moment, and then their edges began to wear away.
And then they fell apart, and the three crescent-shaped blades collapsed almost at the same time.
Seris moved backward, she did not lower her sword, but she did not attack either, her eyes were only focused on the man in front of her, and she was analyzing what had happened.

Her crescent-shaped blades were made so they could destroy anything, change their direction in the middle of their movement, and even leave echoes of themselves behind and make a surprise attack at the right moment.
According to the tests she had done, none of the four elements could disable or stop her crescents.
And those crescent-shaped blades became stronger with every passing moment, and if the moon was in the sky, all of her attacks became up to 300% stronger.

And the moon-shaped shadow that had appeared behind her also became stronger with every passing moment, and every time its color became more complete, until it completely became a moon, it increased her stats by 25% each time, and when it became a complete moon, by 100%.
Of course, the increase of all these things was temporary, and she could not keep it for a long time.
But with all of this, Lian had been able to defend against her attacks so easily and even make the crescents collapse? How?
Neither of them spoke for a few seconds.
Lian did not explain, there was no need, Seris was already analyzing what she had seen herself.
"What was that thing that disabled my crescents?"
"Its name is Eclipse energy." He answered simply.
"Eclipse energy? You got it after your Evolution?" Seris thought for a moment and asked.
"Kind of, what about you? What exactly is that moon-shaped shadow behind you?"
"Moon Manifestation."
"I see, but I doubt you have shown all of its power."
This time, the girl answered and looked at him for a few more seconds, then raised her sword.
Lian understood that she had not only refused to give up, on the contrary, she now wanted to continue even more.
He had no problem with that, maybe from the outside, the fact that they had suddenly started a training duel at the moment they met looked stupid.
But in truth, he could understand that Seris was only communicating through this, she was excited to show her progress to the only person she recognized as a rival and, more importantly, as a friend.
How many other people were there in this world that Young Pendragon would actually want to spend even a moment with? Probably no one, or maybe only Aurelia.
This girl had come out after a month of isolation, and instead of going to anyone else, she had come directly to him and wanted to show him her progress.
The moon-shaped shadow behind Seris suddenly released more light, and ten crescents formed around her.
Lian moved his eyes across them, she no longer intended to test him step by step, and Mana came out of her body with greater force.
The moon behind her expanded, and the empty part of it began to fill.
Almost three-quarters of it had become fully colored, in other words, it was giving her a 75% boost to her stats.
But the field was no longer the same field it had been a few minutes ago.
Ten moon blades were floating around Lian, some above, some near the ground, and some behind the ice walls he had created.
And more importantly, the echoes were also there, and her own main attack was there too, the problem was that every one of these attacks was a smart and controllable attack.
If they were like skills where only a hundred blades were created and attacked directly, there would be no problem, a strong defense would be enough to finish it.
But every one of these attacks that surrounded him was like a smart attack.
Seris lowered her sword, and all the crescents moved.
Lian moved as well, the first blade came down from above, but he easily dodged it, the second moved directly toward him, but he easily broke it apart with his fist.
The third came from behind, but ice rose from the ground and the crescent was forced to change its path.
Seris entered between two crescents, and her sword came down toward him.
He caught it, but at that moment, an echo attack appeared from the left.
His body turned and he dodged it, but at the same moment, another crescent moved toward him.
This time, Lian gathered Eclipse energy in the palm of his hand, and with only a short touch, the crescent fell apart.
But the next blade had been hidden behind it, and the moment it collapsed, the next one came toward him.
Slash!

The silver edge passed through the sleeve of his clothes and the fabric was cut open, but the blade stopped right there and could not go any further, it did not have enough power to penetrate his skin.
Even though the attacks had no real result, the girl’s eyes showed a very small amount of satisfaction for a moment, at least one of her attacks had finally reached him.
"Happy?"
"A little."
It was honest, and it made him laugh.
"Then let’s finish this."
Seris’s expression changed, the moon behind her was almost complete.
And at that moment, as he felt the pressure of the battlefield increasing, twelve more crescent-shaped blades appeared around her.
Silver light filled the field, and she held her sword with both hands.
For a few seconds, nothing moved...then they all came down together.
Even Lian decided not to simply walk between them this time.
Gray lightning burned around his legs.
[ Ashen Thunder Step ]
Crack!
The sound of the air breaking spread across the field, the stone under his foot cracked, and his body disappeared from its previous position.
The first crescent hit the ground, and the second passed through the remaining shadow, the third and fourth changed their paths to chase him, but it was too late.
Young Vorhelm had already moved between them...
Seris moved her gaze quickly, something that no one knew and that it was unlikely anyone would notice was that each of those crescent-shaped blades worked like an eye and an ear for her.

Through them, she could see the entire battlefield and have complete control over it, and something like a three-dimensional map of the whole place where they were fighting was now in her field of vision.
She found Lian, on the left, and at the same moment, she turned her sword, and three crescents changed their paths and sent themselves toward him.
Lian disappeared again, and this time, he appeared close, far too close to her.
Seris did not move backward and attacked directly with all the pure power she had.
He passed beside the blade, his left hand rested on the back of her sword for a moment and pushed its path downward.
The fist of his right hand came up, but the girl was not finished yet, and the five remaining crescents returned from behind Lian.
Lian sensed them.
Seris also knew that he had sensed them, but neither of them stopped their movements, and a moment later, his fist stopped beside her neck.
At the same time, five silver crescents stopped several meters behind him.
Not because they had stopped themselves, but because Seris had ordered them to.
Silence filled the entire place.
The moon behind Young Pendragon shone for a few seconds, and then slowly cracked and turned into thousands of silver particles.
She took a deep breath, breathing a little faster than normal.
Lian also lowered his fist.
Seris first looked at the sword, then at the torn sleeve of his clothes, and finally at his face.
"At least I forced you to use a skill."
"Well, if I didn’t use it, I would have to buy new clothes, and honestly, I don’t like shopping."
"You’re a bad liar." She snorted.
"You lost and you’re still complaining."
"That’s right, I lost." Seris put her sword into the training sheath and nodded, this time her tone was neither upset nor disappointed.
Instead, she was simply stating the result.
Even so, at least in this duel, both of them had been able to learn many things about each other, Lian had seen part of her Evolution, and Seris had seen part of his Evolution.

chapters.title: Chapter 552: A Second Incident
paragraphs: A few minutes later, both of them were sitting on the edge of the field.
The defensive lights of the arrays had turned off, and the servants had still not come to repair the damage.
Seris threw a bottle of water to him, and Lian caught it, took a few sips, and his eyes rested on the girl beside him for a moment.
Her Evolution was truly powerful, just as much as he expected, Kain and Roderick had no chance against this girl.
During this whole month that she had been in Enerva, it was clear that she had absorbed a huge amount of resources and had at least raised her stats to 8000.

The problem was that Seris’s standard of comparison was no longer normal people, of course, it had never been, and she knew this herself, and apparently, this was exactly why she was trying to catch up to Lian.
But Lian had no idea that this was not the only reason, she did not want to fall behind him because she wanted to stay beside him.
Silence covered the area, and they did not know what they should talk about, everything they wanted to tell each other, they had already shown each other during their battle.
Young Vorhelm finally added,
"Anyway, we have a debt, I think it’s time we deal with it."
"What?" Young Pendragon looked at him.
"Dreadmaw Sovereign."
The expression on her face changed at that moment.
It was as if Lian had mentioned the name of something that brought a terrible smell from her memory.
"Don’t say the name of that thing."
"You still hate it that much?" Lian gave a short laugh.
Seris gave him a cold look.
"Did you forget what we saw in that village?"
"I remember."
He also remembered this part unfortunately.
Dreadmaw Sovereign was one of the few monsters that was not only dangerous, but truly disgusting.
"So, what do you think about getting our revenge?"
Seris did not even think and nodded, then calmly added,
"This time, I’ll break its jaw first."
Both of them had become strong enough to face that monster.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps came from the entrance of the field, several members of the young Pendragon generation entered.
Caelen was among them, and when he saw Seris and Lian together, his movement slowed for a moment.
Then his eyes moved over the damage in the field, it was clear what had happened.
"Seris."
Seris turned her head and looked at them, but that look was cold, and there was none of the softness that existed when she was beside Lian.
Caelen took a few steps forward.
"I didn’t think that after receiving the Ancestral Mark, the first thing you would do would be a private duel with a Vorhelm."
"Now you know." She added calmly.
"The ceremony is not finished yet."
"I know."

"And the family is also in the middle of a security crisis. Maybe it would be better—" He slightly tightened his jaw, he wanted to say that at least as a true heir, she should go and take care of the guests.
"Caelen." Seris’s voice did not rise, and the man became silent.
"If I need your approval for my plans for the day, I’ll tell you myself.
The two people behind Caelen exchanged a quick look, Caelen said nothing for a few seconds and then moved his eyes toward Lian.
Not enough to be a threat, but there was no interest behind it either.
"Whatever you want."
He turned around, and the group with him also moved.
Lian watched them until they left the field and then said,
"He’s not happy to see me."
"Ignore him."
"I think he’s not the only one."
"Ignore them too."
They said nothing after that, but Young Pendragon realized that even though she did not like it, she had duties that she probably had to handle, at least some of them.
Especially when a member of one of the six great families had been killed in one of the safest cities in the world.
The next few hours, the investigation continued in the background.
Lian did not go after the reports, he did not need to.
In a closed city with thousands of important guests inside, information moved fast enough.
By noon, it had been confirmed that the murdered Valemont had been found inside his own room, no unauthorized entry had been recorded, and there was no sign of a long struggle either.
The murder had been done quickly.
And all the first investigations still showed one thing, Stormheart.
When Lian heard the report, he did not think about it for more than a few seconds, only the same feeling from before returned.
It was too obvious.
Someone had killed a member of a great family in the heart of Pendragon territory and had left exactly enough evidence for even the first investigation to connect the killer to a specific family?
Maybe one of the Stormhearts had really done it.
It was possible.
People did not always act logically, and maybe the goal was to make everyone know.
Even so, he did not think about it much, it was not as if it had anything to do with him, as long as a Celestial was handling this matter, why did he need to interfere?
In the afternoon, he and Seris were walking around the old part of the estate.
She had also left all the duties she had to Aurelia, and she had no other important official work.
Because of that, they had strangely peaceful hours together.
They crossed a stone bridge with a narrow channel passing under it.
"Where did you go after we separated?" she asked after some time.
"I stayed at the academy for a while, and after that I returned to the Ruined Realm."
"Where in the Ruined Realm?"
"That part is long."
"The story is long, but I met the natives there."
Lian thought for a few seconds and then started, he told her about the Silent Light city, the Sanctuary, the natives of Region Three, and his battle with the Wolf Of Eight Disaster.
And he saw something very rare, this girl’s jealousy.

"I feel like you had fun while I was in isolation the whole time." Seris said with a little regret, she loved fighting, fighting was peace for her, excitement, happiness, and yet she had done nothing for a whole month.
But he had gone through many battles during that one month.

"Well, I guess you should get used to it, you will definitely become the Pendragon heir, and with all the duties you are going to be given, you are not going to be as free as before, which means fewer battles."
"Really?" Seris’s eyes became empty for a moment.
Seeing her reaction, Lian laughed, apparently teasing this girl was not difficult at all.
"Why are you laughing? If I really become the heir, I won’t be able to fight whenever I want anymore?"
"Of course I’m joking, your family definitely won’t limit you, at least not until you officially become the next leader of the family."
That answer did not make Young Pendragon feel more relieved at all, on the contrary, she felt that she definitely needed to talk about this with Aurelia and her father.
They had told her that even after she became the next heir, she did not need to worry about restrictions and could freely follow her ambition, which was becoming the strongest.
While they continued their conversation, the sound of fast footsteps came from the stone path.
An officer from the Pendragon inner forces was coming toward them quickly, and when he arrived, he stopped directly in front of Seris.
"Lady Seris."
"What happened?"
The man controlled his breathing.
"A second attack has happened."
Lian’s eyes fixed on him and he asked,
"Was he killed?"
"No."
The officer shook his head.
"One of the representatives of the Twelve Ancient Guilds was badly injured, but he is alive."
This time, there was a witness.
"The attacker?"
"Not found."
The man paused for a few moments and then his eyes unwillingly moved toward Lian.
Lian immediately understood that the next part of the news was related to him.
"Continue." Seris also noticed the look.
"The victim was able to describe the attacker’s fighting style before losing consciousness."
"The investigators also confirmed the wounds..."
"The attack was caused by the Vorhelm Seven-Doomsday Warform."
Even Lian was surprised, had the Vorhelms attacked one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds?
Could a real Vorhelm be behind the attack?
Of course.
The family delegation was already inside Verendal.
He had no reason to remove this possibility only because of their family name.
But this was not the fighting style of their family, no matter how much he disliked his family, they would never do something like this.

And two attacks against two great powers with two completely recognizable signatures, in less than one day, and inside a city that had been closed after the first attack, this was far beyond coincidence.
"The elders have asked all the Vorhelms to attend the meeting." The officer said.
Who was stupid enough to try to frame them in front of a Celestial, when such an obviously stupid plan would definitely be exposed?

An officer from the Pendragon inner forces was coming toward them quickly, and when he arrived, he stopped directly in front of Seris.
"Lady Seris."
"What happened?"
The man controlled his breathing.
"A second attack has happened."
Lian’s eyes fixed on him and he asked,
"Was he killed?"
"No."
The officer shook his head.
"One of the representatives of the Twelve Ancient Guilds was badly injured, but he is alive."
This time, there was a witness.
"The attacker?"
"Not found."
The man paused for a few moments and then his eyes unwillingly moved toward Lian.
Lian immediately understood that the next part of the news was related to him.
"Continue." Seris also noticed the look.
"The victim was able to describe the attacker’s fighting style before losing consciousness."
"The investigators also confirmed the wounds..."
"The attack was caused by the Vorhelm Seven-Doomsday Warform."
Even Lian was surprised, had the Vorhelms attacked one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds?
Could a real Vorhelm be behind the attack?
Of course.
The family delegation was already inside Verendal.
He had no reason to remove this possibility only because of their family name.
But this was not the fighting style of their family, no matter how much he disliked his family, they would never do something like this.

And two attacks against two great powers with two completely recognizable signatures, in less than one day, and inside a city that had been closed after the first attack, this was far beyond coincidence.
"The elders have asked all the Vorhelms to attend the meeting." The officer said.
Who was stupid enough to try to frame them in front of a Celestial, when such an obviously stupid plan would definitely be exposed?

chapters.title: Chapter 553: Two Attacks, One Conspiracy
paragraphs: "The elders requested that all the Vorhelms attend the meeting."
The Pendragon officer finished his sentence, and silence remained between the three of them for a few seconds.
Lian said nothing.
Until a few hours ago, the murder of a member of the Valemont Family was something he could at most think about from a distance.
Even when all the evidence pointed toward Stormheart, there was no reason for him to throw himself into a case that people many times more experienced than him were already investigating.
But now the situation was different.
The name Vorhelm had entered the case.
And not because of ice, physical strength, or a skill that hundreds of other Awakened could have something similar to.
The Vorhelm Seven-Doomsday Warform.
A style that the main members of the family gained after the age of sixteen if they successfully awakened, something he had not gained.
A style whose appearance could be copied, but copying its real structure was another matter.
He moved his eyes away from the officer and looked at Seris.
"I think our walk is over."
"I’m coming too," Seris said without the slightest pause.
"The meeting is about the Vorhelms," he added.
"And it is being held in our home."
The answer was so simple that it left no room for an argument, and Lian slowly breathed out.
"Alright."
The officer lowered his head.
"This way."
The council hall was in another part of the central palace.
Unlike the room where Lian had seen Rhaenar Pendragon the day before, this place had not been made for private conversations.
It was a large room with a very high ceiling and walls made of white stone.
In the center, there was an oval table that could seat more than thirty people, and behind it were several rows of smaller seats for companions and less important members.
When he entered, almost all the main seats were occupied.
Pendragon.
Blackthorn.
Stormheart.
Vorhelm.
Grandalz.
Valemont.
Representatives of several guilds from the Twelve Ancient Guilds were also present on another side of the table, and two people with Federation badges were sitting at the end of the hall.
The political power gathered in this one room was probably enough to decide all the policies of the countries in the world.
And these people now did not trust each other.
Cassius was sitting in the official Vorhelm section, and when he saw Lian, he only gave him a short look and slightly lowered his head.
Lian went there as well, but he did not sit beside his brother.
There was no place for him there.
He sat in one of the seats farther back, behind the official members of the Vorhelm delegation.
Seris also separated from him and went to the Pendragon section.
She took her place near Isolde Pendragon and sat down without saying anything.
Rhaenar was at the head of the table and was calm as always.
As if his family’s twenty-five-year ceremony had not been stopped a few hours ago, and as if two great powers of the world were not now being accused of attacks in his city.
When the door closed, he moved his eyes across everyone present.
"Begin."
One of the Pendragon security specialists stood up, and a glowing screen opened above the table.
An image of the second victim’s injured body, the location of the attack, and several Mana charts appeared on it.
"The victim is a member of one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds, he has gone through three Evolutions, and his condition is currently stable."
The image changed, and seven red points appeared on the man’s body.
"A total of seven main strikes were recorded."
The fifth one was on his thigh.
But the order of the injuries looked random from the outside.
But not to the Vorhelms, each of the seven strikes had been made with great accuracy, and their structure looked exactly the same as their family skill.
The Seven-Doomsday Warform.
"The victim identified the attacker’s style before losing consciousness."
Another image appeared.
This time, it showed Mana circulation lines.
"But the identification is not only based on his statement, the remaining Mana inside the tissue, the direction of force transfer, and the sequence of pressure were also examined."
One of the Vorhelm representatives leaned forward, looked at the data for a few moments, and then said without trying to defend his family.
"This is not a simple copy."
Several eyes turned toward him, and he continued.
"Whoever made this attack knew the real structure of the Seven-Doomsday."
The atmosphere in the hall became slightly heavier.
Even Lian could not disagree with this result, the appearance of the style could be copied, you could memorize the steps, copy the direction of the strikes.
You could even learn the order of the seven movements, but the result was not only what the eyes could see.
The Vorhelm Seven-Doomsday Warform was a very complex skill, and if the timing was wrong, the style would fall apart.
The person who attacked the second victim had not made a mistake.
So there was one possibility, a real Vorhelm had done it.
Lian did not throw away that possibility just because he himself had this family name.
His family was not made of saints, no great family was, but if a Vorhelm was behind the attack, they had to be inside the city.

First, there were two problems, the Vorhelms were not the kind of people who did such things, and second, there was no one in the entire Vorhelm delegation who could attack an Awakened with the power of three Evolutions.
"Has the location of all the members of their delegation been checked?" Rhaenar asked calmly.
The Pendragon specialist nodded.
"Yes."
The screen changed, and several time points and location records appeared.
"All the people who have access to the complete version of the Vorhelm family’s Warform had confirmed locations at the time of the attack."
One of the Vorhelms had been in an official meeting.
Two were in the family residence, and their internal entry and exit records confirmed it.
Several others had been seen in public areas.
Cassius had already been present at the security meeting after the first murder.
And what about Lian? A short image from one of the internal sensors of the Pendragon estate appeared.
He and Seris were standing together.
The specialist continued.
"No official member of the Vorhelm delegation could have carried out the attack."
"Official member," Gregor Valemont added, putting emphasis on the two words.
"So there is a possibility that another Vorhelm is inside the city?"
This time, Isolde answered herself.
"Since the city was closed, there have been no unregistered entries, and no one can enter without us knowing."
Gregor looked at her.
"Before that?"
"The records of the last seventy-two hours were checked again."
Isolde calmly placed her hands on the table.
"No one matching the required information entered Verendal without being recorded."
A short silence formed.
So either the security system of one of the safest cities in the world had been bypassed in some unknown way, or the attacker really was not a Vorhelm.
Adrian Stormheart spoke at that moment.
"Read the first case again."
Gregor turned his face toward him.
"What does that have to do—"
"It has everything to do with it."
Adrian was calm.
"Because exactly the same thing happened to us."
With a small movement, Rhaenar allowed the first report to be displayed again.
The body of the Valemont member, electrical damage, burned nerve paths, remaining Mana, and a structure that belonged to one of the Stormheart skills.
But this time, the location records of the Stormheart members were also displayed with it.
And the result was almost the same.
The people who had the ability to use the technique at that level had been in other places when the murder happened.

Some were in front of dozens of witnesses, one was inside a recorded business meeting, two were in the ceremony grounds, and none of them could reach the Valemont residence and return without being recorded.
"Do you still think one of my people is the killer?" Adrian looked at Gregor.
Gregor clenched his jaw, one of his family members had died, he was angry, and now there was not even a culprit.
Lian could understand why accepting the result was not easy for him.
But the man was not stupid, and after a few seconds, he said.
"If you say your people were not responsible, then tell me how your family’s power was left on the body."
This time, no one had an immediate answer, and one of the Federation representatives calmly said.
"Two attacks."
The eyes turned toward him.
"Two completely different family signatures, both made with great accuracy, and in both cases, the people who truly have the ability to use them were somewhere else."
He placed his hand on the table.
"So either two independent security systems and many witnesses are wrong...or someone is framing both families."
This time, there was no immediate objection.
Lian was sitting in one of the back seats, leaning against the back of the chair and listening in silence.
The first murder being the work of Stormheart and the second attack being the work of Vorhelm, if they were independent, their timing was far too strange.
But if one person was behind both of them? Then the goal was not only to kill.
If someone really wanted to secretly eliminate a person, why would they leave the name of a family on the victim’s body?
Why would they choose an attack whose source the specialists could identify almost immediately?
The answer was simple, the killer wanted to be identified, just not by his own name.
But there was one problem, he felt that something was still wrong, but he could not understand what it was.
That bad feeling was still inside his heart, and his instinct told him that they were only getting farther and farther away from the truth.

chapters.title: Chapter 554: You Should Have Made a Better Story ( Castle Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian slowly moved his index finger along the armrest of the chair.
Interesting.
Even proving that the two families were innocent might not count as a failure of the plan.
Maybe they had expected it from the beginning.
Because the next question was completely predictable.
Who could fake something like this?
And exactly that question was asked in the hall a few seconds later.
One of the Blackthorn representatives leaned forward.
"Let’s assume both families are being framed."
His eyes stayed on the images.
"Who can copy the signatures of your attacks this accurately?"
The discussion became quiet for a few moments, and one of the specialists said.
"There are many copying abilities."
There were skills that could copy the appearance of an attack.
Talents that allowed a person to imitate another element for a limited time.
Artifacts that could recreate a seen skill with lower power, but none of them answered this question.
Lian also knew why, the first attack was not just "lightning", if it was only lightning, hundreds of Awakened around the world could create something similar.
He himself was an example.
What remained on the body was the signature of Stormheart.
And the second attack was not just a few movements similar to the Seven-Doomsday Warform, it was exactly the same, without any difference.
"We are not looking for something that can copy the appearance of the power, it has to be able to record and recreate the actual pattern." someone else said.
Silence formed, and this time it was different.
The Young Vorhelm noticed the change in the eyes of several people, the older people present had remembered something.
A name.
"The Thousand Faces Mirror." the Grandalz representative said quietly.
Several people almost at the same time turned their eyes toward the Ancient Guild section.
One of the treasures of the Primal Firmament Guild.
The atmosphere in the hall changed.
Among the Twelve Ancient Guilds, the Primal Firmament held a different position, not because the other eleven Guilds were directly under its command.
But in terms of the number of high-rank Awakened, influence, resources, foreign territories, and especially operational power in the Heavenly Realm, none of them could easily compare to it.
In many joint operations, even without an official title, the Primal Firmament was considered the natural leader.
And the Thousand Faces Mirror? It was one of the reasons for their fame, this was a treasure they had obtained in the Heavenly Realm about fifteen years ago.
One of the Federation specialists explained.
"The Mirror can record the structure of a skill or attack after observing it, it does not steal the person’s basic power, but what it records is the pattern of how the skill is used."
How Mana is gathered, how it moves, when it is compressed, what signature it creates when it is released.
And then it can recreate a version of the same attack that is extremely close to the original, with 99.99% perfection.

Lian sat a little straighter, so if the Thousand Faces Mirror had seen the Vorhelm Warform, it could not only copy the shape of the steps, it could create something extremely close to the actual structure.
The same was true for Stormheart.
Everything fit together in an uncomfortable way.
"Do we know of any other artifact at this level?" the Blackthorn representative asked.
No one answered immediately, and then one of the Federation members said.
"Nothing that has been recorded.
Silence filled the room once again, and that silence was the first real accusation.
The Young Vorhelm turned his eyes toward the Primal Firmament section, a man was sitting there who had barely spoken until now.
He looked about fifty years old, with dark gray hair, simple dark blue clothes, and the circular symbol of the Primal Firmament on his collar.
Severin Rath.
The leader of the delegation sent by the Guild.
Even now, with a large part of the hall looking at him, his expression had not changed.
"I’m not saying the Primal Firmament did this, but if the question is who has the ability to do it, for now we only have one known answer." one of the Stormheart delegation members added.
This time, the looks were no longer hidden, and almost all of them turned toward Severin.
Lian organized the information in his mind.
Ability? They had it.
Information? Naturally.
The Primal Firmament had seen members of Vorhelm and Stormheart many times during joint operations.
Opportunity? Their representatives were in Verendal right now.
And as for motive? That part also came to the table very quickly.
One of the Valemonts said.
"How many times have you argued with the families over the division of resources in the Heavenly Realm during the past year?"
Another added.
"Three times just in the official Exploration Council."
The path was becoming clearer now.
Lian had been so busy with his own problems during the past few months that he had not followed the major politics between the powers, but even he knew the basic situation.
Unlike the Six Great Families, the Twelve Ancient Guilds usually acted more like a united group when it came to major matters.
There was competition between them and even hatred, but when their shared interests were involved, they often stood behind each other.
The Six Great Families were not like that.
Pendragon might sign a contract with Vorhelm today and compete with them over a resource tomorrow.
Blackthorn and Grandalz could unite over one issue and become enemies over another.
There was no permanent common structure above them.
This difference had become even clearer in the Heavenly Realm.
A minimum level of sixty was required to enter that world, and because of that, every operational force inside it was considered elite from the beginning.

And the Twelve Ancient Guilds, with their shared structure, large number of high-rank Awakened, and established bases, had managed to gain control of a large part of the exploration routes, mines, resources, and newly conquered areas earlier.
The Six Great Families were not happy with this situation, they had not been happy for a long time.
"If several great families become involved in an internal conflict, who gains the most?" one of the Grandalz members said.
There was no need to say the answer, and the looks themselves gave the answer.
The Primal Firmament and the Twelve Guilds alongside it.
For a few moments, Lian seriously thought that maybe this was the answer.
Tools.
Knowledge.
Opportunity.
Motive.
It fit together too well.
Severin Rath had remained silent the entire time, finally, when the last sentence ended, he took his hand off the armrest of the chair.
"Are you done?"
His tone was calm, but no one took it as friendly.
"No one has officially accused you, but all the evidence shows that you are responsible." one of the Blackthorn elders said.
Severin slightly turned his head and looked at all the faces that were still looking at him.
"Of course, the entire hall is looking at me."
No one answered, and he stood up from his seat, without releasing any power.
But even that simple movement caused the representatives of the other eleven Guilds to give him their full attention.
"So your argument is this, two different powers were copied with high accuracy, and the only famous artifact that can do something like this belongs to us."
"And because there are disagreements between us and the Six Great Families over the Heavenly Realm, it must naturally be the work of the Primal Firmament."
"When all the pieces point in one direction, you cannot ignore them." one of the Valemonts said.
Severin looked at him.
"I completely agree."
The man stopped for a moment and then said.
"Or maybe that is exactly what you wanted."
This time, the hall truly became silent.
Lian kept his eyes on him and was surprised for a moment, the direction of the discussion had completely changed.
"For how many years have the Six Great Families been trying to limit the influence of the Guilds in the Heavenly Realm?"
No one answered, and he answered himself.
"A lot."
Then he looked at one of the Federation representatives.
"Increasing the families’ share of the newly discovered areas."
His eyes moved to Grandalz.
"Canceling some exclusive resource rights."
Then to Blackthorn.
"Opening the routes that our forces made safe with our own losses."
Finally, Pendragon.
"And increasing supervision over the territories the Guilds have obtained."
His voice had still not become louder, but it was clear that he held anger and resentment toward the Six Great Families.
"Where did all these proposals come from?"
"Because the Heavenly Realm is not your personal property." one of the Blackthorn members answered.
Severin smiled very calmly.
"And the land is not the personal property of the Six Great Families."
The air in the hall became heavier, and he continued.
"Now someone is killed inside Pendragon territory, the second attack copies the Vorhelm style, and a few hours later, all of you reach the only artifact that seems to have the ability to do this."
"An artifact that belongs to the strongest Guild among the Twelve Ancient Guilds, which is us."
His eyes moved between the elders.
"What an interesting coincidence, don’t you think it is too much of a coincidence? Or did you really think we were stupid?"
"You want to say we killed our own person?" one of the Valemont members said angrily.

"I didn’t say anything, I’m just looking for someone who has a motive, just like you." He thought that the Six Great Families had planned this from the beginning so they could blame everything on them.
And then he said directly.
"If your goal is to isolate the Primal Firmament and then break the unity of the Twelve Guilds, I expected you to at least make up a better story."
Lian’s expression also became blank, what tge fuck?

"The Mirror can record the structure of a skill or attack after observing it, it does not steal the person’s basic power, but what it records is the pattern of how the skill is used."
How Mana is gathered, how it moves, when it is compressed, what signature it creates when it is released.
And then it can recreate a version of the same attack that is extremely close to the original, with 99.99% perfection.

Lian sat a little straighter, so if the Thousand Faces Mirror had seen the Vorhelm Warform, it could not only copy the shape of the steps, it could create something extremely close to the actual structure.
The same was true for Stormheart.
Everything fit together in an uncomfortable way.
"Do we know of any other artifact at this level?" the Blackthorn representative asked.
No one answered immediately, and then one of the Federation members said.
"Nothing that has been recorded.
Silence filled the room once again, and that silence was the first real accusation.
The Young Vorhelm turned his eyes toward the Primal Firmament section, a man was sitting there who had barely spoken until now.
He looked about fifty years old, with dark gray hair, simple dark blue clothes, and the circular symbol of the Primal Firmament on his collar.
Severin Rath.
The leader of the delegation sent by the Guild.
Even now, with a large part of the hall looking at him, his expression had not changed.
"I’m not saying the Primal Firmament did this, but if the question is who has the ability to do it, for now we only have one known answer." one of the Stormheart delegation members added.
This time, the looks were no longer hidden, and almost all of them turned toward Severin.
Lian organized the information in his mind.
Ability?
They had it.
Information?
Naturally.
The Primal Firmament had seen members of Vorhelm and Stormheart many times during joint operations.
Opportunity?
Their representatives were in Verendal right now.
And as for motive?
That part also came to the table very quickly.
One of the Valemonts said.
"How many times have you argued with the families over the division of resources in the Heavenly Realm during the past year?"
Another added.
"Three times just in the official Exploration Council."
The path was becoming clearer now.
Lian had been so busy with his own problems during the past few months that he had not followed the major politics between the powers, but even he knew the basic situation.
Unlike the Six Great Families, the Twelve Ancient Guilds usually acted more like a united group when it came to major matters.
There was competition between them and even hatred, but when their shared interests were involved, they often stood behind each other.
The Six Great Families were not like that.
Pendragon might sign a contract with Vorhelm today and compete with them over a resource tomorrow.
Blackthorn and Grandalz could unite over one issue and become enemies over another.
There was no permanent common structure above them.
This difference had become even clearer in the Heavenly Realm.
A minimum level of sixty was required to enter that world, and because of that, every operational force inside it was considered elite from the beginning.

And the Twelve Ancient Guilds, with their shared structure, large number of high-rank Awakened, and established bases, had managed to gain control of a large part of the exploration routes, mines, resources, and newly conquered areas earlier.
The Six Great Families were not happy with this situation, they had not been happy for a long time.
"If several great families become involved in an internal conflict, who gains the most?" one of the Grandalz members said.
There was no need to say the answer, and the looks themselves gave the answer.
The Primal Firmament and the Twelve Guilds alongside it.
For a few moments, Lian seriously thought that maybe this was the answer.
Tools.
Knowledge.
Opportunity.
Motive.
It fit together too well.
Severin Rath had remained silent the entire time, finally, when the last sentence ended, he took his hand off the armrest of the chair.
"Are you done?"
His tone was calm, but no one took it as friendly.
"No one has officially accused you, but all the evidence shows that you are responsible." one of the Blackthorn elders said.
Severin slightly turned his head and looked at all the faces that were still looking at him.
"Of course, the entire hall is looking at me."
No one answered, and he stood up from his seat, without releasing any power.
But even that simple movement caused the representatives of the other eleven Guilds to give him their full attention.
"So your argument is this, two different powers were copied with high accuracy, and the only famous artifact that can do something like this belongs to us."
"And because there are disagreements between us and the Six Great Families over the Heavenly Realm, it must naturally be the work of the Primal Firmament."
"When all the pieces point in one direction, you cannot ignore them." one of the Valemonts said.
Severin looked at him.
"I completely agree."
The man stopped for a moment and then said.
"Or maybe that is exactly what you wanted."
This time, the hall truly became silent.
Lian kept his eyes on him and was surprised for a moment, the direction of the discussion had completely changed.
"For how many years have the Six Great Families been trying to limit the influence of the Guilds in the Heavenly Realm?"
No one answered, and he answered himself.
"A lot."
Then he looked at one of the Federation representatives.
"Increasing the families’ share of the newly discovered areas."
His eyes moved to Grandalz.
"Canceling some exclusive resource rights."
Then to Blackthorn.
"Opening the routes that our forces made safe with our own losses."
Finally, Pendragon.
"And increasing supervision over the territories the Guilds have obtained."
His voice had still not become louder, but it was clear that he held anger and resentment toward the Six Great Families.
"Where did all these proposals come from?"
"Because the Heavenly Realm is not your personal property." one of the Blackthorn members answered.
Severin smiled very calmly.
"And the land is not the personal property of the Six Great Families."
The air in the hall became heavier, and he continued.
"Now someone is killed inside Pendragon territory, the second attack copies the Vorhelm style, and a few hours later, all of you reach the only artifact that seems to have the ability to do this."
"An artifact that belongs to the strongest Guild among the Twelve Ancient Guilds, which is us."
His eyes moved between the elders.
"What an interesting coincidence, don’t you think it is too much of a coincidence?
Or did you really think we were stupid?"
"You want to say we killed our own person?" one of the Valemont members said angrily.

"I didn’t say anything, I’m just looking for someone who has a motive, just like you." He thought that the Six Great Families had planned this from the beginning so they could blame everything on them.
And then he said directly.
"If your goal is to isolate the Primal Firmament and then break the unity of the Twelve Guilds, I expected you to at least make up a better story."
Lian’s expression also became blank, what tge fuck?

chapters.title: Chapter 555: Out Of Control ( Castle Bonus - )
paragraphs: The noise immediately grew louder, and one of the representatives of the other Guilds stood up from his seat.
"Today you accuse the Primal Firmament because we have an artifact, what about tomorrow? Because one of our artifacts has the ability to create poison, will every poisoning murder become our work?"
"If this becomes accepted, none of us will have any political safety!" a representative of another Guild said.
"Interesting that the eleven Guilds suddenly remembered that they are all brothers." one of the Grandalz members replied mockingly.
The man turned toward him.
"At least when our shared interests are involved, we know how to stand together."
That sentence had a greater effect than he might have wanted.
"That is exactly the problem." one of the Blackthorn members said.
Now the voices became louder.
"You divided the resources of the Heavenly Realm as if they were your personal property."
"Because our forces conquered those areas." a representative of one of the Guilds replied.
"With equipment that a large part of our industries built for you six families!"
"But our people were the ones who died!"
"As if the families have no forces there." one of the Blackthorn members said angrily.
"How many of your spoiled heirs died to take those lands?" the Guild representative said mockingly.
A chair moved back with a loud sound, and a man from the Blackthorn section stood up.
Mana came out from around his body for a moment, and at the same time, two people from the Guilds also stood up.
One of the Valemonts said something, and Stormheart answered.
In less than a minute, the discussion about who had carried out the two attacks was almost lost.
Now the subject was something else.

Resources, the power of the Heavenly Realm, ownership rights, the influence of the Federation, the Guilds’ control over certain things, and the pride of the families and powers that had built their positions without family bloodlines.
All the hatred that had been kept under the negotiation tables for years had now found a way to come out.
Lian watched from the back seat of the hall.
For a moment, he seriously thought that if someone from outside entered, they probably would not believe that these were the same people who controlled a large part of the world.
Of course, from their own point of view? Almost every one of them had something to say, and that was the dangerous part.
Another pressure started to form, this time from one of the Guild representatives, and the answer came from one of the family elders.
Before either of them could fully release it, a calm voice spread through the hall.
"Enough." Rhaenar said calmly, with his palm on the table.
Just that.
But the Manas that were rising one after another suddenly disappeared.
The Blackthorn man slowly sat down, and the Guild representatives did the same, everyone knew where they were.
A verbal disagreement was one thing, starting a fight in the heart of Verendal?
That meant crossing a line that Rhaenar probably would not allow anyone to cross and remain alive.
He looked around the hall coldly.
"Anyone who wants to argue can argue, but anyone who wants to fight can do it outside my city.
No one answered, but the silence lasted only a few seconds.
The discussion started again, and this time without Mana, but the violence continued through words.
Lian slightly leaned his head against the back of the chair, at first, he himself had almost been convinced.
The Thousand Faces Mirror was exactly what was needed for such attacks.
The Primal Firmament had access to real examples of Vorhelm and Stormheart abilities, they had the necessary influence, and they also had a political motive.
If someone had asked him a few minutes ago who the most likely suspect was, he probably would have said the same name.
But then Severin had spoken, and the worst part was that his argument was not stupid either.
From the point of view of the Twelve Guilds, the Six Great Families had been trying for years to take a larger share of the Heavenly Realm.
If the Primal Firmament was dragged into a huge scandal and the unity of the Guilds came under pressure, the families would benefit.
So why should they not think that all of this had been designed to hurt them?
Lian moved his eyes between the two sides of the hall.
The families and the Guilds, both sides thought they were defending themselves against the other.
On one hand, it was truly possible that the Six Great Families had done it because they wanted to suppress the Twelve Guilds, how could he know that this really was not their conspiracy?
He had never been involved in the politics of the Six Great Families, but he knew how ruthless they were, and this was a plan they were truly capable of carrying out.
And everything was too clean, for example, in the first murder the evidence said Stormheart, and then Stormheart was cleared.
The second attack put the blame on Vorhelm, and then Vorhelm was cleared, the next question was completely natural, who could copy both?
The answer? The Primal Firmament and their famous artifact, the Thousand Faces Mirror.
But if the Primal Firmament was really behind all of this, why would they use a method that would eventually lead everyone directly to their only famous artifact?
They were not stupid.
They were the strongest Ancient Guild in the world, they had fought for centuries, negotiated, and learned about governments, families, and their own rivals.
If their goal was to make Stormheart and Vorhelm fight with the others, the final part of the plan should not have been something that forced all the experienced people present to say the same name.
Unless they wanted to be discovered, but if they wanted to be discovered, then why show the two families as the culprits in the first place?
They could have attacked directly, they could have left a message, or they could have threatened them in another way.
This chain of events was too obvious for someone who wanted to hide themselves.
And it was too complicated for someone who wanted to reveal themselves, so the third possibility? This was a conspiracy by the Six Great Families.
Lian looked around the hall again.
The men who had been sitting beside each other during the ceremony that morning were now talking about ownership of resources, global control, and betrayal.
Severin’s voice was heard again.
"You know the Thousand Faces Mirror very well yourselves, that artifact was brought out of the Heavenly Realm more than fifteen years ago."
"Since then, every important use of it has been recorded, its location has been recorded, and even the people who are allowed to get close to it are known."
"Records can be changed." one of the family representatives said mockingly.
Severin gave a small laugh.
"So now all records that help us can be changed, but the records that are against us are absolute truth?"
The discussion became louder again, but Lian felt that this discussion had no good ending and had turned into complete chaos.
Whoever was behind these murders was truly succeeding in starting a world war between the two sides.
The meeting continued for almost another hour.
The result? Almost nothing.
The Primal Firmament refused to accept even the smallest responsibility.
The other eleven Guilds also announced that as long as there was no direct evidence, they would not allow one of their own to be isolated based on political guesses.
The Six Great Families also refused to remove the possibility of Guild involvement, in fact, they were now even more certain than before that this matter was connected to the Guilds.
Rhaenar did not allow anyone to leave the city.
The Guilds requested that all their members gather in specific areas and have joint security forces.
The families did almost the same thing, and the trust between the great powers of the world had been cut in half in less than one day.
Lian remained in his seat.
First Stormheart, then Vorhelm, and now the Primal Firmament, every time, the evidence had appeared in a way that almost placed the answer directly in front of everyone.
That was the problem because good evidence usually led people to an answer, this evidence seemed to be trying to force the answer into their mouths.
And every time, the answer placed another great power of the world against the others.

He moved his eyes over the people present, his brain was no longer working either and he had no idea, from his point of view, either side could have carried out this conspiracy and each had its own reasons.
Before he could think about it any further, a strong red light above the main door of the hall turned on.
All conversations stopped, and one of the Pendragon commanders entered the hall almost at that exact moment.
The commander looked at the people around the table for one second and then spoke directly to the Patriarch.
"Several powerful presences have appeared outside the borders of Verendal."
"How many?" Isolde slightly frowned.
"It is not clear yet, but the defense system has identified at least five people at the Overlord level."
A heavy silence filled the hall.
Five Overlords.
Outside a city where almost all the most important powers in the world were currently trapped.
"And it seems they were sent here by several great powers of the world."
Lian slowly moved his eyes toward the tall window of the hall, so the news had already left Verendal.
Rhaenar stood up from his seat.
The Guild members looked at each other, and the family elders also became silent, the matter was no longer just a few accusations and a murder case.
Peak powers were sending forces to the gates of Verendal.
Lian slowly breathed out.
Apparently, whoever was behind this game had achieved results much faster than he had expected.
The situation was getting out of control.
