chapters.title: Chapter 556: Another Celestial Is Here
paragraphs: "At least five Overlord-level presences have been detected outside the borders of Verendal."
The sentence remained in the hall for several seconds.
The discussion that had been going on between the Six Great Families and the representatives of the Twelve Ancient Guilds until a moment ago almost immediately went silent.
Even Severin, who was still standing in front of the family leaders, turned his head toward the commander.
Lian sat a little straighter.
Five Overlords.
The presence of even one person at this level was enough to make the defense forces of many countries around the world go on high alert.
Now, at least five of them had appeared almost at the same time outside one of the most important cities in the world.
Rhaenar, however, did not even frown and only asked,
"Who called them here?"
The commander paused for a moment.
Before he could answer, Gregor Valemont spoke from the other side of the table.
"I did."
Several gazes turned toward him.
Gregor showed no shame in admitting it.
"One of my people was killed inside a city under the protection of the Pendragon Family. Then it turns out that the killer is probably not what we first thought, so of course I would ask for backup."
Adrian Stormheart spoke almost immediately.
"I requested backup too."
Gregor looked at him.
Adrian continued without changing his expression.
"We were accused of murder, and that is not something we are going to stay silent about."
One of the representatives of the Ancient Guilds also placed his hand on the table.
"We did the same."
Then another person.
And another.
It soon became clear that no foreign army had suddenly decided to surround Verendal.
Almost all the powerful forces gathered outside the city had been called by the same people who were now looking at each other inside this hall.
Lian moved his gaze between them for a moment.
It was completely logical, actually, and it was expected that something like this would happen.
Valemont had asked for an Overlord because one of their people had been killed, and Stormheart had practically been accused of killing a member of the Six Great Families.
The others who had requested backup had probably done it just to be safe, or perhaps the forces behind them had decided on their own to send an Overlord.
And considering the current situation, the presence of the Overlords could only increase the tension and make it even harder to control.
No one wanted a war, but everyone was preparing themselves so that if a war started, they would not be the first ones to lose.
And this exact preparation was making the chance of a war starting even higher, Lian slowly moved his finger along the armrest of his chair, he did not like this situation.
More than anything, because he had that same feeling from before again, as if every step was creating the next step by itself and that bad feeling was still in his heart.
He was still trying to figure out which of the two sides was the real culprit behind all of this.
The problem was that both sides could have their own reasons for doing it, and he was sure that the Six Great Families also definitely had the means to do something like this.
But which side was willing to go as far as starting a world war? Which side would benefits more in the end?
The commander continued.
"They’re all outside the city and they don’t dare to enter, Your Majesty."
Rhaenar stood up, and this simple movement made the room become even quieter.
Isolde gave her husband a brief look, but she did not ask anything.
The patriarch walked toward the tall window at the end of the hall.
Then the view behind the glass changed.
The towers of Verendal that were hundreds of meters away seemed to bend slightly, the horizon lost its natural shape for a moment and the distance between the buildings seemed to become compressed.
Space simply... folded.
Several kilometers of distance folded in on itself like a piece of cloth being gathered from the middle.
Rhaenar took one step forward and disappeared.
Lian did not even blink for a moment, the place where the Pendragon Patriarch had been standing until one second ago was now empty.
There was no speed involved and the man had not moved from the first point to the second point, he had simply removed the distance between them.
Everyone stared at the empty space for a while and took a deep breath.
Celestial.
Maybe this was the reason for their name.
At that level, the laws that seemed fixed to most humans were no longer that fixed, perhaps none of the laws of the world had any meaning to them at all.
Several kilometers outside the western wall of Verendal, the air bent for a moment.
Rhaenar stepped out.
And the five people standing at different distances almost at the same time turned their attention toward him.
Each of them had a different presence and all five were floating in the sky, with distance between them.
"None of you are entering Verendal."
"One of our family members was killed inside your city." A man wearing the Valemont insignia stepped forward.
"I know."
"And now our people are not allowed to leave?"
"That’s right."
The Valemont Overlord remained silent for a moment, while Rhaenar kept his usual calm expression.
"So, Your Majesty, you expect us to stand here and trust that everything is under control?"
"No, you don’t need to trust me, but you are not entering the city either." The patriarch said calmly.
"My people inside may be in danger." One of the Guild Overlords said.
"They are safer inside Verendal than here.
"That’s what you say."
"Exactly, no one enters and no one leaves, until I give the order, and this is better for all of you, unless you want to oppose me." The patriarch said calmly and then looked around.
All the Overlords became silent and did not dare to say anything more, none of the people present were young or stupid enough not to understand who was standing in front of them.
For a few seconds, it seemed that everyone had accepted this.
Then the sky changed.
The color of the sky gained a strange depth for a moment, as if something was behind it and was now passing through it.
The Overlords around them almost reacted at the same time and immediately moved aside to make way for whoever was coming.
Rhaenar raised his head and his attention became completely fixed on one point.
A man stepped out of the bent space, with almost white hair, a hard face, and a long robe with the insignia of the Primal Firmament.
No huge amount of Mana was coming out of him.

But his presence was so heavy that all the Overlords around him felt as if they could be crushed under that pressure at any moment, unlike the Pendragon Patriarch, who controlled his aura and power, this one did not seem interested in doing so.
Kairos.
One of the main Celestials of the Primal Firmament, and his eyes were directly fixed on Rhaenar.
"Rhaenar."
"Kairos."
There was no greeting between them and the two men simply looked at each other for several seconds.
"Release my people." Kairos said next.
"They are not prisoners."
"Then let them leave."
"No."
Rhaenar’s answer did not have even a moment of delay and Kairos remained silent for several seconds.
"An interesting name for a prison."
"It’s called a crime scene." The Pendragon Patriarch gave a very small smile this time.
The space between the two became compressed for a moment and cracks appeared in the sky itself, as if space-time was starting to crack and could fall apart at any moment.
The Overlords moved back again.
One of them even created a distance of more than a thousand meters without taking his eyes off the two Celestials.
No one intended to stand between these two.
Kairos said calmly,
"One member of the Twelve Guilds has been injured, then a tool belonging to my Guild is accused, and my representatives are not allowed to leave? Rhaenar, do you think I’m afraid of you?"
It was completely clear that he had heard about everything that had happened and knew that his Guild had been accused.
And that was not good.

sentences.text: "At least five Overlord-level presences have been detected outside the borders of Verendal."
The sentence remained in the hall for several seconds.
The discussion that had been going on between the Six Great Families and the representatives of the Twelve Ancient Guilds until a moment ago almost immediately went silent.
Even Severin, who was still standing in front of the family leaders, turned his head toward the commander.
Lian sat a little straighter.
Five Overlords.
The presence of even one person at this level was enough to make the defense forces of many countries around the world go on high alert.
Now, at least five of them had appeared almost at the same time outside one of the most important cities in the world.
Rhaenar, however, did not even frown and only asked,
"Who called them here?"
The commander paused for a moment.
Before he could answer, Gregor Valemont spoke from the other side of the table.
"I did."
Several gazes turned toward him.
Gregor showed no shame in admitting it.
"One of my people was killed inside a city under the protection of the Pendragon Family.
Then it turns out that the killer is probably not what we first thought, so of course I would ask for backup."
Adrian Stormheart spoke almost immediately.
"I requested backup too."
Gregor looked at him.
Adrian continued without changing his expression.
"We were accused of murder, and that is not something we are going to stay silent about."
One of the representatives of the Ancient Guilds also placed his hand on the table.
"We did the same."
Then another person.
And another.
It soon became clear that no foreign army had suddenly decided to surround Verendal.
Almost all the powerful forces gathered outside the city had been called by the same people who were now looking at each other inside this hall.
Lian moved his gaze between them for a moment.
It was completely logical, actually, and it was expected that something like this would happen.
Valemont had asked for an Overlord because one of their people had been killed, and Stormheart had practically been accused of killing a member of the Six Great Families.
The others who had requested backup had probably done it just to be safe, or perhaps the forces behind them had decided on their own to send an Overlord.
And considering the current situation, the presence of the Overlords could only increase the tension and make it even harder to control.
No one wanted a war, but everyone was preparing themselves so that if a war started, they would not be the first ones to lose.
And this exact preparation was making the chance of a war starting even higher, Lian slowly moved his finger along the armrest of his chair, he did not like this situation.
More than anything, because he had that same feeling from before again, as if every step was creating the next step by itself and that bad feeling was still in his heart.
He was still trying to figure out which of the two sides was the real culprit behind all of this.
The problem was that both sides could have their own reasons for doing it, and he was sure that the Six Great Families also definitely had the means to do something like this.
But which side was willing to go as far as starting a world war?
Which side would benefits more in the end?
The commander continued.
"They’re all outside the city and they don’t dare to enter, Your Majesty."
Rhaenar stood up, and this simple movement made the room become even quieter.
Isolde gave her husband a brief look, but she did not ask anything.
The patriarch walked toward the tall window at the end of the hall.
Then the view behind the glass changed.
The towers of Verendal that were hundreds of meters away seemed to bend slightly, the horizon lost its natural shape for a moment and the distance between the buildings seemed to become compressed.
Space simply... folded.
Several kilometers of distance folded in on itself like a piece of cloth being gathered from the middle.
Rhaenar took one step forward and disappeared.
Lian did not even blink for a moment, the place where the Pendragon Patriarch had been standing until one second ago was now empty.
There was no speed involved and the man had not moved from the first point to the second point, he had simply removed the distance between them.
Everyone stared at the empty space for a while and took a deep breath.
Celestial.
Maybe this was the reason for their name.
At that level, the laws that seemed fixed to most humans were no longer that fixed, perhaps none of the laws of the world had any meaning to them at all.
Several kilometers outside the western wall of Verendal, the air bent for a moment.
Rhaenar stepped out.
And the five people standing at different distances almost at the same time turned their attention toward him.
Each of them had a different presence and all five were floating in the sky, with distance between them.
"None of you are entering Verendal."
"One of our family members was killed inside your city." A man wearing the Valemont insignia stepped forward.
"I know."
"And now our people are not allowed to leave?"
"That’s right."
The Valemont Overlord remained silent for a moment, while Rhaenar kept his usual calm expression.
"So, Your Majesty, you expect us to stand here and trust that everything is under control?"
"No, you don’t need to trust me, but you are not entering the city either." The patriarch said calmly.
"My people inside may be in danger." One of the Guild Overlords said.
"They are safer inside Verendal than here.
"That’s what you say."
"Exactly, no one enters and no one leaves, until I give the order, and this is better for all of you, unless you want to oppose me." The patriarch said calmly and then looked around.
All the Overlords became silent and did not dare to say anything more, none of the people present were young or stupid enough not to understand who was standing in front of them.
For a few seconds, it seemed that everyone had accepted this.
Then the sky changed.
The color of the sky gained a strange depth for a moment, as if something was behind it and was now passing through it.
The Overlords around them almost reacted at the same time and immediately moved aside to make way for whoever was coming.
Rhaenar raised his head and his attention became completely fixed on one point.
A man stepped out of the bent space, with almost white hair, a hard face, and a long robe with the insignia of the Primal Firmament.
No huge amount of Mana was coming out of him.

But his presence was so heavy that all the Overlords around him felt as if they could be crushed under that pressure at any moment, unlike the Pendragon Patriarch, who controlled his aura and power, this one did not seem interested in doing so.
Kairos.
One of the main Celestials of the Primal Firmament, and his eyes were directly fixed on Rhaenar.
"Rhaenar."
"Kairos."
There was no greeting between them and the two men simply looked at each other for several seconds.
"Release my people." Kairos said next.
"They are not prisoners."
"Then let them leave."
"No."
Rhaenar’s answer did not have even a moment of delay and Kairos remained silent for several seconds.
"An interesting name for a prison."
"It’s called a crime scene." The Pendragon Patriarch gave a very small smile this time.
The space between the two became compressed for a moment and cracks appeared in the sky itself, as if space-time was starting to crack and could fall apart at any moment.
The Overlords moved back again.
One of them even created a distance of more than a thousand meters without taking his eyes off the two Celestials.
No one intended to stand between these two.
Kairos said calmly,
"One member of the Twelve Guilds has been injured, then a tool belonging to my Guild is accused, and my representatives are not allowed to leave?
Rhaenar, do you think I’m afraid of you?"
It was completely clear that he had heard about everything that had happened and knew that his Guild had been accused.
And that was not good.

chapters.title: Chapter 557: Who Benefits the Most?
paragraphs: Rhaenar felt a slight headache, this matter was slowly starting to bother him too, how had everything come to this?
Then he calmly added,
"And two Great Families were accused before you."
"So your problem isn’t with us?" Kairos thought for a moment and then asked.
"My problem is with whoever is killing people inside my city, until I find them, no one leaves." He was now even more determined not to allow anyone to leave.
He knew that if both sides left the city now without finding the real culprit, the two sides would develop a deep hatred for each other and this matter could reach very dangerous levels.
Kairos looked at him for several moments and Rhaenar did not look away either, neither of them attacked but neither of them could leave the place.
Kairos could not enter Pendragon territory without permission; such a move in the presence of the Patriarch would mean much more than simply "checking the situation of his people."
Rhaenar also could not simply turn his back and return to the city.
As long as a Celestial from the power that was currently being accused was standing several kilometers away, leaving this place would not be a reasonable choice.
Two people, without even throwing a single attack, had stopped each other right there.
Inside the hall, Isolde looked at Rhaenar’s empty seat for only a few seconds and then sat down.
"We continue."
Her tone had not changed at all, if anyone had expected Rhaenar leaving the command center of Verendal to throw everything into chaos, they were disappointed very quickly.
She turned toward everyone and said,
"All delegations will remain inside their assigned areas until further notice, movement between sections will only be allowed with registration and an escort from the internal forces."
"Place barrier forces between the residential areas, no unit from any Family or Guild is allowed to change its location without registration."
Then she looked at the person in charge of the information systems.
"Lock all security data related to the attacks in three independent copies, no one, not even our own people, should have individual access to the original copy."
Lian watched everything from the back of the hall.
Isolde was not exactly like Rhaenar.
Rhaenar’s presence made others understand by themselves where they needed to stop.
But this woman set the boundaries herself, however, the real limitation quickly became clear even to her.
She could create order, she could close the halls, she could separate the forces and she could place dozens of layers of security around the city.
But she could not order anyone to trust.
Mental communications began, everyone wanted to speak with the forces behind them once again.
One of the Stormheart elders closed his eyes and remained still for a few seconds, when he raised his eyes again, his expression had become a little harder.
The Valemont representative did the same.
And one by one, everyone contacted the forces behind them and
Lian could not hear the content of the conversations.
But he did not need to because their effects were completely clear.
Someone who had been willing to cooperate to some extent with the joint investigation group before the communication became more careful after a few minutes.
One of the elders who was still sitting beside the representative of another Family moved his chair slightly backward.
The Primal Firmament gathered its own people closer together.
The people outside were probably saying something similar, be careful and do not trust anyone, keep your people separated until the truth is clear.
From each person’s point of view, it was a completely reasonable suggestion, but when eighteen different powers were following the same suggestion at the same time, the result was something else.
Lian gave a very faint smirk, the same problem again, individual decisions that were logical were creating a stupid result when put together.
No one wanted to make the crisis worse but everyone was doing exactly that.
The discussion continued for another twenty minutes, but no new issue was solved, the direct accusations had become fewer, but the trust had not increased either.
In the end, Isolde tapped her fingers on the table once.
"Enough."
Her voice was not loud but the conversations stopped one after another, she moved her gaze between both sides of the table.
"Even if we repeat the same words until midnight, the killer will not be found and none of you will suddenly decide to trust the other side."
No one said anything.
"Twenty-four hours, every power currently inside Verendal has twenty-four hours to check its evidence and collect anything it thinks is related to the case."
"With what access?" Severin asked.
"Every Family and every Guild will introduce a limited number of specialists, all security information related to the two attacks will be given to the investigation groups at the same time."
Isolde placed her finger on the table.
"No data will remain only in the hands of the Pendragon Family, every copy will be given to several groups at the same time so no one can claim that something was changed."
No one objected, it was a reasonable suggestion.
"No new accusation will be made public without evidence and no guest will leave the city, and no foreign force will enter either."
Then her gaze stayed on the Guild representatives for a moment.
"Tomorrow, at this same time, we will gather here again."
"And what if one of the sides does not accept this ceasefire?" one of the Blackthorn members asked.
The Matriarch answered just as calmly.
"Then their problem will no longer be with the other side, they will be dealing with the Pendragon Family."
There was no doubt left.
Naturally, not everyone agreed at that exact moment, one of the Guild representatives objected to the reliability of the security information.
Isolde allowed their own specialists to check the raw version of the data as well.
Valemont asked for more people to join the investigation.
But a specific number was set for all sides.
Stormheart requested that the evidence related to the first murder be checked again by an independent specialist.
It was accepted.
Severin remained almost completely silent for most of the time and finally said,
"So if no evidence against us is found within twenty-four hours, all Six Great Families must apologize to us."
The representatives of the Six Great Families frowned and the tension rose again, they were the Six Great Families!
None of them were willing to apologize to one of the Twelve Guilds under any circumstances and they did not see any reason to do so either.
Isolde frowned, all the peace she had worked for had started to crack again.
"We will see what happens." In the end, she neither accepted nor rejected it, she could not force the Six Great Families to apologize.
Severin did not say anything more after that and only snorted.
After that, the resistance of the others also slowly broke down, not because trust had returned, but because what other choice did they have?
Five Overlords outside the city and two Celestials now standing against each other.
And eighteen great powers that might not even have the chance to explain themselves if one person made a mistake.
Twenty-four hours was the best thing they had for now.
The meeting was almost over when one of the Primal Firmament members raised a new issue.
"Our people will remain in an independent section until the end of these twenty-four hours."
"Your residential area has already been decided." One of the Pendragon elders looked at him.

"I mean independent from the shared movement network, until we know who is behind these attacks, I do not want my Guild members to pass through a hallway or system that the other accused group also has access to."
"We want the same thing." Adrian Stormheart immediately said.
"And us." Gregor Valemont added very quickly.
Then Blackthorn, another Guild and within a few minutes, almost everyone had the same request.
Lian looked at Isolde’s expression, the woman did not answer immediately, not because the request was unreasonable but exactly the opposite, from a security point of view it was very reasonable.
If you did not know who the enemy was, reducing the points of contact between the powers was the best way to prevent a third attack.
"The separation security protocol will be activated."
"Until the end of the ceasefire, Verendal will be divided into independent security areas, movement between the sections will only be activated with direct permission from the center."
Her gaze moved across the group.
"This means that even Pendragon forces will not enter your areas without registration." Doing this was not difficult.

chapters.title: Chapter 558: A Perfect Chain of Events
paragraphs: Such a thing could easily be done with the formations, and the entire city had a defensive formation system that was also capable of doing this.
The formation could only be rewritten.
The objections became fewer and almost everyone was satisfied with this decision.
Lian also saw no problem with it at first glance.
If thousands of people from powers that now suspected each other were going to remain inside the city for an entire day, separating them from each other would greatly reduce the chance of a conflict.
It was the right decision and this was how the meeting ended.
After leaving the hall, he remained alone for a few minutes, Cassius had gone to the Vorhelm section with the elders of the Family.
The Guild members were also moving mostly in their own closed groups, the atmosphere of the palace was strangely different from the morning.
At that time, the representatives of all the powers had sat beside each other at a ceremony, now even in the hallways the natural distance between the groups had become greater.
Lian entered the garden through one of the side exits and only a few minutes had passed when he heard a familiar voice from behind.
"Lian."
Seris was approaching from the stone path.
She had changed out of the formal clothes from the ceremony and was now wearing her simpler white and black clothes, but the Ancestral Mark could still be seen on the back of her right hand.
Lian waited for her to come closer.
"I didn’t think the ceremony would turn out like this." She thought for a moment and added,
"No one thought it would, well, except the one responsible for something like this."
"That’s true." The Young Pendragon nodded and after thinking for a moment added, "Do you think it was the Primal Firmament?" and added,
"They have the ability to do it too, and maybe they are trying to make the Six Great Families enter a conflict."
"I don’t know, I feel like both sides could do this, we just need to see which side benefits more from it." Lian answered simply.
The girl fell into thought for a moment, she had no bias that would make her say it was definitely the work of the Twelve Ancient Guilds, instead, she felt that his opinion was completely logical.

"But which side benefits more? From this point of view, it should be the Six Great Families, it gives them an excuse to suppress the Twelve Guilds, which have gained a lot of power over the years because of their alliance." She reasoned and then added,

"The Twelve Guilds get no benefit from this, on the contrary, they would be forced into a war that would eventually hurt them, they are already growing like this, so why would they create trouble for themselves?"
"So in the end, there is a hidden plan from the Six Great Families?" Seris concluded.
As they walked, the two of them moved toward a terrace that overlooked a large part of Verendal.
There were more soldiers at the intersections and the guest groups were moving toward their assigned areas.
"It’s not only that, but something did not make sense from the very beginning." Lian added another point after thinking for a moment.
He looked at the city for a few seconds.
Where should he start?
"First, Valemont, one of their people gets killed and all the evidence points to Stormheart."
"Then they investigate and it turns out Stormheart could not have carried out the attack."
Seris nodded.
"Then someone from the Twelve Guilds is attacked."

And this time all the accusations point toward the Vorhelms, and this time there was a witness, the same person who was attacked, and he said that the attack was carried out by the Vorhelm Warform Seven-Doomsday.
"And again, when they investigate, we are cleared too."
"Then the question becomes who can imitate both of them." Seris said calmly.
Lian looked at her.
"The Primal Firmament with the Thousand Faces Mirror artifact."
"Yeah.
For a few seconds, both of them remained silent.
"And you don’t think it was them." She added, she could see where this argument was going.
The Young Pendragon raised his shoulder slightly.
"I don’t know."
This time, he really meant it.
"It could be, but something is bothering me."
"What?"
Lian searched for the most exact word for a few seconds and then said,
"It’s going too neatly."
Seris waited for him to continue.
"Every time something happens, a clear answer appears in front of everyone. First Stormheart, then Vorhelm, then the Primal Firmament."
He paused for a moment.
"But the first answer was wrong, the second answer was wrong too."
"So you think the third one is wrong too?" Seris raised her eyebrows.
"Maybe, more than that... I feel like we’re following a script."
"The first murder happened."
The result?
"Verendal was locked down."
"The second attack happened."
Vorhelm also became part of the case.
Then when it became clear that two different powers had been copied, everyone naturally went to the only thing that could make such an imitation.
The Thousand Faces Mirror.
The result? The Twelve Guilds stood behind the Primal Firmament and the Six Great Families stood against them.
Then the Overlords were sent and now another Celestial was standing outside Verendal.
"None of these reactions were strange."
That was exactly the problem.
"Everyone did almost exactly what was expected of them."
"Which means someone calculated the reactions in advance." Seris looked at the city below for a few seconds and then said calmly,
"If my guess is right, the person behind all of this not only knows what powers the Families have or what effect each Guild has, but also knows how they will act when pressure is put on them."
This part was the worst of all.

To copy a skill, you needed to identify its structure, and to design a chain like this, you had to know the political conflicts, the pride of the Families, the interests of the Guilds, and the limits of all of them.
"Doesn’t this make it even more logical that it was the Six Great Families?" Seris looked at him.
Lian did not answer for several seconds.
The Six Great Families and the Twelve Guilds were now practically standing against each other in two different blocks.
The Overlords were outside and two Celestials were standing not far away, if someone wanted to push the world into a crisis, they had done a good job so far.
The Six Great Families were also the only ones who could design such a complicated plan, they knew each other’s personalities and knew how each of them would react.
They even had the motive, not necessarily to destroy the Twelve Guilds, but to have an excuse to suppress and weaken them.

But was it the work of all Six Great Families or only one of them? Considering that the Six Great Families had pushed the accusations toward the Twelve Guilds, it was clear that if they were behind it, then it was a plan involving all of them.
But something was still bothering him, was weakening the Twelve Guilds really worth putting the world into such a crisis? When the situation of the world was already not good?
"Maybe, if the goal is an excuse to suppress and weaken the Twelve Guilds, they already have it now."
"Then what’s the problem?"
"I don’t know."
This time, his answer was honest.
"I just have a feeling that this... is the result of all these chain events, not the final goal."
Seris said nothing, perhaps because she did not have an answer either, both of them only knew that something was wrong but they still did not know exactly which part.
Whatever it was, they had become fairly sure that this plan was the work of the Six Great Families, including both of their Families, they just could not understand whether it was really worth it.
Was the only thing the Six Great Families would gain the suppression and weakening of the Twelve Ancient Guilds? Or was there another goal behind all of this?
Unfortunately for Seris, even though she was practically the next heir, she was not allowed into the major political matters, not to mention that she herself had no interest in them.
Maybe talking to her father or mother could give her the answers to her questions.
Although before she had the chance to do that... Boom!
A deep sound passed from beneath the city and both of them almost raised their heads at the same time.
It did not seem like an explosion or an earthquake, but more like the sound of a huge machine starting up deep underground.
Lian turned back toward the city.
The golden lights that ran along the towers and main buildings lit up one after another.
First the northern section, then the west, the east, and the paths of light turned the entire city into a huge network for several seconds.
Then some lines turned off and new paths formed in their place.
Several sections that had been directly connected to the center until that moment were separated from it and formed independent rings.
Lian watched carefully.
"Is this the security separation?"
Seris nodded and her eyes moved along the Mana lines of the city.
"My mother divided the internal network."
From a security point of view, it was completely logical.
Under normal conditions, most of Verendal’s systems were connected to each other through one large network.
Now each important guest section would have separate protection.
If someone wanted to attack another section, they could no longer freely use the same paths as before.

Because Seris suddenly fell to the ground.
"What—" Lian’s sentence was not completed.
And a painful scream came from the girl.
"Ahhh—aghhh!"

sentences.text: Such a thing could easily be done with the formations, and the entire city had a defensive formation system that was also capable of doing this.
The formation could only be rewritten.
The objections became fewer and almost everyone was satisfied with this decision.
Lian also saw no problem with it at first glance.
If thousands of people from powers that now suspected each other were going to remain inside the city for an entire day, separating them from each other would greatly reduce the chance of a conflict.
It was the right decision and this was how the meeting ended.
After leaving the hall, he remained alone for a few minutes, Cassius had gone to the Vorhelm section with the elders of the Family.
The Guild members were also moving mostly in their own closed groups, the atmosphere of the palace was strangely different from the morning.
At that time, the representatives of all the powers had sat beside each other at a ceremony, now even in the hallways the natural distance between the groups had become greater.
Lian entered the garden through one of the side exits and only a few minutes had passed when he heard a familiar voice from behind.
"Lian."
Seris was approaching from the stone path.
She had changed out of the formal clothes from the ceremony and was now wearing her simpler white and black clothes, but the Ancestral Mark could still be seen on the back of her right hand.
Lian waited for her to come closer.
"I didn’t think the ceremony would turn out like this." She thought for a moment and added,
"No one thought it would, well, except the one responsible for something like this."
"That’s true." The Young Pendragon nodded and after thinking for a moment added, "Do you think it was the Primal Firmament?" and added,
"They have the ability to do it too, and maybe they are trying to make the Six Great Families enter a conflict."
"I don’t know, I feel like both sides could do this, we just need to see which side benefits more from it." Lian answered simply.
The girl fell into thought for a moment, she had no bias that would make her say it was definitely the work of the Twelve Ancient Guilds, instead, she felt that his opinion was completely logical.
"But which side benefits more?

From this point of view, it should be the Six Great Families, it gives them an excuse to suppress the Twelve Guilds, which have gained a lot of power over the years because of their alliance." She reasoned and then added,

"The Twelve Guilds get no benefit from this, on the contrary, they would be forced into a war that would eventually hurt them, they are already growing like this, so why would they create trouble for themselves?"
"So in the end, there is a hidden plan from the Six Great Families?" Seris concluded.
As they walked, the two of them moved toward a terrace that overlooked a large part of Verendal.
There were more soldiers at the intersections and the guest groups were moving toward their assigned areas.
"It’s not only that, but something did not make sense from the very beginning." Lian added another point after thinking for a moment.
He looked at the city for a few seconds.
Where should he start?
"First, Valemont, one of their people gets killed and all the evidence points to Stormheart."
"Then they investigate and it turns out Stormheart could not have carried out the attack."
Seris nodded.
"Then someone from the Twelve Guilds is attacked."

And this time all the accusations point toward the Vorhelms, and this time there was a witness, the same person who was attacked, and he said that the attack was carried out by the Vorhelm Warform Seven-Doomsday.
"And again, when they investigate, we are cleared too."
"Then the question becomes who can imitate both of them." Seris said calmly.
Lian looked at her.
"The Primal Firmament with the Thousand Faces Mirror artifact."
"Yeah.
For a few seconds, both of them remained silent.
"And you don’t think it was them." She added, she could see where this argument was going.
The Young Pendragon raised his shoulder slightly.
"I don’t know."
This time, he really meant it.
"It could be, but something is bothering me."
"What?"
Lian searched for the most exact word for a few seconds and then said,
"It’s going too neatly."
Seris waited for him to continue.
"Every time something happens, a clear answer appears in front of everyone.
First Stormheart, then Vorhelm, then the Primal Firmament."
He paused for a moment.
"But the first answer was wrong, the second answer was wrong too."
"So you think the third one is wrong too?" Seris raised her eyebrows.
"Maybe, more than that...
I feel like we’re following a script."
"The first murder happened."
The result?
"Verendal was locked down."
"The second attack happened."
Vorhelm also became part of the case.
Then when it became clear that two different powers had been copied, everyone naturally went to the only thing that could make such an imitation.
The Thousand Faces Mirror.
The result?
The Twelve Guilds stood behind the Primal Firmament and the Six Great Families stood against them.
Then the Overlords were sent and now another Celestial was standing outside Verendal.
"None of these reactions were strange."
That was exactly the problem.
"Everyone did almost exactly what was expected of them."
"Which means someone calculated the reactions in advance." Seris looked at the city below for a few seconds and then said calmly,
"If my guess is right, the person behind all of this not only knows what powers the Families have or what effect each Guild has, but also knows how they will act when pressure is put on them."
This part was the worst of all.

To copy a skill, you needed to identify its structure, and to design a chain like this, you had to know the political conflicts, the pride of the Families, the interests of the Guilds, and the limits of all of them.
"Doesn’t this make it even more logical that it was the Six Great Families?" Seris looked at him.
Lian did not answer for several seconds.
The Six Great Families and the Twelve Guilds were now practically standing against each other in two different blocks.
The Overlords were outside and two Celestials were standing not far away, if someone wanted to push the world into a crisis, they had done a good job so far.
The Six Great Families were also the only ones who could design such a complicated plan, they knew each other’s personalities and knew how each of them would react.
They even had the motive, not necessarily to destroy the Twelve Guilds, but to have an excuse to suppress and weaken them.
But was it the work of all Six Great Families or only one of them?
Considering that the Six Great Families had pushed the accusations toward the Twelve Guilds, it was clear that if they were behind it, then it was a plan involving all of them.
But something was still bothering him, was weakening the Twelve Guilds really worth putting the world into such a crisis?
When the situation of the world was already not good?
"Maybe, if the goal is an excuse to suppress and weaken the Twelve Guilds, they already have it now."
"Then what’s the problem?"
"I don’t know."
This time, his answer was honest.
"I just have a feeling that this... is the result of all these chain events, not the final goal."
Seris said nothing, perhaps because she did not have an answer either, both of them only knew that something was wrong but they still did not know exactly which part.
Whatever it was, they had become fairly sure that this plan was the work of the Six Great Families, including both of their Families, they just could not understand whether it was really worth it.
Was the only thing the Six Great Families would gain the suppression and weakening of the Twelve Ancient Guilds?
Or was there another goal behind all of this?
Unfortunately for Seris, even though she was practically the next heir, she was not allowed into the major political matters, not to mention that she herself had no interest in them.
Maybe talking to her father or mother could give her the answers to her questions.
Although before she had the chance to do that...
Boom!
A deep sound passed from beneath the city and both of them almost raised their heads at the same time.
It did not seem like an explosion or an earthquake, but more like the sound of a huge machine starting up deep underground.
Lian turned back toward the city.
The golden lights that ran along the towers and main buildings lit up one after another.
First the northern section, then the west, the east, and the paths of light turned the entire city into a huge network for several seconds.
Then some lines turned off and new paths formed in their place.
Several sections that had been directly connected to the center until that moment were separated from it and formed independent rings.
Lian watched carefully.
"Is this the security separation?"
Seris nodded and her eyes moved along the Mana lines of the city.
"My mother divided the internal network."
From a security point of view, it was completely logical.
Under normal conditions, most of Verendal’s systems were connected to each other through one large network.
Now each important guest section would have separate protection.
If someone wanted to attack another section, they could no longer freely use the same paths as before.
The Young Pendragon watched the rearrangement of the network for a few more seconds, but he did not have much time to pay attention to it.
Because Seris suddenly fell to the ground.
"What—" Lian’s sentence was not completed.
And a painful scream came from the girl.
"Ahhh—aghhh!"

chapters.title: Chapter 559: The Pendragons Are in Danger
paragraphs: The Dragon Mark on Seris’s hand lit up, and in an instant, golden lines flared from the back of her hand to her wrist.
Seris raised her hand.
"This..."
At the same time, similar lights appeared from different parts of the estate.
One appeared on the hand of one of the family elders who was standing on the lower path, and another appeared on the neck of a woman from the family who was walking through a hallway.
Farther away, several other Pendragon members had also stopped.
All the Dragon Marks on all the Pendragons who had them had lit up almost at the same time.
For a moment, the sight was even beautiful, and then the light started to fade.
At first, Lian thought it was simply returning to its normal state.
But no.
The lines on Seris’s hand went even lower than their normal strength, the gold he had seen that morning was now much weaker.
But it was as if part of something flowing inside it had decreased.
Seris frowned and touched the mark with her finger, she had experienced extremely terrible pain at that moment.
She had a very high tolerance for pain, much higher than all people her age, and even so, the pain was so terrible that even she could not ignore it.
"This is not normal."
"Has this happened before?" Young Vorhelm looked at her hand.
"No."
It was not only her, in other parts of the city, several other Pendragons were also checking their hands.
One had rolled up his sleeve, and the other young people who had received their marks today were looking at their hands with worry.
What had happened to their Dragon Marks? What had suddenly happened?
And this showed that the problem was not only with the Ancestral Mark, everyone who had a Dragon Mark had experienced the same change.
Lian looked at the city’s defensive network again.
The timing of this happening was exactly the same as the change in the formations, was it possible that they were connected?
At the same time, a completely different meeting was taking place.
Isolde was not sitting in front of outside powers this time, and only the Pendragon members inside the hall were present in the smaller hall.
Several family elders, the main commanders of the internal forces, Aurelia, and several people responsible for the city’s defensive network.

"Separation is not enough. Until we understand how the attacker moved inside the protected areas and managed to carry out an attack, all movement of guests must be completely stopped." One of the elders said.
Another man disagreed.
"If we practically lock everyone inside their residences, the Guilds will use this tomorrow as an excuse and say that the Pendragons intended to control them."
"They are already saying that."
"Then we don’t need to give them evidence as well."
Another person said.
"Mental communication should also be limited, we don’t know what information they are sending outside, this can only increase the tension."
Aurelia, who had been sitting on one of the chairs to the side until then, said.
"If you cut off communication, the first thing the forces outside will do is assume that their people have been taken hostage."
"No one asked you to defend the Guilds." The family elder looked at her with a frown.
"I defended common sense." She answered very calmly.
Isolde placed her fingers against her temple, the meeting had been going around the same few issues for almost ten minutes.
In the end, she slowly let out a breath.
"That’s enough for now."
Everyone became silent, and she looked at the empty chair beside her for a moment.
Rhaenar was still outside the city.
Then, as if something had just come to her mind, she asked.
"By the way... where is my daughter?"
Several people looked at each other, and one of the family elders answered.
"With that Vorhelm."
The Matriarch did not react for two seconds, and then she laughed.
"She locked herself away for a month, then comes out and instead of coming to see her mother first, she goes looking for a Vorhelm?"
"New priorities." Aurelia started laughing from the other side of the room.
However, several family elders did not see anything funny about the matter, and one of them said.
"This is not a laughing matter, My Lady."
"No?" Isolde still had a very small smile on her face.
"The Vorhelms are not our friends."
The woman’s smile became weaker, this part was true, the Pendragons and Vorhelms were not in an official war, but "friends"? They were not even close to that.

Over the past few generations, the two families had faced each other many times over resources, contracts, influence in the Federation, areas in the Heavenly Realm, and their position among the Six Great Families.

Sometimes they also worked together and made deals, but their rivalry was so old that many elders from both sides practically saw the other side as an enemy who simply had no reason to fight them yet.
One of the elders continued.
"And especially now, when the Vorhelms themselves are in the middle of a succession crisis."
"And a few hours ago, their family’s style was seen in the second attack, it is true that they were not responsible for it, but that does not mean we should ignore this." Another person said.
"Ignore what? Were we attacked with that style?" Aurelia sighed.
The man frowned.
"The matter is not only about that attack."
"I know, the matter is that you don’t like Seris liking someone you didn’t choose for her." She said sarcastically.
A short silence appeared.
"Seris was supposed to focus on the family and her own path." The family elder said.
"She is."
"Then why does she spend time with that boy every chance she gets?"
"Because she wants to." Aurelia smiled.
That answer made the man even more unhappy.
"Is this matter really that simple to you?"
"Yes, I don’t see any complexity in it, or have you become so old that you can’t understand even such simple things?"
Another elder joined the discussion.
"You know better than anyone how the Vorhelms work, every relationship with them is destructive! They will use even relationships for their own benefit!"
This time, Aurelia did not even lose her smile.
"And we don’t?
The room became silent for a moment, and they had no answer to give.
"Do you really want to have this argument with me? In a family that has used the marriages of its heirs to build political alliances for generations?"
No one had a quick answer, and she continued.
"At least that boy has not used the Vorhelm name even once to get close to Seris so far, and as far as I know, he has not used that family name to get anything in his life."
"You defend him too much." One of the elders said with dissatisfaction.
Aurelia casually shrugged.
"Because at least he is better than most of the suitors you choose for the daughters of this family."
"Aurelia." Isolde placed her hand on her forehead this time.
"What? Am I wrong?"
"No, but this meeting is not for choosing a son-in-law."
Aurelia leaned back with satisfaction.
The elder who had been arguing a few moments earlier muttered something under his breath that was probably better left unheard.
The Matriarch slowly let out a breath.
"Enough, Seris’s relationship with whoever she chooses is not the matter we are dealing with today."
At that moment, the hall door opened and everyone turned their eyes toward it.
Lucien Pendragon entered, one of the five strongest members of the current generation and the same person who had received the Sovereign Mark that morning.
Lysandra, Kaelen, and the other members of the younger generation usually behaved carefully in the presence of the elders.
Lucien even more so.
But this time, his formal bow was shorter than usual, and his face did not have its usual calmness.
"What happened?" Isolde became serious immediately.
Lucien said nothing and raised his right hand, the Dragon Mark on the back of his hand was still there.
But its light had become weak, much more than it should have been after the natural end of the ceremony.
One of the elders stood up from his seat.
"What is this?"
"We don’t know." Lucien did not take his eyes off the mark.
"But it is not only mine, everyone we have checked so far has the same condition."
Isolde’s expression finally changed.
The murder of a guest was a political crisis.
The accusation against the Primal Firmament was a global crisis.
But the Dragon Marks? This was no longer about other people, it was directly related to the Pendragons.
They had not noticed this because none of them had Dragon Marks anymore, the mark only existed until reaching the third evolution, and after that, it was used to create a [Dragon Body].
"When did this start?" The Matriarch stood up from her seat.
"Almost at the same time as the changes made to the city’s defensive mechanism."
The room became even quieter, all the discussion about Lian and Seris was completely forgotten at that moment.
The Matriarch’s face became more and more serious, and before she could even think about what was happening, her husband, Rhaenar, contacted her through mental communication.
And he said only one sentence, one sentence that, if it became reality, could turn into the greatest disaster in the history of the Pendragons.
And that was enough to leave the Matriarch frozen in shock and a deep sense of fear rising in her heart.
"They want to release the Dragon."

chapters.title: Chapter 560: The Biggest Secret of the Pendragons
paragraphs: The pain in Seris’s hand was gone, or at least, she acted as if it was.

She was standing on her feet again and had the same cold expression she always had on her face, but from such a close distance, Lian could see that the fingers of her right hand unconsciously curled and opened again every few seconds.
It was a small movement.
For someone who did not know Seris, it was almost impossible to notice.
He kept his eyes on the Ancestral Dragon Mark.
The golden dragon could still be seen on the back of her hand, but the light that had been flowing through its lines that morning had become weaker.
Seris was also looking at the same place.
"It happened at the same time as the change in the formations."
"It seems it wasn’t only yours." Lian slightly raised his head and looked down.
Down on the terrace, several other Pendragon members were still checking their own marks.
One of the younger members had rolled his sleeve up above his elbow and was talking to an older man.
A little farther away, a woman with a Dragon Mark on her neck had also stopped moving.
The same thing had happened to all of them at the same moment.
The young Pendragon ran her thumb over the faded lines of the mark.
"So the marks are not independent."
All the holders of the marks were in different parts of Verendal.

Some had received their marks only today, while some had probably received them years ago, if all of them had reacted at exactly the same moment, then there had to be a shared connection somewhere deep inside their structure.
"And the changes in the formations touched that root, but how? How can these two be connected?" Lian looked at the city again.
According to what both of them knew, the Dragon Mark was a type of blessing given by an ancient treasure that belonged to a Demon.
And the city’s formations were part of the city’s defensive mechanism, so how could changing the city’s defensive mechanism affect the marks?
The result was clear, these two had a connection that they did not know about, or that had been hidden from them...

"The first murder locked down the city, the second attack brought the families into it, the accusation against the Primal Firmament pulled the Guilds into it, the Overlords took my father outside the city." Seris slowly whispered.
Then her eyes moved toward the city.
"And the conflicts made my mother change the network."
Silence fell between them, when all those events were seen separately, each one had a natural reason.
A murder justified locking down the city, the accusation against Vorhelm justified investigating the family.
Finding the Thousand-Faced Mirror led to suspicion against the Primal Firmament.
Calling in backup forces was also not strange in the current atmosphere of distrust, but when you placed them one after another, they started to look like a path.
And somehow, what had just happened to the marks was connected to them.
But how?
Could it be... that the target was to rewrite the city’s defensive mechanism?
"If someone wanted the defensive formations to be changed from the beginning..." Lian said quietly, but did not finish his sentence.
Seris said nothing either, because she had already understood the rest of his thought.

If the final goal was to change Verendal’s defensive network, then all the events before this could have simply been a way to force the Pendragons to do something that no outside enemy could directly force them to do.
The Pendragons had to rearrange the network with their own hands.
Both of their eyes widened for a moment, did that mean that all this time... all the events that had happened were only a preparation for changing the defensive mechanism of this city?
But why? Why would a plan have to go this far? What benefit could it give them?
A voice came from behind them.
"There is no need to guess any further.
Both of them turned around.
Isolde Pendragon was standing at the beginning of the stone path of the terrace.
Two high-ranking guards stood several meters behind her, but even they did not come any closer.

The woman’s face was different from when she had been sitting on the ceremony platform a few hours ago, she was not afraid, but the somewhat relaxed calmness and short smiles she had before were gone.
She walked directly toward Seris.
"Show me your hand."
Seris held out her right hand without asking any questions.
Isolde grabbed her daughter’s wrist and closely examined the faded mark, her finger moved once over one of the golden lines, and for a moment, her expression became more serious.
"Did it hurt?"
"It passed."
She raised her head and looked directly into her daughter’s eyes for several seconds.
"That was not an answer to my question."
"A lot." Seris paused briefly.
Those two words were enough.
Isolde’s hand remained on her daughter’s wrist for a moment, the pressure of her fingers changed very slightly, so slightly that she might not have even noticed it herself.
Then she let go.
"Are you okay?"
"Yes."
The Matriarch did not insist any further and moved her eyes to Lian.
"Both of you come with me." And without saying anything else, she turned around and left.

Pendragon forces were present at almost every intersection in the city, some doors that had previously been open were now sealed with several layers, and in two hallways on the western side, even restraint formations were active.
But the people being taken under protection attracted even more attention.
Several members of the Primal Firmament seemed to have been arrested...?
Six Pendragon forces were moving around them, and Mana restraint rings could be seen on the wrists of two of them.
Seris only gave her mother a look.
"Before I came to get you, I ordered the arrest of all members of the Primal Firmament delegation." Isolde said without stopping.
Lian raised an eyebrow.
This was no longer normal caution.
A Celestial belonging to the same Guild was currently outside Verendal, standing against Rhaenar, and Isolde had arrested his delegation inside the city.
If the news reached Kairos, which it certainly would, the situation outside would not become calmer.
"Are you that certain?"
"No."
Her answer came immediately.
"But the risk of waiting is greater."
They walked a few more meters.
"The Thousand-Faced Mirror is the only known artifact that can recreate an attack’s signature and structure with the level of accuracy we saw today.
Young Vorhelm said nothing, she already knew this part.

"The first person who requested a complete separation of the security routes after the twenty-four-hour agreement was the representative of the Primal Firmament, and that caused us to rewrite the city’s defensive mechanism."
This point caused his expression to change slightly.
It really was true.
The others had made their requests after that.

If that request had not been made, perhaps the city’s defensive mechanism would never have been changed, and as a result, what happened to Seris and the other Dragon Mark holders would never have happened.
But what exactly had happened to the holders of the Dragon Marks? What had happened that even the Pendragon Matriarch seemed worried?
Isolde said.
"A few minutes after the network was rearranged, all the Dragon Marks reacted."
"The others sent Overlords, but the Primal Firmament sent a Celestial."
Lian did not answer.
The result of that decision was right in front of everyone.
Kairos had arrived, and Rhaenar had personally been forced to leave the center of Verendal, right before the defensive mechanism was changed.
Isolde gave him a brief look.
"Kairos did not need to come."
Her voice became colder.
"If it was only about protecting the delegation, an Overlord would have been enough."
"His presence made it impossible for Father to leave that place." Seris said shortly.
"Exactly."
All the pieces were pointing toward the Primal Firmament again, even more than before and with greater certainty.
Isolde placed her hand against the wall beside them, there was no door there, but when she touched it, very faint golden lines lit up under the stone, and part of the wall slowly moved backward.
"If they are innocent, they will be released later, if they are not, I don’t want them walking freely around my city until then."
Behind the wall was a short hallway that ended at a completely dark room.

The feeling of the environment immediately changed.
Lian almost completely lost his connection with the outside, as if this part of the city was completely isolated.
Isolde touched one of the seals on the wall, and very faint golden lines lit up, giving the room just enough light for their faces to be seen.
Then the woman looked directly at Lian.
"From this moment on, everything you hear stays here."
"Even from the Vorhelms?" Lian held her gaze for several seconds.
"Especially from the Vorhelms." Her tone was not joking.
He tilted his head slightly, this level of secrecy was not normal for an ordinary security crisis.
Beside him, Seris also remained silent.
"Do you know the Demon of End?" The Matriarch walked a few steps forward and asked.
"The dragon that the founders of the Pendragons killed, right?" Lian answered almost immediately.
For a moment, no one spoke, Isolde seemed unsure how to say the next words...
In the end, she sighed and added.
"They didn’t kill it, that dragon is still alive."

chapters.title: Chapter 561: The Pendragons Lied
paragraphs: Lian kept his eyes fixed on the woman’s face, for a moment, he felt like he had heard completely wrong.
"They never managed to." Isolde slowly let out a breath.
"The Demon of End is still alive and imprisoned beneath Verendal."
The room remained silent.
Young Vorhelm had not expected such an answer, not because she was surprised that there was a great secret within the Pendragon Family.
Great families probably would not remain great families without great secrets.
But this? This was not just a family secret.
One of the most famous recorded battles between humanity and Demon Rank beings was based on the claim that the Demon of End had been killed.

The Pendragons had been known for that victory for centuries, today’s ceremony had also been built around that legend, the entire myth, reputation, honor, and greatness of this family came from that story.
And now it turned out that there had never been a body, because the thing that should have been a corpse was still alive.
Was this some kind of fucking joke? Had the great Pendragon Family lied to the entire world for more than dozens of years?
Lian gave Seris a look, her face had almost no change.
But her right hand was beside her body, and her thumb was slowly pressing against the edge of her index finger.
It was a simple movement, but it had a clear meaning, the girl was upset, much more than she was showing.
"Do the elders of the family know?"
"Some of them, but not all."
"Aurelia?"
"No, the total number of people who know about this fact is less than twenty."
"When were you going to tell me?" Seris’s finger pressed slightly harder.
Isolde looked at her, this time, her answer came a little later.
"After the ceremony."
"So today."
"Yes."
The young Pendragon did not ask anything else, she did not raise her voice or accuse her mother, but Lian felt that this silence was heavier than an argument.
She had grown up with a great story that was considered part of her family’s identity.
Now, within a few sentences, she had learned that her parents had known another truth all this time.
And they had hidden it not only from the world, but from her as well.
The reason the Pendragon Family was famous was nothing but a lie.
He turned his eyes back to the Matriarch, so the Pendragons had lied to the entire world for centuries.
It was understandable.
If news of a living Demon Rank being under Verendal became public, how many enemies would try to release that dragon over the course of several centuries?
Probably not a small number.
So hiding the truth was logical, but the fact that a lie was logical did not make it any smaller.
Isolde did not let the silence continue for too long.
"The Dragon Mark is not just something that increases the power of the younger generation."
Seris fixed her eyes on her mother again.
"All active marks are connected to the main structure of the seal."
Lian looked at the faded mark on Seris’s hand, now what had happened a few minutes ago had a different meaning.
"When they all activated at the same time and then their energy dropped, it means something entered the prison network."
"Something?" he asked.
"We still don’t know what it is."
She gave one of the seals in the room a brief look.
"Rhaenar sensed the change in the flow from outside, an unknown structure is weakening the seal from inside, its clear goal is to release it."

This time, there was no doubt left, all the events of today, from the murder to the framing, the accusations, the Overlords, the Celestial, and the change in the formations, were probably connected to a being that the world did not even know was still alive.
Isolde added.
"It has not been released yet, if it had been, this meeting would not be our problem right now." But then her voice became slightly lower.
"But we don’t know how much time we have."
"Why are you telling us all this?" Lian asked a much more important question, and his eyes moved to Seris for a moment.
"I understand that, but why me?"
The woman remained silent for a few seconds, there was something in her expression that told Lian that she did not like the answer very much either.
"You have to enter the prison and stop whatever is trying to release that Demon, only holders of the Dragon Mark can enter that prison."

"The Dragon Mark acts like a key to the prison and at the same time provides energy to the seal, that is why the holder of this mark can be considered the key to the prison of that monster, the fact that the marks are fading means that someone is weakening the seal." Then she looked at Lian.
"And as for you, Rhaenar said you also have to go, more precisely, you may be the only person who can go with her."
"That’s it?"
"That’s it."
So Rhaenar had seen or understood something that made him insist on Lian being there.

Isolde either did not know what it was, or had no interest in explaining it, and that meant the Patriarch had seen something inside him that made him certain that Lian also had the ability to enter the prison of that Demon.
Either way, now was not the time to pressure her, they had a much, much bigger problem now.
"So the Dragon Mark was also a lie?" Seris whispered.

"Yes and no, the Dragon Mark is an artifact that belongs to that Demon, to imprison that Demon, a sealing formation was created and that artifact is also part of it, the formation needs energy to keep working and the holders of the Dragon Marks provide that energy." Isolde paused slightly and then completed her explanation.

"So someone killed a person, framed two families, turned the Six Great Families and the Twelve Guilds against each other, brought Overlords here, and even brought a Celestial into the game... all of this to release a dragon?" he whispered.
Isolde looked directly at him.
"Not a dragon, but the Demon of End."
Those two words alone were enough to remind him of the weight of the difference.
A being at the Demon Rank.
The same rank that only a limited number of beings had been recorded at throughout human history, and each one of them could turn a continent into a disaster.
If something like that were released in the heart of Europe, the problem would not only be the destruction of Verendal, all the powers of the world would be forced to react.
And exactly at a time when trust between the greatest powers had reached its lowest point and they were unlikely to show any interest in cooperating.
"Who could even come up with such a plan?" Lian asked, the plan was truly flawless and impressive.
No matter how he looked at it, this plan had been designed to cause as much damage as possible to humanity and the entire world.

If a human or a power in their world did something like this, it would be nothing but extreme stupidity and pure wickedness, because they could practically push their world into another era of the apocalypse.
"I still think it was the Primal Firmament." Isolde answered calmly.

Lian’s expression changed slightly, he could not believe that something like this could be the work of humans, this was not only a blow against the Great Families, it could cause the fall of another continent.
"Still?"
"More than before."
She walked toward one of the walls.

"They have the imitation tool and they were the ones who suggested rewriting the defensive network, rewriting the defensive network caused whatever is now trying to release the dragon to enter the prison."
Then she turned around.
"And they were the only ones who brought a Celestial."
The last point was more important, all the other powers had settled for an Overlord.
The Primal Firmament was the only one that had raised the crisis one level higher, Kairos did not need to come personally.
If the goal was only to protect the Guild representatives, an Overlord would have been enough to show their seriousness.
But Kairos had come, the result? Rhaenar had left the heart of the city.
Isolde said calmly.
"If someone wanted Rhaenar to be away from the center of Verendal at exactly this time, they could not have chosen a better method."
Lian could not disagree, this one was really bad, and when you placed it beside the request to separate the security areas, the Primal Firmament once again looked too perfectly placed.
"That is why I ordered the complete arrest of the delegation before coming here."
"What about Celestial Kairos?" Seris asked shortly.
"He is outside and has not done anything yet."
But all the people from the Primal Firmament inside Verendal were now under the control of the Pendragons.
Lian still had the same feeling as before, there was a lot of evidence, far too much, but perhaps Isolde was right.
Perhaps the fact that they were so obvious was itself part of the plan.
If the Primal Firmament had intentionally brought itself to the edge of being accused, the Twelve Guilds would stand behind it.
And Kairos would have a perfect reason to be there, in that case, even something that looked like a mistake could have been planned.
The Matriarch placed her hand on one of the seals and another door opened at the end of the room.
"We don’t have time."
The path ahead was dark.
"The Demon is still sealed, you are looking for whatever is touching the seal and trying to release that dragon."
"I understand." Seris said.
"What if whatever is down there is stronger than us?"
"You come back."
Seris had only one question.
"What if we can’t?"
"You can, you have to be able to, and in the worst case, your father will step in."
