Their beauty was strange.
Even within the vast Prison of the Demon of End, Lian’s new wings had an appearance that was difficult to ignore.
When he spread them, the air around him was pushed backward.
The shadow of the wings covered a large part of the broken platform.
For a moment, he felt as if two new limbs had been added to his body.
He could move even the smallest parts of them, change the angle of each wing, and even feel the air pressure building beneath them.
Seris glanced at him, and it was not difficult for her to understand that he had obtained them as the Blessing of an Ancestral Dragon Mark.
But before she could ask for more details, the roar of the Demon of End shook the prison once again.
The dragon’s massive claw came down toward them.
Lian did not even have time to test all the abilities of his new wings, and could only think about moving.
The two black wings spread open.
Whoosh!
His body shot up from the platform at a terrifying speed, and for a moment, the distance between him and the Demon of End almost disappeared.
However, this speed was different from Reinar’s spatial movement.
Lian had actually moved, while that man bent space-time according to his own will.
Air pressure struck his armor, and the stones beneath the place where he had taken off shifted due to the wave of force created by his wings opening.
In the middle of his movement, he folded one of his wings.
His direction changed.
The Demon of End’s claw passed through the place where he had been a moment ago.
BOOOOOOM!
Part of the platform shattered.
Lian turned his body in the air and headed back toward Seris, but this time, instead of landing, he remained suspended several meters above the platform.
True flight, with a speed that, if he released the full power of the Blessing, would be dozens of times greater than even his maximum running speed.
Of course, he could also feel the mana consumption.
The faster he moved, the more energy left his body.
So, for now, he did not use his full capacity, saving it for a time when he truly needed it.
She looked up at him from below, and her gaze remained on his black wings for a moment.
Lian gave a faint smile.
"What do you think?"
"They’re good and... beautiful." Seris answered after a short pause.
He laughed.
"That was a huge compliment."
But the girl was no longer looking at him, she had raised her sword, and behind her, something began to take shape in the darkness.
First, two golden eyes opened, and then a deep roar echoed through the prison.
A massive amount of mana gathered behind her and slowly took shape.
A magnificent dragon’s head with long golden horns, a neck covered in silver-white scales, and two massive wings with lines of cold light flowing between them.
When the manifestation was complete, a dragon stood behind Seris.
Its body was semi-material, but the pressure of its presence was so real that even the air around the girl changed.
The moonlight that had previously formed behind her was now moving around the manifestation.
Two different powers, yet strangely in sync.

Lian looked at the scene for a moment, if he was not mistaken, this dragon manifestation should be the Blessing Seris had obtained from her Ancestral Dragon Mark, now he just needed to see what its abilities were.
The Demon of End noticed it as well, and its massive eyes remained fixed on the manifestation for a moment.
"This...
Its voice grew heavier.
"You damn Pendragons, you’re using my Dragon Pearl in such a stupid way?"
Then it raised its partially freed arm again.
Lian saw the direction of its movement.
"Seris, now!"

She could create a dragon phantom and combine it with her attack, and the result was an increase of up to 3333% in her attack power.
Silver mana gathered along the blade.
The moon phantom grew brighter, and the dragon behind Seris opened its mouth.
For a moment, the sounds of two roars merged.
She swung her sword downward.
At the same time, the dragon phantom followed the same path, and the power of the sword strike and the force of the manifestation merged at a single point.
CRRRRAAAAAASH!

The sound of the impact echoed throughout the prison, and several old scales that already had cracks in them shattered.
The dragon’s massive claw stopped in the middle of its movement.

Even Lian was surprised by the result for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 574: The Second Core ( Castle Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian descended through the spatial rifts.
"That’s enough!"
His voice was harsher than usual this time.
"Both of you, return!"
One put up almost no resistance, because it couldn’t, its strength had reached its limit.
Two also still intended to stand despite its severe injuries, but the Colony Link responded to Lian’s command.
Both creatures disappeared amid the flow of mana and returned to the Colony House.
He checked their conditions through the link.
They were alive, but their injuries were severe.
One was almost unable to move, and Two had lost a large part of its combat strength.
Returning to the Colony House only removed them from the battlefield and improved their recovery conditions.
It did not heal their wounds immediately.
He took a deep breath, anger rose inside him for a moment, but he did not let it change his decision.
The Demon of End was still in front of him, and if he lost control now, One and Two’s sacrifices would mean nothing.
The dragon moved its arm again.
Lian raised his gaze, Seris was still busy maintaining the seal.

The golden flow of the sacrificed Dragon Marks, which had only just been stabilized through the anchor and the new source, had almost reached the final stage, but several main connections still needed to be stabilized.
And the dragon intended to strike before they were complete.
He spread his black wings, this time, he had no intention of simply escaping.
In his perception, the paths of air and mana took shape around his two wings.
It was time to see what creating a storm with the help of these wings would look like.
Black lines emerged from the edges of his wings, and the air around his body began to spin.
At first, a small tornado formed behind him.
Then it grew larger.
The spinning currents overlapped, and a massive pillar of black wind rose into the air.
The young Vorhelm spread both wings to their full extent.
The energy needed to activate the ability gathered within them, and seventy percent of his remaining mana was transferred in that instant.
Heavy pressure spread through his body, but Lian gritted his teeth.
Now.
His wings moved forward with all their strength.
VVOOOOOOOOOM!
The black tornado rushed toward the Demon of End, lifting the broken stones around the platform off the ground.
The sea of red mist parted for a moment along the tornado’s path, and the massive spinning mass of energy collided with one of the rifts of End the dragon had created.
For several moments, the black wind and the spatial rift pushed against each other.
Then the outer part of the tornado split apart, but its dense center continued forward.

Lian focused all his power on changing the attack’s direction, not on directly fighting against the Essence of End, the tornado struck the rift and shifted it a few degrees away from its original path.
Those few degrees were enough.
Instead of hitting the Root of the seal, the Demon of End’s attack passed beside it and struck an empty, damaged part of the prison.
Space turned black for a moment, and then a massive wave of pressure was released in the distance.
Lian remained in the air, breathing heavily, his mana had dropped sharply.
His black wings were still there, but even maintaining his flight now placed greater pressure on his body.
However, Seris had succeeded, the final golden path of the seal lit up.
Her Ancestral Mark shone brightly, and all the energy gathered from the sacrificed Dragon Marks moved along the prison’s chains.
Hundreds of massive rings lit up one after another, and the ancient broken pillars connected to the main structure through golden strands.
The chains that the Demon of End had loosened during the battle were pulled tight again.
But just before the seal could close completely, Lian sensed something else.
A part of the Essence of End had become trapped in the central path, energy that had been separated from the dragon’s body during its attacks and was now caught among the flows of the seal.
If it remained there, the prison’s final command could not be completed properly.
Seris looked at Lian, she had also noticed the problem.
He took a short breath, his remaining mana was now very low.
But if he did not destroy that Essence of End, the seal structure could not start working, but that thing was the Essence of End, the essence of a Demon.
The last time he had touched a Demon’s essence, he had obtained his first Core, and now another essence was right in front of him.
He thought for a moment, this was an opportunity he did not want to miss.
However, before moving toward the remaining Essence of End, he glanced at the Elf, she was secretly doing something and thought she could hide it from him.

He smirked and released a small amount of Eclipse energy to stop the Elf’s trick, then, while moving toward the Essence o End at full speed, he picked something up along the way without anyone noticing.
Then bringing his right hand forward as essence flowed along his fingers.
And then he made contact with the Essence of End,
At first, nothing happened, then, for a moment, his mind became separated from all the sounds of the prison.
The space around him changed, everything, even Seris, disappeared, and another scene formed in front of him.
It was not difficult to understand that, just like when he had come into contact with the Essence of Eclipse, he was now seeing the memories of the Demon of End.
A massive battlefield beneath a red sky, and a dragon displaying its full, true glory.
The Demon of End.
But this time, it was not imprisoned, its massive wings covered a large part of the sky, there were no chains around its body, and the golden spike had not yet pierced its chest.
Tens of thousands of warriors stood before it, wearing golden and black armor and carrying flags bearing the Pendragon Family’s symbol.
Among the images, he saw warriors whose presence was even greater than that of many high-ranked Awakened he had seen so far.
But they also fell one after another before the Demon of End.
The dragon’s massive claw moved, and a part of the battlefield split down the middle, hundreds of people disappeared in that instant..
All of them vanished into rifts that passed through the ground and space.
Lian saw another moment.
Several Pendragon warriors attacked the dragon with all their strength.
One of them was guiding a massive golden spike toward the Demon’s chest with the help of the others.
Thousands of people died to open a path, sacrificing themselves one after another until the spike finally struck the Demon’s body.
A massive roar shook the sky, and the first golden chain wrapped around the dragon’s neck.
But this memory did not last long, and the scene changed.
This time, Lian was standing in an unknown place, with several massive beings in front of him, none of them looked much like one another.
Some had bodies similar to monsters, while others looked almost human, but their presence was so heavy that even watching this memory created a strange feeling inside him.
He felt like the lowest form of life in the presence of these beings, and each of them had a presence at least equal to, or even stronger than, that of the Demon of End.
It was not difficult to understand that these were Demons.
But before he could clearly recognize their faces or number, the scene changed again.
This time, he was no longer even sure where he was.
A vast space where stars and galaxies floated like bright dots in the distance.
There were no visible boundaries, no ground, and no sky either, only endless space, where light itself moved in strange ways in some places.
On one side of the battlefield, there were beings made of light.
Lian could not clearly see their true forms.
Some were hidden behind auras of light, while others seemed so large that it was impossible to tell how far away they were.
But one thing was clear.
Their presence seemed divine, something like the sacred presence of gods.
On the other side, there were seven massive shadows.
But their forms were unlike anything that could be compared to any other known living creature.
One of them had a body filled with thousands of moving points of light, and the strange thing was that each of those points seemed to be a planet or a star.

Another had massive wings that seemed larger than the entire world, and they looked as if they were made of galaxies, as though every movement of its wings could cause planets and galaxies to collapse.
Another being moved its head, and the reality around it changed direction for a moment, as if all of space-time and the layers of reality were about to collapse under its presence.
The remaining four beings could also be seen among the darkness and broken lights, each of them seemed like a godlike being beyond description.
Lian tried to obtain more information, but there was nothing, the image was too unclear, however, he could make a few guesses.
Those beings made of sacred ... Gods?
Another thought immediately came to his mind, and what about those seven beings? In the known hierarchy of monsters, there was a rank above Demons.
Supreme.
Was it possible that those seven beings were monsters of the same rank?
If that was the case, their level of power was different from anything he had ever seen.
But before he could reach any further conclusions, the images shattered.
Lian heard the sound of the prison chains again, only a moment of real time had passed, and his right hand was still connected to the seal’s main path.
But the Essence of End had now entered his body.
The space where his Cores were located began to tremble, and another space became active beside the Eclipse Core.
The Essence of End gathered at that point, but every time it tried to form a stable structure, it cut off part of its own flow.
It was as if it was unwilling to remain inside any container, as though anything that tried to contain it would be brought to an "end".
Lian felt intense pressure inside his body.
The Ruined Heart beat for a moment.
Thump!
And that alone was enough to stop the aggression and wildness of the Essence of End inside his body, making it calm and quiet, like a well-behaved child.
It immediately gathered at a single point and formed a new structure.
[ New Core Formed ]
[ Name: End Core ]
[ Origin: Demon of End ]
[ Status: Incomplete ]
Special Energy: End Essence.
[ Current Number of Cores: 2 ]

chapters.title: Chapter 575: The Dragon Falls Asleep Again ( Castle Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian looked at the message for a moment.
He now had two cores, the Eclipse Core and the End Core.
However, contrary to what the message might suggest, he had not suddenly gained all the power of the Demon of End.
The new core was still incomplete, its stored energy was very limited, and using it also required precise control.
Even in this early state, it was an unusual power.
He was still examining the changes in his body when a terrifying voice came from a distance.
"No!"
The Demon of End had raised its head again, its enormous eyes fixed on Lian.
But this time, something in its gaze was even worse than before.
"No... no!"
The enormous chains were pulled tight under pressure.
"You should not exist!"
The young Vorhelm raised his head.
When the Demon of End saw the formation of the second core, it seemed to lose the last bit of control it had.
"Die!"
Its partially freed arm moved, and a black rift appeared in the space in front of it.
But before it could reach him, the newly strengthened chains tightened.
The arm was pulled back several meters, and the Demon let out a furious roar.
"You must die!"
Seris placed her hand on the main path of the seal, the Ancestral Mark shone, and the last remaining part of the seal was activated.
The energy of all the sacrificed Marks, which had been stored inside the prison’s structure, began to flow through the main paths.
The enormous pillars lit up one after another.
The black and golden chains tightened around the Demon’s neck, wings, and arms, and the central golden spike in the dragon’s chest shone with intense light.
The Demon of End tried to resist.
But this time, unlike at the beginning of the battle, almost all the main paths of the seal had been reactivated.
Its freed arm gradually moved back, its neck was pulled down, and its enormous wing became motionless again under the pressure of the chains.
"Anomaly!"
The Demon’s voice echoed throughout the prison.
"An anomaly should not exist!"
Lian looked at it with a serious expression, the Ruined Heart inside his body was now silent, but the Demon was still staring at the same spot.
"Die! You must die!"
The dragon’s final roar mixed with the sound of the chains tightening, then the golden rings around its head closed.
The red light in its eyes grew weaker, its enormous eyelids slowly lowered, and finally, the Demon of End fell asleep again.
For several moments, no one spoke, and the sound of Lian’s heavy breathing could be heard inside the prison.
The World-Devourer Bastion armor was still on his body, but many of its plates were cracked, and parts of the armor on his arms and shoulders were badly damaged.
His black wings were also still behind him, although his low mana meant that he could no longer freely use their full power as before.
Seris stood several meters away, her right hand was trembling.
Both of them looked at the enormous dragon that had settled quietly among the chains again.
They had survived, and more importantly, they had succeeded.
Just then, a system message appeared.
[Emergency Quest Completed]
[The release of the Demon of End has been stopped]
[Rewards have been granted]
[Level increased by 2]
[200 Fragments]
[200 Stat Points]
Another window appeared in front of Lian.
[Total Current stats: 20,000 / 20,000 ]
[Bonus Stat Points cannot be allocated]
[200 bonus Stat Points have been converted into 200 additional Fragments]
[Total Fragments Received: 400]
[Current Level: 29]
He kept his eyes on the message, four hundred Fragments and two levels, and besides that, he had also obtained an Ancestral Mark and a new monster core.
These were enormous rewards.
But when he looked at his wounded body and the empty spaces where One and Two had been, he knew very well what price he had paid for them.
He had not even had time to think about this when another message appeared.
[New Title Obtained]
[Survivor of the End]
[Requirement: Survive a direct encounter with a creature in the Demon rank and participate in restraining it again]
[Title Effects]
[When fighting Demon-rank creatures, all stats increase by 50%, damage received is reduced by up to 5%, and the chance of landing a critical hit with each successful attack is 5%]
Lian raised his eyebrows.
This title was truly powerful.
Especially the 50% increase to all stats when facing a Demon.
Of course, its effect was temporary and depended on fighting creatures of the same rank, and it did not change the permanent limit of the First Evolution.
But it was still a very valuable reward.
At the same moment, Seris was also looking at the windows in front of her, apparently, she had received the same title.
He gave a very faint smile.
"I think it was worth it."
She looked at him and then glanced at the Ancestral Mark on her own hand.
"Maybe."
Her short answer made Lian realize that she was still thinking about the lost Marks of her family.
But there was another matter that remained.
He turned his gaze back toward the heart of the prison, the Silver Elf was still there.
Her image had become a little unstable, and the golden rings around her were no longer polluted by silver light as they had been before.
But she could still speak.
Seris raised her sword, and Lian also used [True Trail] to examine the connection path of the image.
For several moments, they tried to surround the Elf’s connection from several directions.
He summoned [Eternal Grave Maw] around the central part of the image to restrain any remaining mana structures.
But the result was not very promising.
What stood before them was not her real body.
Even if they destroyed the entire clone structure, they would only cut off the connection.
The Silver Elf herself would still be alive, the silver creature noticed their attempt and looked at them for a moment.
Then she laughed.
"Do you really think you’ve won?"
"Your plan has fallen apart, so what are you laughing at?" Lian raised his head.
The Elf tilted her head slightly, her mirror-like eyes shone in the prison’s golden light.
"You humans are truly stupid."
This time, her voice was full of mockery.
"I only gave your greatest powers a few things to worry about. You did the rest yourselves."
The young Vorhelm remained silent.
"The families have started suspecting each other, and the Twelve Guilds have stood against you. The Overlords have gathered, and even your Celestials are making threats against each other."
She spread her arms.
"Do you think I lost just because this dragon wasn’t released?"
Another laugh came from her throat.
"Only one part of the plan failed! Your world is already on the edge of war, and even if I disappear here, the distrust won’t disappear with me."
She paused for a moment and then added with satisfaction.
"I still won."
Lian looked at her for several seconds, in a way, she was right, the Demon of End had been imprisoned again.
But the political crisis outside the prison still remained.
Severin had been arrested, Kairos was standing against Rhaenar, and the Six Great Families and the Twelve Guilds probably still blamed each other.
If this situation continued, the world could enter a massive crisis even without the Demon of End being released.
But there was still one thing the Elf did not know.
He raised the corner of his mouth.
"Don’t be so sure."
"What?" The Elf looked at him.
Lian raised his right hand, a silver seed with a cracked surface, but it still seemed intact.
The Silver Corruption Seed.
For a moment, the Elf did not react at all, then all her attention became fixed on the seed.
"That..."
Lian held the seed between two fingers.
"Are you looking for this?"
The Elf took a step forward, her eyes trembled violently for a moment.
"How?!"
"I think you left something behind."
"Impossible! I made sure it was destroyed!"
"The shell, yes, it was cracked, but what about the rest?" Lian laughed.
A few minutes earlier, just when the Silver Elf had realized that the operation to release the Demon of End was failing, she had activated the seed’s self-destruction command.
Lian had seen that
But instead of destroying the seed itself, he had sent only an extremely thin strand of Eclipse energy into the self-destruction command’s path.
The connection between the outer shell and the main center of the seed had been weakened.
The shell had cracked according to the Elf’s command and released silver light, which from a distance looked exactly like the seed’s complete destruction.
But the inside of the seed, including its central part, had remained intact.
And just when the Elf’s attention had been focused on the seal and the Demon of End, Lian had picked it up while he was going to deal with the Essence of End.
And now, the main evidence of the entire conspiracy was in his hands.
The Silver Elf stared at the seed in disbelief, she did not even speak for several seconds.
Then anger replaced her shock.
"Damn human!"
Her clone trembled.
"You... you ruined our plans!"

chapters.title: Chapter 576: Seriously? Another Fight?
paragraphs: Lian shrugged slightly.
"It seems so."
"You think this is over?!"
The Elf’s voice grew louder.
"We will return! You can be sure that we will take revenge! You won’t get away with this without paying a price! My mother will definitely punish you for ruining our plan!"
"Human, you will die a horrible death! You will beg for death, and then I will look at your face and laugh."
"We spent fifteen years planning this! You damn human! How dare you ruin our grand plan!"
He no longer paid attention to her threats.
Beside him, Seris glanced at the seed and then at Lian’s face.
For a moment, something like admiration appeared in her eyes, she knew Lian was smart, and she knew that in battle, he could see several moves ahead.

But the fact that he had even thought about securing evidence to prevent a war between the world’s powers while fighting a living Demon, when they could lose their lives at any moment, was unexpected even to her.
The corner of her lips lifted slightly.
The young Vorhelm noticed.
"What?"
Seris shook her head.
"Nothing."
Lian gave her a brief glance, but before he could ask anything, the Elf’s shouting started again.
"I’m talking to you, ugly human!"
He let out a short sigh.
"Ugly?"
Then he turned his attention to the new core that had formed inside his body.
The End Core.
The amount of energy stored inside it was very low, but it might be enough for what he intended to do.
He reached out with his right hand.
An extremely thin line of End energy moved along his fingers, and he directly targeted the Elf’s clone.
The End energy reached the clone, and for a moment, the silver light around the Elf stopped moving.
She was still shouting.
"All humans are ugly! And you think you can—"
But she could not finish her sentence, because the rest of the clone no longer existed, her fingers began to disappear.
Then her hands.
Her shoulders.
And finally, her face.
There was no fire and no explosion, the clone simply stopped existing, as if the thread that held the entire image together had reached its end at that point.
Her mirror-like eyes remained fixed on Lian for one last moment, then there was nothing.
The Silver Elf’s clone disappeared from the prison.
Lian lowered his hand.
The End Core trembled for a moment, even this small use had consumed part of its limited energy.
But the result was very good.
Seris glanced at the empty space where the image had been.
Then she looked at Lian’s hand.
"She talked too much," he said in his usual manner, unfortunately, that clone had no use for them.
They could neither interrogate her nor expect her to be stupid enough to reveal anything, and all she had done was curse and complain.
So it was better to get rid of her.
Seris gave a short answer.
"A lot."
Some time later, both of them returned to the central altar of Verendal through the path they had taken before.
The enormous gate closed behind them.

The six stone rings of the ceremony were back on the ground, they had finally left the prison, their goal had been achieved, and they had also identified the real culprit behind everything that had happened.
But when Lian looked around, he realized that something was wrong, Isolde was not there.
And the lights on the walls seemed unusually unstable.
He looked at Seris, the girl had noticed it too.
And at that exact moment...BOOOOOOM!
The entire altar shook.
Dust fell from the enormous pillars.
The young Vorhelm instinctively spread his black wings slightly, while the young Pendragon raised her sword.
Another impact sounded from far away.
This time, the entire altar and hall shook again. It was as if they were about to collapse on top of them.
"What is this now?" He frowned.
Seris said nothing.
She simply moved toward the exit.
Lian followed her, and when they came out of the hall, they saw a sight that destroyed all the brief peace they had felt after the battle with the Demon of End.
Verendal’s defensive dome was shaking.
The enormous golden network covering the entire city bent under repeated attacks, and large waves of light moved across its surface.
In the distant streets, Pendragon forces were moving into position.
Alarms rang out from the defensive towers, and groups of people were moving toward the inner shelters.
Lian raised his head.
Several kilometers away, above the city walls, space was changing around two beings.
One of them moved from one point to another by twisting the distance between them.
The other released an enormous force that made even space and time move aside from that distance.
Every movement and every strike they made was enough to tear reality apart like paper and bend layers of space over one another.
When their two powers collided...KRRRRRAAAASH!
A massive wave of pressure spread across the sky, and part of Verendal’s defensive dome bent inward.
Several towers immediately lit up and sent more energy toward that spot to return the dome to its normal shape.
He stood still for a moment, he recognized these two presences.
Rhaenar Pendragon.
Kairos.
There was no longer any standing face-to-face and negotiating, the two Celestials were actually fighting.
Lian calmly looked at the Silver Corruption Seed in his hand.
Inside the prison, they had managed to stop one of the most dangerous beings in the world from being released.
The Demon of End had fallen asleep again.
But outside? The accusations still remained.
Severin had been arrested first, and now Rhaenar and Kairos had moved beyond threats.
Seris stood beside him, her gaze fixed on the two beings fighting in the sky.
"My father..."
The young Vorhelm let out a slow breath, his black wings moved slightly behind him, and for a moment, he even felt like laughing.
Of course, he was not laughing because he found it amusing, but because it seemed that today still had no intention of ending.
He looked back at the sky, the battle with the Demon of End was over, but apparently, it was still too early to rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 577: Between Two Celestials
paragraphs: CRAAAAAASH!
A massive wave of pressure spread across the sky above Verendal.
The city’s golden dome bent inward under the impact of the two powers, and for a moment, hundreds of defensive towers lit up at the same time.
Thick streams of mana reached from the towers to the dome and slowly pushed its sunken surface back to its original shape.
Lian looked at the sky with a frown.

Several kilometers away, two beings moved among the shattered clouds, and every time they clashed, a large part of the sky changed shape, while the pressure from their attacks could even be felt through the city’s defensive network.
Seris stood beside him, her usual cold gaze fixed on the sky, but the way her fingers were wrapped around her sword’s hilt showed that she was following the situation closely.
Fortunately, they had evidence that could change the course of the entire situation.
"I think it’s time to show them this."
She looked at him.
"Are you going up there?"
He raised his head.
At that moment, one of Kairos’s attacks passed by Rhaenar and struck the bent space at a distant point.
Part of the energy spread out at that spot, and the remaining shockwave made the surface of the dome shake again.
Lian gave a faint smile.
"I don’t think they’re coming down on their own."
Seris looked at the black wings behind him for a moment.
"Be careful."
He gave her a brief glance, as hearing those words from Seris was rather unusual.
"Okay."
The girl nodded, then turned her gaze back to the sky.
The young Vorhelm took a slow breath, and the two huge black wings behind him spread open.
With the first movement of his wings, his body rose from the ground. A small cloud of dust rose from the stone pavement beneath his feet, and he quickly flew toward the sky at a controlled speed.
Using these wings still felt strange.
It was as if two new limbs had been added to his body, limbs he could control in terms of angle, pressure, and movement without even needing to think about it.
The higher he flew, the more pressure he felt from the battle between the two Celestials.
He raised his head slightly.

In the distance, Rhaenar disappeared from one point in the sky with a single step and appeared several hundred meters away. Kairos’s attack passed through the empty space, but before it could move toward Verendal, Rhaenar once again bent the distance between the two points.
The attack changed direction and was released into an empty part of the sky.
Those two beings were truly fighting on another level.
Lian had no intention of interfering in their battle, and he did not even imagine that he could withstand one of their direct attacks.
He only needed to get close enough for them to hear him.
When he reached the upper part of the defensive dome, he slowed down.
Right at that moment...BOOOOM!
A wave of pressure was released not far away.
He was not even in the attack’s direct path, but the remaining force was so strong that his right wing was pushed backward, throwing off his balance for a moment.
The armor plates on his injured shoulder struck each other with a dry sound.
Sharp pain spread through his arm, and he gritted his teeth. By folding one wing, he turned his body sideways.
The wave passed by him.
But before he could correct his position, another wave of pressure moved toward him.
Damn it.
Even the leftover force from their clashes was dangerous to him.
He prepared to use [Ashen Thunder Step] to change his path.
But before he could activate the skill, the space around him changed.

He raised his head. In the distance, Rhaenar was looking at him. The Patriarch had apparently noticed his presence.

"Lian?"

"It seems your trip down there wasn’t without its rewards."
Lian looked at his wings for a moment.
"It’s a long story."
Rhaenar gave a very small smile.
"I’m sure it is."
Then his expression returned to normal.
"But what are you doing here?"
Before answering, he turned his gaze toward Kairos.
The man was floating in the air at a distance, and the pressure of his presence was still heavy, although much of the released mana had now settled down.
Kairos was also examining Lian. His eyes remained on the wings for a moment before returning to his face.
"A Vorhelm?"
"Lian Vorhelm." Lian nodded.

The young Vorhelm held up the seed.
"I think I’ve found something both of you need to see."
Kairos glanced at the seed.
"What is that?"
"Evidence that might prove all the accusations were wrong from the beginning."
Silence fell for a few seconds.
Lian continued.
"We found the person behind the two attacks, someone who forged Stormheart’s signature and the Vorhelm Warform."
Kairos’s expression changed.
"And you expect me to believe a child?"
"No."
He raised the seed a little higher.
"I expect you to examine it yourselves."
This time, the man said nothing, his gaze fixed on the seed.

But a single glance was not enough to determine its origin or all of its uses.
Lian continued.
"If I’m wrong, you lose nothing. You only need to spend a few minutes examining the evidence."
He paused.
"But if I’m right, you two are fighting over something neither of you was responsible for."
Rhaenar gave Kairos a brief glance.
"I don’t think a few minutes will kill us."
Kairos was still looking at the Vorhelm before he slowly spoke.
"If this turns out to be another trick, you’ll be held responsible."
Lian gave a slight shrug.
In the end, the pressure around them decreased, and the sky around Verendal became calmer.
The battle between the two Celestials had stopped, not because they had suddenly started trusting each other, but because evidence had appeared that was worth examining.
Returning to the palace was much faster than Lian’s climb.
By bending the distance, Rhaenar transported them directly to one of the central security areas.
Isolde Pendragon also came there after receiving news that the battle had stopped.
When she saw Lian with Rhaenar and Kairos, she gave him a brief glance, but contrary to his expectations, she did not ask how he had managed to enter the battlefield of two Celestials.
Lian placed the Silver Corruption Seed on the examination platform.

chapters.title: Chapter 578: Aftermath
paragraphs: The two Celestials looked at the seed at the same time, first examining its cracked outer shell, then its central part.
"It has some kind of reflective and corrupting structure."

"It’s not just reflective, part of its structure is designed to record and recreate mana signatures, I wouldn’t say its purpose is to recreate attacks and strikes, but there is a structure inside it that has that ability." Rhaenar whispered.
The seed’s main purpose was to disable formations, but part of its structure had the ability to reflect attacks and skills.
The same structure that was also used in the Thousand-Faced Mirror.
And both Celestials knew very well which race was capable of creating such a seed.
The Silver Elves.
This time, even Kairos leaned forward slightly.
The similarities were not a coincidence, but that was not the point, this seed was only evidence confirming the existence of a Silver Elf.
Both of them looked at Lian.
"Well, kid, do you want to explain?"
Lian looked at them, then gave both of them a full explanation about the Silver Elf he had seen, although he made sure not to say anything about the Demon of End in front of Kairos.
Because of that, many parts of the story had to be left out, but he still managed to explain the main points.

He explained that he and Seris had caught the Silver Elf while she was trying to steal an artifact belonging to the Demon of End, and that the elf had used this seed to disable the formations protecting the treasure.

When the two of them caught the elf, they discovered that she was only a clone. Her main goal was to create conflict between the world’s great powers, start an internal war between them, and steal one of the Pendragons’ greatest treasures.
Of course, that was partly a lie, but he did not want to tell Kairos that the Demon of End was still alive. First, Rhaenar had trusted him and shared such a secret with him.
Second, he was selfish and wanted to kill that Demon himself in the future, he did not want to let other Celestials hunt it down.
After hearing the explanation, Kairos thought for a moment before finally speaking.
"The Silver Elves are capable of carrying out such a false flag operation, but the fact that a clone managed to fool all of us..." He glanced at the seed.
He had never seen such a seed before, but there was no doubt that it belonged to the Silver Elves.
He then looked at Rhaenar, their battle had started because he had learned that his delegation had been captured by the Pendragons.

He knew it was unlikely that the Six Great Families would carry out those murders and then blame the Twelve Ancient Guilds. Unlike the elders, representatives, and lower-level figures, he was a Celestial and knew many truths that others did not.
The Six Great Families would never start a war for survival against the Twelve Ancient Guilds for any reason.
So it was clear that there was a foreign conspiracy, but he had not expected that the outsiders would be so "foreign" that people from another world had managed to play them all.
He sighed.
"At least release the members of my guild."
Isolde nodded and immediately ordered the release of the Primal Firmament delegation.
Kairos went to see his delegation, and it was decided that a meeting about the Silver Elves would be held the next day with all the delegations present.
Isolde and Rhaenar also needed to inspect the Dragon Prison, and Lian was dismissed as well.
However, all of this only lasted for a few hours.
A few hours later, Rhaenar requested that Lian and Seris come to his private room.
Isolde was there as well.
When Lian entered, he had already removed the World-Devourer Bastion armor from his body.
Seris was also feeling better now, both of them had consumed healing potions during these past few hours and had returned to their peak condition.
Rhaenar was sitting behind his desk, and when the two entered, he greeted them with his usual calm smile and said.
"I think it’s time for me to find out exactly what happened."
The young Vorhelm glanced at her, and the girl nodded.
Then he began.
He started from the moment they entered the prison, describing how they saw the Silver Elf and the Silver Corruption Seed.
He explained the awakening of the Demon of End and what had happened afterward.
At first, the Patriarch simply listened.
But when Lian explained the power of the End, his expression changed slightly.
"So it was able to use its own nature."
Lian nodded.
"Not at its full power, but even that amount was enough to tear apart parts of the prison’s space."
Isolde placed her fingers firmly on the armrest of her chair.
"And the main seals?"
"Several of them were damaged, but they were restored." Seris answered, then added after a short pause.
"But all the Dragon Marks had to be sacrificed."
The room fell silent for a few seconds.
Rhaenar looked at his daughter.
"All of them?"
"Almost all the active Marks."
Isolde slowly breathed out.
Although she already knew that the younger generation’s Marks had disappeared, hearing Seris confirm it directly made the matter feel more serious.
Those Dragon Marks had been a great advantage for their younger generation, and now they no longer existed.
However, Rhaenar showed no clear reaction and simply said.
"Continue."
Lian explained how Seris had reached the heart of the formation and returned the energy from all the Dragon Marks to the seal structure.
After the main flow had been restored, a new problem had appeared.
Without a stable source, the formation could not maintain all the gathered energy. And that was what had caused him to enter the central structure.
When his report reached this part, Rhaenar’s calm gaze settled on his right hand.
"So almost all the family’s active Marks disappeared, but it seems you gained one yourself."
The young Vorhelm raised his right hand, and the black and golden Dragon Mark on the back of his hand was clearly visible.
The Ancestral Dragon Mark.
The Patriarch examined it for a few moments, then shifted his gaze to Seris, but there was no anger in his eyes, only a kind of calm understanding.
He knew better than anyone that someone from outside the family could not enter the heart of the formation and receive an Ancestral Grade Mark without direct help.
So his daughter had not only allowed Lian to enter, but had also played a key role in creating that Mark.
The young Pendragon met her father’s gaze without saying anything more.
Lian also only gave a faint smile.
After a few seconds, Rhaenar let out a short laugh.
"Interesting."
And he did not continue the topic.
But the young Vorhelm could tell that a lot was hidden behind that one word. The report about the battle continued.
Lian then explained how the Demon had returned to sleep, how the Silver Elf had lost control of the situation, and how her clone had been destroyed.
When he finished speaking, silence filled the room for a few moments.
Rhaenar leaned back in his chair, then spoke slowly.
"You did a great job." This time, his tone was serious.
Isolde also looked at her daughter, and for a moment, the formal expression on her face softened as she quietly said.
"Indeed."
Seris said nothing, and after a while, Lian brought up another matter.
"There’s another problem."
"Go on."
"The formation is stable for now, but it can’t rely on just our Marks forever."
He raised his right hand slightly.
"The main energy comes from the prison’s own reserves, but those reserves aren’t unlimited. In the past, thousands of active Marks also helped maintain the network’s stability."
Rhaenar nodded, he understood this matter better than the young man did.
"If we want the situation to remain stable for many years, we will probably have to give Dragon Marks to the other Pendragons again."
Isolde looked at her husband, as she also considered this suggestion reasonable.
But the Patriarch remained silent for a few seconds before speaking.
"Restoring all the Marks would cost a lot."
His gaze moved toward the large window in the room.
"Especially now, when a large part of the stored energy is needed to keep the seal stable. I’ll do something else."
That was all he said, and he gave no further explanation.
Lian looked at him for a few seconds, then decided not to ask any more questions and instead asked.
"Do you still want to hide the existence of that Dragon from the world?"
"Of course." Rhaenar answered without hesitation.
"Even after what happened today?"
"Especially after what happened today."
This time, the Patriarch was completely serious.
"You saw what happened, just one person managed to enter the prison’s structure, and we nearly faced a disaster on a continental scale."
He placed his hand on the desk.
"The existence of that Demon must remain hidden."

chapters.title: Chapter 579: How Did a Clone Fool Everyone?
paragraphs: Lian understood this.
Even if half the world feared that creature, the other half would probably try to find a way to use its power.
Humans had always been like that, however, there was another issue.
He looked at Rhaenar.
"Eventually, you’ll have to kill it one day."
Silence lasted for a few seconds, and the Patriarch was no longer smiling.
His gaze remained fixed on the table for a moment before returning to him.
"It’s impossible alone."
Lian did not move, but that sentence caught his full attention for a moment.
Rhaenar Pendragon.
One of the few humans who had completed five evolutions, and one of the most powerful Awakened humans still alive.
And yet, he admitted that he could not kill the Demon of End on his own.
Lian immediately remembered the battle inside the prison. Even with a large part of its power suppressed by the chains and the central spike, the creature had still almost killed him and Seris.
If its full power was ever released, the result of the battle would be clear, even a yawn from that Dragon would be enough to kill the two of them a thousand times over.
Rhaenar moved his gaze between Lian and Seris.
"But perhaps the two of you will be able to do it in the future."
Seris looked at her father for a moment, while Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Us?"
"Not now, and not even anytime soon, but if you continue on your current paths of growth, perhaps one day you’ll reach a point where you can do what our previous generations couldn’t."
He paused briefly.
"And if you really manage to kill the Demon of End, I’ll hand the Dragon Pearl over to you."
The young Vorhelm fell silent for a moment.
"The Dragon Pearl?"
The Patriarch nodded.
"The treasure that creates the Dragon Marks."
The Dragon Pearl.
Rhaenar explained that what the entire world had seen during the Dragon Mark Ceremony was actually the outer form of one of the most valuable treasures belonging to the Demon of End.
An ancient pearl with a direct connection to the nature and bloodline of Dragons.
Its main abilities were to store, compress, and transfer Dragon energy.
But what truly made it valuable was its ability to turn that same energy into Blessings that could remain with their holders for years.
The Dragon Marks.
The Blessings that the Pendragons received across generations all came from that same pearl.
"After our ancestors defeated the Demon of End, they separated the pearl from it."
His gaze returned to Lian.
"Then they used the pearl’s own power to create one of the prison’s main cores."
"Every twenty-five years, part of the energy stored inside the pearl is released in a controlled way, and the Dragon Mark Ceremony uses that same flow."
He gave a slight smile.
"For several centuries, one of that creature’s greatest sources of power has been part of what keeps its prison standing."
Lian actually found this part interesting. If the Demon of End was ever killed, there would no longer be any need to use the pearl to maintain the prison.
And then, a treasure belonging to a creature at the Demon level, with the ability to create Dragon Marks, could fall into their hands.
He looked at Seris, and the girl looked back at him. Neither of them said anything, though it was not as if they planned to return to the prison tomorrow and fight the Demon of End.
They knew very well how great the difference in power between them and that creature was.
But in the future? He thought about the End Core inside his body, and the Ruined Heart. He also remembered the Demon of End’s terrified reaction when it recognized what was inside him.
There were still many unanswered questions, and that Demon certainly knew the answers to some of them. He would probably have to face that creature again one day.
Rhaenar looked at them, then gave a very small smile.
"That’s enough for today."
He stood up.
"You’re both tired, so go and get some rest. Make sure you’re both present at tomorrow’s meeting as well."
Seris nodded, and Lian also stood up, but before leaving, he gave Rhaenar a brief glance.
The Patriarch was still the same calm man who had asked him to stay away from Seris the day before.
Only now, he apparently had no hurry to separate them anymore.
After the door closed, the room remained silent for a while.

chapters.title: Chapter 580: A Guest Hidden for Fifteen Years ( Castle Bonus - )
paragraphs: The discussion continued for several minutes, and different theories were brought up.
Unknown gates, cooperation between some humans and the natives of the Heavenly Realm.

There was even the possibility that the Silver Elves had a type of treasure that allowed them to travel between worlds, exactly like the other native the Federation had recently discovered and imprisoned, who also possessed such a treasure, the Mad Scientist.
However, none of these theories had enough evidence to support them.
Lian listened quietly the entire time, but after a while, he slightly raised his right hand.
"Can I share my guess too?"
Several people turned to look at him, and one of the Blackthorn elders frowned. One of the guild representatives also seemed ready to say that this discussion was no place for young people.
But before anyone could speak,
"Go ahead."
It was Kairos.
At almost the same time, Rhaenar also nodded.
Lian looked at the two Celestials for a moment.
Well.
Since these two had given him permission, probably no one else would object.
He stood up.
Seris gave him a brief glance as he faced the group.
"I think this matter is related to the Primal Firmament."
The atmosphere in the hall became heavy again, and several members of the Primal Firmament delegation sat up straighter almost at the same time.
Severin frowned, and even Kairos narrowed his eyes slightly.
The young Vorhelm noticed their reactions and continued before anyone could object.
"Relax, I’m not saying you were behind the attacks, I’m talking about the Thousand-Faced Mirror."
Kairos watched him for a few seconds.
"Go on."
Lian nodded.
"The Thousand-Faced Mirror was brought to Earth fifteen years ago, right?"
"That’s right."
One of the Primal Firmament members added,
"Of course, the artifact itself is much older. It was discovered in the Heavenly Realm more than sixty years ago, but we brought it to Earth fifteen years ago."
Lian nodded. This was exactly what he needed.
"And the original artifact belonged to the Silver Elves."
"As far as our records show, yes." Severin remained silent for a few seconds before answering.
The young Vorhelm looked around at the people present.
"Then perhaps the answer entered our world fifteen years ago."
Murmurs spread among the representatives, and one of the Federation members leaned forward slightly.
"What do you mean?"
Lian pointed at the image of the seed.
"What we saw yesterday wasn’t the real body of an Elf, it was a mana structure controlled from a distance, something like a clone, but not exactly, to be more precise, it was a puppet."
Then he looked at Kairos.
"Now, imagine that something was hidden inside the Thousand-Faced Mirror when it was brought here."
Severin frowned.
"Something like what?"
"A dormant pattern, not a living creature, but something that didn’t release any unusual energy of its own and was simply waiting for the right conditions."
One of the Federation members remained silent for a moment before speaking under his breath.
"Then ordinary inspections might not have detected it at all."
Lian nodded.
"Exactly."
He then explained that such a structure could have activated after being brought to Earth, using some kind of special system or even the energy stored inside the mirror itself.

If the Silver Elves’ technology was really this advanced, perhaps a reflection of an Elf’s consciousness could have moved through the human world by using tools, connected networks, and different communication channels.
Of course, it wouldn’t have been a real body, but a structure that used the energy and information around it to recreate its presence each time.
He placed his hand on the table.
"Fifteen years is a very long time."

"It’s more than enough time to learn about the families, their old conflicts, their political relationships, their resources, and even the personalities of the people who control the most powerful forces in the world."
His gaze moved between the different seats.
"Imagine if someone had planned from the beginning to turn Earth’s powerful forces against each other one day."
He paused.
"They would have had fifteen years to learn which family hated which other family, which guild had problems with whom, and how each of them would react when threatened."
Lian then brought up the events of yesterday, the murder of a Valemont member, the accusation against Stormheart, followed by the second attack and the accusation against Vorhelm.
After that, the accusations had turned toward the Thousand-Faced Mirror and the Primal Firmament.
"None of our reactions were unusual, and that’s exactly what made this dangerous."
"The person behind this plan didn’t need to control our decisions, they only needed to know what we would usually do when put under pressure."
For a few seconds, heavy silence filled the hall.

"So perhaps that reflection had been active in our world for fifteen years, gathering information. Maybe it had also been in contact with the Silver Elves in the Heavenly Realm and was being controlled remotely like a puppet."
His gaze briefly fell on the image of the seed.
"Then it waited for the best opportunity."
The Pendragon Ceremony, the day when almost all the most powerful forces in the world had gathered in one city.
What better opportunity could there be?
Kairos had listened quietly the entire time. Now, he leaned back in his chair.
"So, in your opinion, they spent fifteen years preparing this plan just to turn us against each other?"
Lian said nothing for a moment. The answer was both yes and no, because turning them against each other was not their only plan.
Their main goal wasn’t simply to start a conflict between the Six Great Families and the Twelve Ancient Guilds. The Silver Elves had also tried to release a Demon-rank creature.
A creature that could destroy a large part of Europe, but he didn’t want to reveal that secret.
Lian briefly glanced at Rhaenar, who remained calmly seated.
He turned back to Kairos.
"Turning Earth’s powerful forces against each other was definitely one of their goals, they might have other goals as well, we still don’t know everything."
The statement was correct on the surface, but it wasn’t the whole truth.
Kairos watched him for a few seconds before slowly nodding. Apparently, he had no intention of continuing the discussion for now.
Meanwhile, several Federation members were thinking hard about what they had heard.
Because if Lian’s theory was correct, a foreign being had been present in their world for fifteen years.
It had spent fifteen years gathering information, and it might even have sent some of Earth’s sensitive information to the Heavenly Realm.
This was no longer just a matter of two murders, it was a security threat on a global scale.
One of the Overlords present placed his hand on the table.
"We can’t just leave this matter alone."
Several people looked at him, and the man continued.
"They managed to carry out an operation like this inside our world today, what about tomorrow? They might target another city, or one of the Federation’s main facilities."
Adrian Stormheart nodded.
"If they really found a way to infiltrate our world like this, we need to stop them before they use it again."
Gregor Valemont also didn’t object this time. He had still lost one of his family’s members.
And now, at least he knew that the real enemy was probably outside the circle of the great families.
Isolde joined the discussion from her seat.
"What do you think about a joint operation against the Silver Elves’ bases?"
Several people looked at her for a moment. This was no small proposal.
Entering the territory of a native race and attacking its facilities could have major political and military consequences.
But the Matriarch continued.
"Not a blind attack."
Her gaze moved across the guild representatives.

"First, we’ll find the origin of the seed and identify the group that created it or directed the operation. Then the forces stationed in the Heavenly Realm will carry out a joint operation against those same facilities, this can serve as a warning to them."
This proposal was more reasonable.
Even the Primal Firmament couldn’t easily oppose it.
If the method of infiltration had really come from the Heavenly Realm, leaving it unanswered would only make the enemy bolder.

The discussion continued for a while, covering the number of forces, the information they needed, the area of the operation, and how none of the powers should take advantage of this situation to seize more resources or territory.
In the end, they reached an initial agreement.
A joint team of specialists and forces stationed in the Heavenly Realm would be formed to investigate the matter and prepare for the operation.
Lian found this interesting. Yesterday, these same people had almost gone to war over the two attacks.
Now, they were talking about a joint operation.
And the main reason for this change was the small seed he had taken from the heart of the prison.
When the main part of the meeting ended, Kairos stood up and fixed his gaze on him.
"Lian Vorhelm."
"Yes?"
The Celestial examined him for a few seconds before speaking.
"I owe you my thanks."
Several people in the hall stopped moving for a moment.
A Celestial.
And one from the Primal Firmament at that.
He was thanking a young man who had only recently completed his First Evolution.
"If you hadn’t found that seed, we would probably be dealing with something very different right now instead of holding this meeting."
"I only did what needed to be done." Lian gave him a slight smile.
Kairos laughed briefly.
"Good." Then his gaze moved toward the Vorhelm seats.
"I heard that your relationship with your own family isn’t very good."
The expressions of several members of the Vorhelm delegation immediately changed. Cassius, who was seated in the family’s official section, looked more serious.
But he said nothing.
Kairos looked back at Lian.
"If you ever decide to separate your path from your family, the Primal Firmament could be a good place for you."

"If you hadn’t found that seed, we would probably be dealing with something very different right now instead of holding this meeting."
"I only did what needed to be done." Lian gave him a slight smile.
Kairos laughed briefly.
"Good." Then his gaze moved toward the Vorhelm seats.
"I heard that your relationship with your own family isn’t very good."
The expressions of several members of the Vorhelm delegation immediately changed.
Cassius, who was seated in the family’s official section, looked more serious.
But he said nothing.
Kairos looked back at Lian.
"If you ever decide to separate your path from your family, the Primal Firmament could be a good place for you."

paragraphs: "If you ever decide to separate your path from your family, the Primal Firmament could be a good place for you."
A strange silence filled the hall.
This was no longer a simple thank-you.

One of the most powerful people in the world, a member of the strongest Ancient Guild in the world, had openly invited Lian to join their guild in front of the representatives of the Six Great Families.
Lian raised an eyebrow for a moment, he hadn’t expected such an offer.
Of course, from Kairos’s point of view, the matter wasn’t just about his current strength.
A young man who had grown at an unusual rate at such a young age had managed to prevent a global crisis through reasoning and gathering evidence.
Such a person was valuable to any major power, but to the Vorhelms?
Publicly inviting him to join an independent guild, especially when the family’s succession was approaching, was not something they would be happy about.
The expressions of the Vorhelm delegation members turned ugly. They wanted to object, they didn’t want to lose Lian, but they didn’t dare say anything against a Celestial.
Lian hadn’t decided how to respond when Rhaenar’s voice rang out.
"We still have a lot of work to do regarding the Thousand-Faced Mirror."
Kairos turned his gaze toward the patriarch, who continued with the same calm expression.
"We need to make sure that the artifact wasn’t hiding any other structures."
Then he looked at the Federation representatives.

"And this investigation shouldn’t be limited to the mirror, all treasures brought to Earth from the Heavenly Realm must be checked again, especially artifacts that can store mana, record information, or communicate over long distances."
Several people began discussing the suggestion after hearing it.
Such an investigation would not be easy.
Hundreds of ancient artifacts were held by the families, guilds, the Federation, and even some countries.
But if one artifact had managed to hide an unknown structure for years, there was no guarantee that others hadn’t been brought here as well.
Rhaenar placed his hand on the table.
"We’re already dealing with the Ruined Realm, the Heavenly Realm, and the growing number of rifts, we can’t allow a civil war to start at the same time."
His tone became slightly more serious this time.
"Earth’s security must come before any other disagreements."
Kairos looked at him for a few seconds before giving a brief smile.
Apparently, he had realized that Rhaenar had deliberately changed the subject of Lian’s invitation, but he said nothing and simply turned back toward the young Vorhelm.
"My offer still stands."
Lian nodded.
"Thank you."
Kairos then looked at Rhaenar.
"The Primal Firmament will also help with the investigation, we’ll make the Thousand-Faced Mirror available to the experts for a joint examination."
"Good."
Kairos prepared to leave with his delegation, but just before reaching the door, Rhaenar spoke again.
"Aren’t you staying for the Heir Announcement Ceremony?"
He stopped and looked at the patriarch for a moment, then his gaze fell on Seris.
The girl was sitting beside Lian with her usual cold expression.
Kairos gave a very slight smile.
"There’s no need."
He paused.
"After all these years, you’ve finally found a worthy heir. It looks like a golden generation is coming, congratulations."
Then, without saying anything else, he left the hall with the members of the Primal Firmament.
Lian glanced at Rhaenar for a moment. The patriarch was still calm, and it wasn’t long before the meeting came to an end.
Several hours later, the unfinished ceremony began again.
This time, there were no long ceremonies and formalities like before, but thousands of people had still gathered in Verendal’s central square.

The seats of the Six Great Families, the remaining representatives of the Ancient Guilds, the main members of the Pendragon Family, and the special guests who were still in Verendal because the city remained under lockdown.
Everyone’s eyes were fixed on the central altar.
The same place where Seris had received the Ancestral Mark, but unlike the previous day, there were now many rumors spreading through the crowd.
The Dragon Marks had disappeared, not just one or two, but almost all the active Dragon Marks belonging to the younger generation of the Pendragon Family.
No one knew the reason. Some thought something had gone wrong during the ceremony, while others suspected that yesterday’s security crisis had affected the Dragon Pearl.
However, no official explanation had been given.
And this had increased the worry and dissatisfaction among the younger generation of the family.
Lian looked around from his seat, he could see many people still checking their empty hands from time to time.
Kaelen.
Lysandra.
Tristan.
Even Lucien didn’t seem very happy, despite his usual calmness.
He could understand the reason.
If he were in their place and suddenly lost his most important reward without any explanation after years of effort, he probably wouldn’t feel good either.
But it had nothing to do with him.
Seris was standing not too far away, she also glanced at the members of her generation but said nothing.
She simply straightened her clothes and walked toward the altar.
Rhaenar Pendragon appeared on the main platform alongside Isolde, and the square slowly fell silent as the two arrived.
The patriarch looked at the crowd for a few seconds before speaking in a clear voice.
"Twenty-five years ago, the previous generation of the Pendragon Family stood before the Dragon Marks."
His voice was calm, but it carried a certain weight.
"Some of them are commanders, family elders, or parents of the new generation today, and sadly, some are no longer with us."
Several people in the main seats lowered their heads.
"Now it’s the new generation’s turn."
His gaze moved across the family’s five strongest young members.
Tristan.
Lysandra.
Kaelen.
Lucien.
And finally, Seris.
"Talent, strength, and Marks are important, but none of them alone is enough to lead the Pendragon Family."
"The person who takes control of this family’s future must be able to accept responsibility for decisions that even their closest people may not understand."
This sentence was probably not meant only for the crowd, as Rhaenar also fixed his gaze on his daughter.
"Seris Pendragon."
Seris took a step forward and stood in the center of the altar.
Her black and white clothes looked calm under the golden light of the square, and the Ancestral Mark on the back of her right hand was clearly visible.
"The bearer of the Ancestral Mark."
For a moment, murmurs rose from the crowd. Even now, hearing this title was strange for many Pendragons.
"From today onward, you will be the official heir of the Pendragon Family."
A brief silence followed, then applause rose from some of the seats.
She lowered her head slightly.
Her usual calm expression remained on her face, she recited the short heir’s oath and stood straight again.
Lian watched her from his seat, and a small smile appeared on his face for a moment.
Considering everything that had happened over the past few days, seeing the ceremony finally reach its proper conclusion felt strange.
But apparently, Rhaenar hadn’t finished speaking yet.
"And there’s one more person I need to thank."
The patriarch’s voice caused the murmurs in the crowd to fall silent again.
He was looking directly at a particular seat.
"Lian Vorhelm."
For a moment, Lian even thought he had heard wrong, then he realized that the gazes around him were turning toward him one after another.
Well. This wasn’t part of the plan.
The patriarch continued.
"I want to thank Seris and Lian for what they did for the Pendragon Family."
Several people in the main seats looked at each other.
What had they done? No explanation had been given.
"And today, the Pendragon Family also recognizes the second Ancestral Mark of this generation."
A strange silence fell, and several people instinctively looked toward Seris.
The second Mark?
Who?
"A Mark that now belongs to Lian Vorhelm."
This time, not even applause could be heard. For a few seconds, the square fell into almost complete silence.
Then the murmurs began.
"What?"
"Vorhelm?"
"An Ancestral Mark?"
"How is that possible?"
"How can a Vorhelm obtain a Dragon Mark?"
"When and how did this happen?"
Lian slowly stood up from his seat, in the official Vorhelm section, Cassius had fixed his gaze on him.
For a moment, his expression seemed caught between surprise and something like laughter.
But the rest of the delegation didn’t look very happy.
On the other side, the younger generation of the Pendragon Family was almost openly shocked.
Kaelen looked at his right hand, the same hand where the Crown Mark had appeared the previous day.
Now it was empty.
Lysandra stared at Lian in disbelief.
Even Lucien, who usually had complete control over his expression, couldn’t fully hide the change in his eyes this time.
And the family elders? Some of them looked at each other from the main seats.
Several people were whispering under their breath.
Lian could guess part of what they were saying, all the active Dragon Marks of the younger generation had disappeared.
But a Vorhelm not only had a Dragon Mark, but had also become the bearer of an Ancestral Mark.
He slightly raised his right hand, and the Dragon Mark on the back of his hand lit up.
This time, there was no room left to doubt that the Mark existed, even from a distance, people could feel that its quality was different.
The Mark was real.
More importantly, Rhaenar Pendragon himself had confirmed it. No one dared to openly claim that the patriarch was wrong.
But that didn’t mean they were satisfied.
Not at all.
The Pendragons were not happy about this in the slightest.
Rhaenar allowed the murmurs to continue for a few moments before speaking again.
"As thanks for what these two have done, I’ve prepared a special reward."
This time, even Lian became curious.
What reward?
The patriarch looked between him and Seris before speaking.
"Both of you are allowed to train in the Dragon Blood River for one full month."
This time, the crowd’s reaction was completely different. Several people almost stood up from their seats at the same time.
The murmurs grew much louder.
Even some of the family elders couldn’t hide their surprise.
The Dragon Blood River.
One of the Pendragon Family’s most valuable cultivation resources, a place where a refined part of the remaining blood of the Demon of End was kept.
The blood of a Demon-rank creature did not lose its value, even after centuries.
Quite the opposite.
If properly preserved and refined, it could be used for generations.
But what truly made this resource valuable was its ability to refine the body and soul.
Lian’s expression became more serious when he heard the name of the river, he had now reached the First Evolution’s attribute limit of twenty thousand.
But refining the body and soul was different from directly increasing attributes.
If he could use the blood of a demonic dragon to refine the structure of his body and soul, the result might be far beyond what he could gain from several thousand attribute points.
And for a full month?
He looked at Rhaenar. This was no small reward.
But for the Pendragons, the matter was even more serious.
Many members of the family were not allowed to use the Dragon Blood River for more than a few days or a limited number of sessions during their entire lives.
This resource was so valuable that even the elders made decisions about its usage with great care.
And now, Rhaenar had given one full month to Seris and Lian Vorhelm.
This time, the murmurs didn’t die down easily.
The younger generation of the Pendragon Family, who were still unhappy about losing their Marks, felt even worse after seeing such a huge reward given to an outsider.
Kaelen clenched his jaw tightly, his gaze moving between Lian, Seris, and Rhaenar.
Lysandra sat quietly, but her fingers had curled around the armrest of her chair.
Even some of the elders who had tried to stay out of the ceremony until now no longer seemed calm.
One of the senior family elders pressed his hand against the armrest of his chair, the same man who had opposed Lian getting close to Seris from the beginning.
He had remained silent the entire time.
When Rhaenar thanked Lian, he said nothing.
Even when the second Ancestral Mark was announced, he didn’t object, despite his obvious dissatisfaction.
But the Dragon Blood River?
For a full month?
This was no longer something he could tolerate.
The man stood up.
The sound of his chair scraping backward could be heard among the murmurs in the square.
"Patriarch!"
The surrounding gazes turned toward him.
Rhaenar turned his head slightly, his expression still as calm as ever.
"Yes?"
The family elder first gave Lian a brief glance before continuing.
"All the Dragon Marks of our children have disappeared without any explanation."
His voice grew louder.
"They worked for years to reach this stage, some of them had planned their entire future around those Marks!"
Several members of the younger generation instinctively nodded.
The man continued.
"But now, a Vorhelm has received an Ancestral Mark, and you’re even allowing him to spend an entire month in the Dragon Blood River?!"
For a moment, a heavy silence fell. No one intervened, because this was the same question that many members of the family had in their minds.
The family elder took a step forward, his voice firmer this time.
"With all due respect, Patriarch... I object to this decision!"

chapters.title: Chapter 582: The Problem Is His Last Name
paragraphs: "With all due respect, Patriarch... I object to this decision!"
The voice of the Pendragon family elder echoed across Verendal’s central square.
The applause that had risen moments earlier to announce the family’s new heir had now completely died down.
Thousands of people were sitting in different sections, their gazes moving between the man who had raised his objection, Lian Vorhelm, and Rhaenar Pendragon.
The family elder was still standing.
His fingers were gripping the armrest of his chair tightly, and his expression made it clear that he had struggled with himself for a long time before raising his objection.
He wasn’t the only one dissatisfied with the patriarch’s decision.
In the younger generation’s section, Caelen had clenched his right hand into a fist, the same hand that had held the Crown Mark until yesterday. Now, there was no trace of the Mark left.

Lysandra was also looking at the altar with a serious expression, even some elders who usually never caused the slightest disorder during official ceremonies were now openly waiting for Rhaenar’s answer.
However, the patriarch wasn’t in a hurry to speak, he looked at the man who had objected for a few seconds, then placed his hands behind his back.
"I’ve heard your objection, and I’ll keep it in mind as advice when making future decisions." He finally answered in a calm tone.
The man raised his head for a moment, and several other elders also sat up a little straighter.
But Rhaenar hadn’t finished speaking yet.
"However, it seems you’ve forgotten something." His gaze moved across the other family elders for a moment before returning to the man.
"I announced my decision, I didn’t ask you to vote on it."
An even heavier silence fell over the square, Rhaenar hadn’t even raised his voice, but his words were clear enough.
He continued.

"You’re free to express your opinion, even if you disagree with my decision. But deciding who deserves to use the family’s resources is my responsibility. As long as I’m responsible for the Pendragons, I won’t ask anyone for permission to do that."
The man who had objected pressed his lips together.
The patriarch briefly glanced at Lian.
"And if your only problem is that Lian carries the Vorhelm surname, you’d better find a stronger reason."
This time, several people in the Vorhelm guests’ section instinctively looked at one another.
Lian, who had been standing calmly until then, slightly raised the corner of his mouth.
Well, at least I don’t have to answer this one myself.
But the man who had objected still didn’t back down.
"Patriarch, the problem isn’t just his surname." His tone had become lower, but he was still speaking firmly.

"Our children lost the Marks they had spent years trying to obtain yesterday. No one even knows why yet, and now you’re saying that someone from outside the family has received an Ancestral Mark and is even allowed to train in the Dragon Blood River for a month."
He paused and looked toward the younger generation’s section.
"How do you expect them to accept this decision?"
This time, Rhaenar didn’t answer immediately.
His gaze remained on the faces of the family’s young members for a moment. Some were angry, some were confused, and others still hoped their Marks could somehow return.
Then he spoke.
"Regarding the lost Marks, you have the right to ask for an explanation."
The murmurs in the square grew slightly louder.

"Yesterday, the very foundation of the Dragon Marks was threatened by something that could have destroyed the entire legacy of our family, to prevent that from happening, the energy of the active Marks was returned to the Dragon Pearl.
Several of the more experienced elders became more serious when they heard the words "the very foundation."
They knew about the connection between the Dragon Marks and the family’s ancient Pearl, although even most of them didn’t know the truth about the being imprisoned deep beneath Verendal.
Rhaenar continued.
"If that decision hadn’t been made, there might never have been another Dragon Mark Ceremony in the future."
This time, no one answered immediately, losing the Marks of the current generation was a disaster, but losing the main source of the Marks?
Such an event could have destroyed one of the Pendragons’ most important legacies forever.
The family elder frowned slightly.
"Then who decided to sacrifice all the Marks?"
Rhaenar hadn’t even opened his mouth when a calm voice came from beside the altar.
"Me."
Seris took a step forward.
Her formal black and white clothes looked calm under the golden light of the altar, and all eyes turned toward the family’s new heir.
She looked directly at the man who had objected.
"I sacrificed the Marks."
The man remained silent for a moment.
"My Lady... you?"
"Yes."
"So you knew all the Marks would disappear?"
