chapters.title: Chapter 583: They Can Cry About It
paragraphs: "No, it doesn’t."
Several people were surprised by this answer for a moment.
Lian continued.
"I don’t expect you to be happy about this situation either, but my family name doesn’t mean you can treat the responsibility I accepted as worthless."
He paused briefly.
"If the problem is that a Vorhelm got a Pendragon Mark, then you should probably talk to the Dragon Pearl itself, since it was the one that chose me."
He then smiled.
Several guests failed to hide their smiles completely, while some even burst out laughing.
However, the protesting elder was not amused at all, and he opened his mouth to respond, but at that moment...
"Enough."
Rhaenar’s voice was not loud, but all the whispers near the altar stopped.
The patriarch looked across the family elders.
"Seris is my official heir, and Lian is my approved guest, the rewards for both of them have been decided and will not change."
Then he looked directly at the protesting man.
"I will deal with the issue of the lost Marks separately, but today’s ceremony will not turn into a place for more complaints."
The man remained still for a moment before lowering his head.
"I understand, Patriarch."
Rhaenar gave a small nod.
"Good."
With the same calmness he always showed, he announced the end of the ceremony.

No threats or displays of power were needed, the decision had been made, and as long as Rhaenar Pendragon stood at the head of the family, no one could change it simply because they were unhappy with it.
However, as Lian left the altar, he clearly noticed that some of the young members and elders were still giving him hostile looks.
It seemed that having an Ancestral Dragon Mark would bring its own troubles, but he didn’t care, the Blessing from that Mark was so powerful that he had no intention of giving it up.
If the Pendragons were so upset, they could go cry about it.
He didn’t even care about the Vorhelm family, his own family, so why should he care about the Pendragons?
The ceremony had ended, but discussions about it continued throughout the palace corridors.
As he passed through one of the side halls, he felt several curious gazes on him.
Some guests openly looked at the back of his right hand, while others began whispering to each other after he passed.
Of course, he had no interest in listening to all of it.
If he reacted every time someone started a rumor about him, he would probably never have time to write his system reports or practice his skills.
"Lian."
He turned around when he heard the voice.
Cassius Vorhelm was walking toward him from the end of the corridor.
His older brother was still wearing the formal clothes of the Vorhelm delegation, but unlike during the ceremony, his expression was a little more relaxed.
When he came closer, his gaze settled on Lian’s Ancestral Mark.
"I still can’t believe it."
"Which part?"
"That a Vorhelm managed to get a Pendragon Dragon Mark."
"Apparently, the Mark itself had no problem with it."
Lian raised his right hand slightly and smiled.
Cassius let out a short laugh before shaking his head.
"I wish the rest of the family could take this as easily as you do."
His tone became more serious this time.
"Do you know what will happen when Father hears the news?"
"He’ll probably be happy."
The young Vorhelm paused for a moment, considering what he knew about his father, that man would definitely be happy about this and would see it as an excuse to make fun of Rhaenar.
A Vorhelm had managed to change a centuries-old tradition that the Pendragons were extremely proud of, and had obtained a Mark for himself.
It was like a slap in the Pendragons’ faces.
Cassius looked at him and sighed.
"Yeah, Father will be happy, and that will upset some other people."
There were already many political conflicts within the family.
Lian smiled but said nothing.
Cassius walked with him for a few more steps before stopping beside a tall window, where other people passing through the corridor would not be able to hear their conversation easily.

"Two Celestials have shown interest in you in less than a few days, one of them personally invited you to join the Primal Firmament, and Rhaenar Pendragon has also allowed you to receive his family’s greatest legacy."
He glanced at the quiet corridor.
"How do you think the other Vorhelms will see this?"
"That depends on which Vorhelm you’re talking about."
Lian put his hands into the pockets of his clothes.
Cassius smiled for a moment.
"Exactly."
Then his expression became serious.

"Some of them want you to return, they were already talking about it even before this ceremony, but now they have more reasons. In their eyes, if the family allows you to get closer to the Primal Firmament or the Pendragons, it’s losing one of the most talented members of your generation."
He paused.
"But others are afraid of the same thing, they’re afraid you’ll return and try to take revenge."
His older brother said this in a calm tone, but the meaning was clear.
Lian had spent a large part of his life outside the family’s attention, but those who had once considered him unimportant now had to think about the possibility of his return.
And for some of them, that possibility was not welcome.
"I’ll return in a few days, it’s better to give my report in person before the news reaches them through several different versions."
"That’s a good idea."
"And one more thing, do you know Father will be returning soon, probably within the next month?"
"I don’t know what decision he’ll make about you when he returns, but you’d better be prepared, I think he might summon you."
Lian raised his shoulders slightly.
"I don’t plan to return for now."
Cassius looked at him before nodding.
"I know."
There was a little sadness in his voice, but he did not try to convince him.
"I just want you to know what’s happening before someone else makes a decision for you."
"Thanks, Brother."
Lian gave him a small smile.
Cassius smiled as well, then made a brief gesture with his hand and walked away down the corridor.
Lian watched him leave for a few seconds.
Among all the members of the Vorhelm family, Cassius was still one of the few people who could talk to him without thinking about political interests.
Of course, that did not mean his brother’s position was simple, Cassius himself held an important place in the family.
And Lian’s possible return could even affect his future, but so far, there had been no sign of hostility in his behavior.
He took a quiet breath, it seemed that after the Pendragons, it was now time for the Vorhelm troubles.
His father might really order him to return, and although he said he wanted to ignore him, things were not that simple.
His father was not an ordinary man, even among all the Celestials, he was an absolute Overlord.
There was a reason even Rhaenar Pendragon called that man a madman, it wasn’t because his father was an unstable lunatic.
It was because none of the other Celestials wanted to face him directly either.

A few minutes later, Seris joined him. She had changed out of her formal ceremony clothes and into something simpler, her hair rested neatly on her shoulders, and there was no sign of what had happened over the past few days.
Lian smiled when he saw her.
"Did you escape from the congratulations session?"
Seris nodded.
"It’s over."
The two of them walked along a corridor overlooking the palace’s inner garden.
The evening light fell through the tall windows onto the stone floor, and the sound of the garden fountains created a peaceful atmosphere, unlike the noise in the ceremony hall.
They said nothing for a while.
The young Vorhelm noticed that she occasionally looked at the Mark on her own hand.
"Are you still thinking about what happened today?"
"The Marks."
The girl nodded.
"Do you think you made the wrong choice?"
"No."
She answered without hesitation, but after walking a few more steps, she continued.
"Some people will hate me."
Lian said nothing for a few seconds, he knew Seris would not bring something like this up without a reason.
She usually paid little attention to what others thought of her, but today’s situation was different.
Those who had lost their Marks were members of her own family, people who were supposed to be under her leadership one day.
The problem was that the real reason behind what had happened could not be explained either.
"Probably some of them will."
He nodded, when people lose something valuable because of someone else, even if that person is their own mother, they can become angry, let alone in the current situation.
Seris looked at him.

"When someone loses something they’ve worked toward for years, it’s natural for them to look for someone to blame, especially when they don’t know the whole truth, but that doesn’t mean your decision was wrong."
"I know."
She nodded.
"Good, because if the same situation happens again, I won’t change my decision either."
The girl turned her head toward him.
"An heir isn’t supposed to keep everyone happy all the time, sometimes they have to choose the option that causes the least damage out of several bad choices."
Seris looked at him for a while before slowly nodding.
Lian added with a small smile.
"Besides, I’ve become a bearer of a Pendragon Mark now too, it seems some of your family’s troubles have reached me as well, and they’re not happy with me either."
"I’m sorry."
Her lips lifted slightly, she was the one who had suggested that plan.
"Well, at least those wings are beautiful enough to make putting up with a few angry old men’s complaints worth it, so I guess we can put up with their complaints together."
He laughed and added softly.
This time, Seris did not hide her smile, although it was so brief that someone else probably would not have noticed it.
Lian looked at her and decided to leave the matter of the Marks aside for now.
"By the way, I have a question."
"Ask."
"What exactly is the Dragon Blood River like?"
"Dragon blood is kept in it."
The young Vorhelm fell silent for a moment before looking at her.
"I figured that part out from the name. Can you elaborate more?"

The girl nodded.
"Do you think you made the wrong choice?"
"No."
She answered without hesitation, but after walking a few more steps, she continued.
"Some people will hate me."
Lian said nothing for a few seconds, he knew Seris would not bring something like this up without a reason.
She usually paid little attention to what others thought of her, but today’s situation was different.
Those who had lost their Marks were members of her own family, people who were supposed to be under her leadership one day.
The problem was that the real reason behind what had happened could not be explained either.
"Probably some of them will."
He nodded, when people lose something valuable because of someone else, even if that person is their own mother, they can become angry, let alone in the current situation.
Seris looked at him.

"When someone loses something they’ve worked toward for years, it’s natural for them to look for someone to blame, especially when they don’t know the whole truth, but that doesn’t mean your decision was wrong."
"I know."
She nodded.
"Good, because if the same situation happens again, I won’t change my decision either."
The girl turned her head toward him.
"An heir isn’t supposed to keep everyone happy all the time, sometimes they have to choose the option that causes the least damage out of several bad choices."
Seris looked at him for a while before slowly nodding.
Lian added with a small smile.
"Besides, I’ve become a bearer of a Pendragon Mark now too, it seems some of your family’s troubles have reached me as well, and they’re not happy with me either."
"I’m sorry."
Her lips lifted slightly, she was the one who had suggested that plan.
"Well, at least those wings are beautiful enough to make putting up with a few angry old men’s complaints worth it, so I guess we can put up with their complaints together."
He laughed and added softly.
This time, Seris did not hide her smile, although it was so brief that someone else probably would not have noticed it.
Lian looked at her and decided to leave the matter of the Marks aside for now.
"By the way, I have a question."
"Ask."
"What exactly is the Dragon Blood River like?"
"Dragon blood is kept in it."
The young Vorhelm fell silent for a moment before looking at her.
"I figured that part out from the name.
Can you elaborate more?"

chapters.title: Chapter 584: The Dragon Blood River
paragraphs: "The dragon blood kept in the river has been refined by formations, the main part of it is dangerous for most Awakened, even if they have gone through more evolutions."
Lian nodded, this was not surprising.
The blood of a Demon-rank creature, even after centuries had passed, should not be something an ordinary human could endure without problems.
Even for the Awakened, something like this could be dangerous, especially when it came from a creature that carried the nature of the End.
Seris continued.
"The formations control the energy in the blood, when you enter the training area, that energy will enter your body and soul."
"And refine them."
He added.
"Yeah."
"Which parts?"
"Bones, muscles, organs, mana channels, and the soul too, if you can endure the pressure."
The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes slightly, this was exactly what interested him.
He had now reached the stat limit of the First Evolution. Increasing his stats directly was no longer possible, but refining his body and soul was not limited by his stat cap.
Two creatures could have the same physical strength stats, but the different quality of their bodies could allow one to perform much better than the other.
And Lian had wanted to strengthen the structure of his monstrous body even further for a long time.
"So, the more we can endure, the better the results?"
Seris nodded.
"To a certain extent, but if your body can’t endure the energy, you’ll get injured."
He thought for a moment, dragon blood, an Ancestral Mark, and the End Core, all three were connected to the same creature.
The Demon of End.
He did not know what would happen when these three things were brought together, but he intended to proceed carefully.
Especially since he now understood better than ever how dangerous it was to play with the power of a living Demon.
A few hours later, the two of them reached their destination, a massive gate made of black stone stood before them.
Complex golden lines were carved across its surface, and even from a few meters away, they could feel the flow of power between them.
When Seris approached, the gate’s formation reacted, several golden rings inside the stone began to rotate, and a deep sound came from behind the gate.
The gate slowly opened.
And what lay behind it left even Lian silent for a moment, a huge underground hall spread out before them.
The ceiling was so high that parts of it were hidden in darkness, and dozens of thick pillars extended upward along both sides of the river.
But the most important part was the river itself, a wide and deep stream of dark red liquid flowed through the middle of the hall.
Its color did not resemble fresh blood, it was darker and denser, and almost black lines could be seen beneath its surface in some places.
Unlike ordinary water, the river moved very slowly, and with every small wave, a heavy mana pressure spread through the surrounding air.
A thin layer of red mist floated above the blood, and the golden formations carved into the walls absorbed parts of it.
Lian took a few steps forward, he had not entered the river yet, but he could already feel the energy pressing against his skin.
"Well."
He looked at the red current.
"Now I understand why using this is so valuable."
Seris stood beside him.
"The upper section has been refined."
The young Vorhelm followed her gaze.
In the distance, where the river passed between two stone walls, several massive golden rings were placed above the flow of blood.
Before the dense energy reached the training area, it passed through those same formations.
Parts of its unstable pressure were separated and stored in special containers.

Therefore, what flowed before him was still the blood of a dragon with enormous power, but it was no longer in its raw and uncontrolled state, even in this refined form, it was still unbearable for most Awakened.
Lian could feel this clearly.
The two of them went to separate training areas along the river.
They were several dozen meters apart, but they could still see each other through the main river.
He first put his right hand into the blood, it was a strange feeling.
The liquid was warm, but not like hot water, and a dense pressure settled over his skin from the moment he touched it.
A few seconds later, the first stream of energy entered his body, and the muscles in his forearm tightened on their own, then the pressure reached his bones.
Lian curled his fingers.
This energy really is heavy.

He slowly entered the river, and when the blood reached his chest, the pressure increased several times, as if something from outside was trying to pass through his skin and muscles and reach the deepest parts of his body.
He slowly breathed out.
His body already had the structure of a Fallen Monster, but even a body like his could not accept all the blood’s energy without resistance.
A dull pain began to form deep inside his bones.
However, he did not stop the flow, he closed his eyes and allowed a controlled amount of the blood’s energy to enter his body.
No more than he could endure.
In another part of the river, Seris had also entered the blood, she sat down on a stone platform beneath the river’s surface and closed her eyes.
The refinement had begun.
A few minutes later, Lian noticed another change.
Inside his body, the End Core was slowly reacting, responding to the nature of the power entering his body from the river.
The blood of the Demon of End, and a core formed from a part of that same Demon’s nature.
It was natural for there to be some kind of compatibility between them, and if his guess was correct, this blood contained some Essence of the End.
And there should be enough of it to strengthen his core, exactly as he had done with the Eclipse Core.
He kept the incoming flow at a level that allowed his body to use it for refinement.
But strengthening the End Core was not his only goal, his body and soul also needed to become stronger.
Hours passed.
The initial pain did not decrease.
On the contrary, the more energy entered the deeper parts of his body, the greater the pressure on his bones and muscles became.
Lian had to reduce his energy absorption several times to give his body time to adapt.
Even so, he did not leave the river.
He had one month, and he had no intention of wasting even a single day.
At last, his breathing became calmer.
Mana flowed through his body at a steady rhythm, and the energy in the blood slowly entered the deepest parts of his physical structure, drop by drop.
Farther away, Seris was also sitting motionless.
Both of them trained in silence, while outside this secret hall, the world continued to move forward.
One month passed.
While the two of them were refining their bodies and souls deep inside the Pendragon Palace, the events in Verendal had consequences far greater than most people could imagine.
In the first few days after the ceremony, the Federation, together with representatives of the Six Great Families and the Twelve Ancient Guilds, released an official report about the crisis.

According to this report, a series of planned attacks had taken place during the Pendragon ceremony, and their source had been traced to an infiltrating structure belonging to the natives of the Heavenly Realm.
The authorities announced that the threat had been identified and neutralized, and that the investigation into all related parties was still ongoing.
But this was only part of the truth, and they tried to completely hide how the intruder had entered their world.
Of course, hiding everything that had happened that day was impossible.
Thousands of people had seen the defensive dome of Verendal shaking under the pressure of a battle between two Celestials, and some of them had even recorded images of the city’s sky.

However, in the official reports, those clashes were described as a security dispute during the investigation, a dispute that had ended after new evidence was discovered, without widespread casualties or the start of a war between the major powers.
For ordinary people, the incident was something like a major security crisis that had been brought under control before it could turn into a disaster.
But among those at the highest levels of power, there was a much deeper concern.
One of the natives of the Heavenly Realm had managed to operate on Earth for an unknown period of time, without the humans’ most powerful security systems noticing their presence.
And this was not something that could be easily ignored.

chapters.title: Chapter 585: World Affairs
paragraphs: During the first week, new security orders were issued.
Treasures brought in from the Heavenly Realm that could store information or reflect mana were reviewed again.
Several ancient artifacts were temporarily removed from important facilities, and Federation experts were ordered to review their methods for detecting inactive structures.
The Thousand-Faced Mirror also remained under a joint investigation.

The Primal Firmament was not willing to easily allow other powers unlimited access to one of its most valuable treasures, but after the events in Verendal, it was no longer possible to completely refuse the security inspections.
Especially since Lian’s theory had still not been disproven.
If an unknown structure had really remained hidden inside that mirror for fifteen years, similar objects might also exist among other treasures.
However, the investigations did not produce results quickly.
The main structure of the Silver Corruption Seed was extremely complex, and even the leading experts still could not explain all the methods used in it.
But at the same time, another decision was also put into action.
A decision that would push the relationship between humans and the Silver Elves into a more dangerous stage.
In the Heavenly Realm, forces stationed there by the Six Great Families, the Twelve Ancient Guilds, and the Federation began several joint operations against facilities connected to the Silver Elves.
The official goal was to identify and destroy facilities that might have played a role in creating the Silver Corruption Seed or carrying out the infiltration operation.
The human commanders expected to launch quick attacks, destroy several important facilities, and send a serious warning to the other side by causing limited but significant damage.
But reality was different.
The Silver Elves were prepared.
In one border region, the human forces encountered several layers of defensive formations before they could even reach their first target.
An attack that was supposed to end quickly continued for hours.
Every time one of the defensive formations was broken, part of the energy from the human attacks was reflected in another direction, forcing the attacking forces to change their own formations.
On another front, the forces of an Ancient Guild managed to destroy two military facilities, but they encountered a counterattack from the Elves while retreating.
Reports stated that a considerable number of forces on both sides had been killed.
In some areas, the land around the border bases had been so badly damaged after several days of fighting that even using ordinary communication formations had become difficult.
An operation that was supposed to be a short warning had turned into bloody battles in several places.
The situation remained unstable at the end of the month.
The humans had managed to destroy several military facilities and supply routes, but the Silver Elves had also shown that they were extremely dangerous opponents in their own territory.
Neither side had achieved a decisive victory.
As a result, the joint human councils decided to consider any expansion of the operations more carefully and keep the forces stationed in the Heavenly Realm ready to deal with possible attacks.
The issue was no longer just about punishing those responsible for an infiltration operation, and a new concern had emerged.
If the Silver Elves had already been prepared for conflicts like this, was the incident in Verendal only one part of a much larger plan?
No one had a definite answer.
But among all the news about battles and political decisions, two names were also being heard more often than before among the world’s powerful circles.
Lian Vorhelm.
And Seris Pendragon.
Seris’s name had already been known as one of the most talented young members of the Six Great Families, but her position had now changed.

She had officially become the heir of the Pendragon Family, received an Ancestral Dragon Mark, and had even been personally praised by Kairos during a ceremony that had been accompanied by a major security crisis.
For many families, these facts alone were enough to place Seris at the top of the list of the most important figures of the new generation.
But Lian’s situation was even stranger.
A young man from the Vorhelm Family who was still at the First Evolution had managed to obtain a Pendragon Ancestral Mark.
It was a Mark that even most members of the Pendragon Family itself would never have the chance to receive, and that was not the only issue.
Kairos, one of the world’s Celestials and the leader of the Primal Firmament, had publicly thanked him and invited him to join the strongest Ancient Guild in the world.
On the other hand, Rhaenar Pendragon had also openly supported him and allowed him to use one of his family’s most valuable training resources.
In some noble circles, this had become a serious topic of discussion.
Two powerful Celestials had shown interest in a young Vorhelm, and for someone of Lian’s current age and position, such an event was far from ordinary.
There were even rumors about a close relationship between Lian and the new Pendragon heir.
Some saw this closeness as an opportunity to reduce the rivalry between the two families, while others believed such a relationship could make their old conflicts even worse.
But despite all these rumors, ordinary people still knew nothing about the most important event that had taken place deep beneath Verendal.
No one outside the small circle of people who knew the truth was aware that these two young people had fought against a living Demon.
And they were the ones who had stopped it from being released.
Among all the families following this news, the Vorhelm Family held a special position.
A few days after the end of the Pendragon ceremony, Cassius returned to the family’s main residence.
Unlike his usual trips, this time his report was not limited to the results of the ceremony and his political meetings, he had to explain events that could affect the future of the family.
Several elders and influential members of the family had gathered in the Vorhelm inner council hall.
Cassius stood before them, and when his report reached the part about Lian receiving an Ancestral Mark, several people fell silent for a moment.
"You mean an Ancestral Dragon Mark?" one of the elders asked in disbelief.
Cassius nodded.
"Yes."
The man leaned back in his chair.
"A Vorhelm received a Pendragon Ancestral Mark?"
"Rhaenar personally confirmed it, there is no doubt about the Mark’s authenticity."
Whispers spread among those present.
But when Cassius mentioned Kairos’s invitation, their reactions became more serious.
One of the elders placed his hand on the table.
"Then we need to bring him back as soon as possible."
Several people looked at him.
The man continued.
"If the Primal Firmament really intends to recruit him, we can’t just sit here and do nothing. No matter what problems Lian has with the family, he’s still a Vorhelm."
Another elder agreed with him.
"We can offer him new conditions. Training resources, an official position, and even independent authority, we must not allow such a talent to slip away so easily."
But opposition soon began as well.
"Bringing him back won’t be that simple."
The voice of another council member caused several people to fall silent.
He looked at Cassius.
"Do you really think a young man who now has Rhaenar Pendragon’s support and is being pursued by Celestial Kairos will follow the family’s orders like before after he returns?"

chapters.title: Chapter 586: The Vorhelms Have a Problem
paragraphs: "Do you really think that a young man who now has the support of Rhaenar Pendragon, and whom Celestial Kairos is also trying to recruit, will follow the family’s orders like before after he returns?"
The first man frowned.
"Are you saying he shouldn’t return?"
"I’m saying we need to understand who we’re bringing back, Lian is no longer the same young man we could simply set aside and expect to leave without complaining."
Cassius had listened in silence the entire time, and the discussion taking place in front of him was exactly what he had expected.
Some wanted Lian to return because they now understood his value, while others were afraid of his return for the very same reason.
The young man who had once been removed from the power struggle because of his weakness and lack of talent could now change the entire situation simply by being there.
"If he returns, the succession issue will also become more complicated." One of the elders spoke in a lower voice.
This made several people exchange meaningful looks.
Cassius finally joined the discussion.
"For now, he has made no request to return."
Everyone looked at him.
"And you’d better not forget this, Lian is no longer a child whose future others can decide without him being present."
Then, without waiting for a reply, he continued his report, but when the meeting ended, it was clear that the Vorhelm Family was now more divided than before.
And neither side intended to back down.
In the same residence, Celestia, the second wife of the Vorhelm patriarch, was sitting in her private room.
Several reports were placed on the table, and she had been looking at one of them for a long time.
Lian Vorhelm’s name could be seen at the top of the page.
Ancestral Mark.
An invitation from Celestial Kairos.
Support from Rhaenar Pendragon.
Every time her eyes fell on one of these phrases, her fingers tightened around the paper a little more.
Finally, she placed the report on the table with a dry sound.
"Impossible."
She stood up.
She walked a few steps around the room, but the calm did not return to her face, she knew very well what position Lian had held in the past.
A boy who had been removed from the family’s main structure.
A young man who was not expected to have any major influence on the Vorhelm Family’s internal struggles anymore.
But now?
That same young man had reached a point where two Celestials were personally showing interest in him.
And this was not good news.
Not at all.
Celestia placed her hand firmly on the edge of the table.
"How could that boy have reached this point?!"
For a few moments, her breathing became heavier.
But what worried her more than all of Lian’s achievements was not just his newfound power.
His return could give an opportunity to those who had been waiting for a change in the balance of power for a long time.
She had to do something, she had to make sure that one of her own children became the heir, no matter what it took.
Her thoughts turned to a specific person.
That woman.
The first wife of the Vorhelm patriarch.
Celestia looked toward the window.
That woman shouldn’t remain silent in this situation either, right? She would definitely make a move as well, but Celestia couldn’t trust her either.
In the end, both of them wanted their own child to become the heir.
She picked up the report again, and this time, her eyes stopped at the section about the patriarch’s return.
In about one month.
There wasn’t much time left, and when he returned, the struggles that had been taking place behind closed doors until then would probably become more open.
Celestia slowly placed the paper on the table, anger was still visible on her face, but now there was worry as well.
Lian was no longer a problem that could be solved by ignoring him.
A few days later, the Vorhelm Family released an official statement.
The family patriarch was expected to return soon, and preparations for the final stage of selecting his successor would begin after his return.
However, the more important part of the statement was the date of the ceremony, the official Vorhelm heir selection ceremony would be held eight months later.
The news quickly spread among the Six Great Families and the Twelve Ancient Guilds, and for many observers, the Vorhelm succession was especially important.
The family had stood among the world’s major powers for years, and its unique fighting style was widely known, now it was going to entrust its future to a member of the younger generation.
But now, Lian’s name was being mentioned again among the possible candidates, even though he had not officially returned to the family’s main structure.
Some believed that after returning, the patriarch would not be able to ignore the achievements of such a young man.
Others said that Lian’s close ties with the Pendragons might prevent his return, while some preferred to make no predictions before hearing the patriarch’s decision.
In any case, one thing was clear.
The Vorhelm succession struggle would no longer be the same as before.
At the same time, in another world, in an unknown part of the Ruined Realm, the sound of another heavy impact echoed between the walls of an underground valley.
KRAAAK!
Part of the rock collapsed.
A huge creature emerged from the dust and landed on the ground with heavy steps, many wounds could be seen on its body, and dark blood flowed down between the thick plates covering its skin.
But it was still alive.
The monster raised its head and let out a rough roar.
Several dozen meters away, Roderick stood on a broken rock.
His clothes were torn, and dried blood covered parts of his arms and shoulders, his breathing was heavy, but his eyes remained fixed on the last enemy.
Behind the monster, the bodies of dozens of other creatures lay on the ground, some of them were so large that their bodies blocked a large part of the valley’s paths.
Others lay among the broken rocks and the holes created during the battles.
This area was not recorded on the usual maps of the Ruined Realm.
Roderick had discovered its hidden entrance a long time ago while exploring one of the remote areas.
Inside, there was a series of natural passages and connected habitats where many powerful monsters lived.
For most Awakened, entering such an area without a backup force would be considered a foolish decision.
But Roderick had seen another opportunity here.
Experience, resources, and most importantly, levels.
He had stayed in this hunting ground for a long time and hunted the monsters one after another.
Sometimes he had won, sometimes he had been forced to retreat, and several times he had suffered wounds that would probably have stopped him from fighting if they had been even slightly more serious.
But every time, he had returned, and now only one monster remained
The huge creature lowered its head.
Roderick noticed the change in the pressure on its feet, its next attack would come straight at him.
He waited.
The monster rushed forward at a speed far greater than its size suggested, the stones beneath its feet shattered, and its huge claw moved toward Roderick.
At the last moment, Roderick moved out of its path, and the claw struck the rock behind him.
BOOOOM!
The rock split along the point of impact, but the monster did not get the chance to complete its second attack, as the human had already passed beside its body.
His fists struck the old wound on the creature’s side, and dark blood splashed onto the ground.
The monster twisted its body with a painful roar, Roderick moved back, but this time, he did not put too much distance between them.
His eyes remained fixed on the monster’s foot movements.
During their previous battle, he had noticed that whenever the creature turned to the left, it placed more weight on its rear leg.
And that same leg was already injured.
When the monster attacked again, Roderick did not retreat, instead, he cut across its path and delivered a heavy strike to its injured leg.
A dry cracking sound rang out.
The creature lost its balance, and its huge body fell onto its side, raising a large cloud of dust from the ground.

Roderick forcefully breathed out, but he did not hesitate, before the monster could get back up, he rushed forward through the dust and delivered his final punch to the spot he had spent the entire battle trying to expose.
KRAAAK!
The monster’s body tightened for a moment, then became motionless.
Roderick stood there for several seconds, his heavy breathing could be heard in the silence of the valley.
Finally, he took a step back and kept his eyes on the last monster’s body.
It was over, there were no living creatures left in the hunting ground, he had hunted every single one of them.
At that moment, a system window appeared in front of him.
[ Level Increased ]
[ Current Level: 40 ]

chapters.title: Chapter 587: A New Body, A New Soul
paragraphs: Roderick stared at the number forty for a few seconds, then a slow smile appeared on his face.
Finally.
All the wounds, all the days he had been forced to remain in this dark area, all the battles where he had sometimes not even had time to rest between them.
They had finally paid off.
Level forty.
Now he could prepare for his second evolution.
He looked at the scattered bodies throughout the valley, and for a moment, another image appeared in his mind.
Lian Vorhelm.
That bastard’s face, his calm behavior, and the humiliation Roderick still had not been able to forget.
"You think everything is over, Lian?"
His voice echoed between the stone walls.
There was no one there to answer him, but he was not waiting for an answer either.
"Next time, I’ll return every bit of humiliation a thousand times over!"
His gaze turned toward the distant entrance of the hunting ground, there was still work left to do.
The second evolution.
And then, his return to the academy.
The time to go to the Land of First Dawn was slowly approaching.
That was where he intended to make up for the humiliation of the past by defeating Lian.
Roderick’s smile disappeared, then, without looking at the bodies behind him again, he walked toward the exit.
This time, he had no intention of losing.
During those same days, deep inside the Pendragon Family’s private territory, the Dragon Blood River continued to flow at a steady pace.
One month had passed since Lian and Seris entered it, and during this time, the pressure of the dragon blood had never left their bodies.
The first few days had been very difficult, even Lian, despite his powerful body structure, had been forced to reduce the speed of energy absorption several times.
The dragon blood did not put pressure only on the surface of the skin or the muscles.
Its dense energy entered the deeper layers of the body and even affected parts whose existence Lian had barely noticed before.
Bones.
Connective tissues.
Organs.
The mana channels where mana flowed through his body.
Each of them had undergone constant refinement.
Sometimes, the pressure increased so much that all the muscles in his body tightened for several minutes.
At other times, he felt heavy heat passing through the inside of his bones.
But this condition did not remain the same, as the days passed, his body began to adapt.
The flow of energy from the blood, which had faced a great deal of resistance at first, gradually began to reach the deeper parts of his body.
Tissues that had been damaged during previous battles healed during periods of rest and refinement.
His muscle structure became denser, his bones developed different qualities, and even the flow of mana through his body slowly became more orderly.
Of course, none of these changes meant a direct increase in his stats, his total stats were still limited by the cap of the First Evolution.
But the quality of the body in which those stats worked was no longer the same as before, and this was the main reason he had entered the river.
Seris had also made significant progress in another part of the river.
The Ancestral Mark on her hand showed a high level of compatibility with the energy in the dragon blood.
On some days, when the flow of blood reached its peak, a faint image of an Ancestral Dragon appeared behind her.
But that manifestation was not meant for combat, it was simply a natural response of her Blessing to the dragon energy present in the blood.
She tried to maintain this harmony while also allowing the energy to reach the deeper parts of her body and soul.

At first, the pressure on her soul was more difficult to endure than the physical pressure, and several times, she had been forced to open her eyes and reduce the speed of energy absorption for a while.
But like Lian, she was not willing to waste her one-month opportunity so easily, and each day, she became more adapted to the river’s flow than the day before.
By the final weeks, both of them could remain in the state of refinement for longer periods without interruption.
However, Lian’s situation was different in some ways, the End Core continued to react to the energy in the blood.
This reaction had been weak during the first few days.
But as time passed, the reaction grew stronger and continued until the core itself became stronger.
As a result, the amount of End energy it could store increased, and the amount of End energy the core could produce also increased by a significant amount.
His End Core was now stronger than his Eclipse Core.
During this time, since he also had some extra time, he had tried to examine the Ruined Heart.
The same broken heart that still hid many secrets within itself.
Lian had tried to examine its unusual reactions several times during this month, but he had not discovered anything that could explain its true nature.
This heart suddenly made sounds from time to time, whenever it wanted, and sometimes doing so could be dangerous, especially in front of a creature like the Demon of End.
But he could not find anything and could only make a few guesses about it, including the possibility that it was the same dead sixth Calamity that Ezrak had mentioned.
But he had no evidence to confirm this, and in the end, it was only a guess.
In the end, he had decided to focus all his attention on the main goal of his training.
Refining his body and refining his soul.
On the final day of the month, Lian sat in a deeper part of the river, the dark red blood had risen to just below his shoulders, and its slow current passed beside his body.
But unlike the first day, not the slightest movement could be seen in the muscles of his face.
His breathing was calm and steady.
The energy in the blood entered his body through his skin and moved along the paths that had been refined many times over the past few weeks.
Inside his bones, the last traces of pressure slowly faded.
The structure of his muscles and organs had now reached a level of stability that even he had not expected at the beginning of this training.
But what was happening at that moment was no longer limited to his body.
Deep inside his soul, nine streams of energy were moving, they were somewhat similar to dragon energy, and during the first few days, these streams had been nothing more than weak strands.
As time passed, the energy in the blood had entered the deeper parts of his soul and gradually compressed them.
Now, each stream had a clear structure, they were not exactly like real dragons but were more like manifestations of energy that had taken the shape of huge dragons.
They moved one after another around the central part of his soul.
None of them was a living creature, they had no independent awareness or separate will, they were part of Lian’s soul structure.
He remained in a state of deep focus, unaware of the outside world.
The only things he could feel were the constant flow of energy from the blood and the slow changes in the structure of his own existence.
The final stage of refinement was also continuing inside his body.
The dragon energy entered layers that had barely reacted even after a month of training.
For a few moments, immense pressure spread throughout his entire body.
Lian’s fingers tightened slightly, but he did not move, he allowed the flow to continue, and the pressure increased.
His bones, muscles, mana channels, and finally, the entire structure of his body responded to it at the same time.
Deep inside his soul, the nine dragon-like streams also began to move in harmony, their rotation slowed, the distances between them changed, and after some time, they all reached a certain balance.
At that moment, the flow of blood around his body slowed for a few seconds.
The heavy pressure that had weighed on his entire existence for a month gradually decreased.
His breathing became deeper, his fingers moved slightly, and finally... Lian opened his eyes.
At that moment, two blue windows appeared in front of him.
[ You have successfully formed an Indestructible Body ]
[ You have successfully formed a Golden Soul of Nine Dragons ]

chapters.title: Chapter 588: A New Body, A New Soul II
paragraphs: Lian slowly opened his eyes.
The red light of the underground hall fell on his face, and for a few seconds, his gaze remained fixed on the calm flow of the river.
He felt that his body had become unusually light, but this lightness did not come from losing weight or becoming weaker.
On the contrary, when he clenched his fingers, the power flowing through the muscles of his forearm was far greater than he had expected.
Even without activating any skills, he could feel the difference, however, what caught his attention the most were the two blue windows in front of him.
[ You have successfully formed an Indestructible Body ]
[ You have successfully formed a Soul of Nine Dragons ]
He looked at the messages for a few seconds.
"Well..."
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"Finally, I can see the results."
He had expected the blood of a creature at the Demon rank to have a significant effect on his body.
Even before entering the river, he had known that refining his body and soul could help him overcome limits that could not be removed through stats alone.
But two separate achievements? And with names like these?
The young Vorhelm selected the first window, and more information appeared in front of him.
[ Indestructible Body ]
[ Completion: 20%. ]
[ Effects: Physical Strength Increased by 250%, Physical Defense Increased by 250%, Damage Taken from Physical Attacks Reduced by 25%, Body’s Natural Healing Speed Increased by up to 250% ]
[ All internal organs, muscles, bones, and physical pathways have undergone structural refinement ]
[ The resistance of vital organs, natural tissue recovery, physical endurance, and stability of mana channels have greatly increased ]
[ The body’s structure is moving toward the physical quality of superior races, including True Dragons. ]
[ Every 20% increase in completion multiplies all effects of the Indestructible Body by ten ]
[ At full completion, the owner’s body will become completely immune to all known and unknown forms of physical damage ]
[ When the Indestructible Body reaches 100% completion, as long as even a single cell or even a single atom remains, the body can quickly rebuild itself ]
[ Note: Final immunity does not include conceptual powers, non-physical attacks, or forces that exist beyond the level of the body’s structure ]
Lian remained motionless for a few moments, then looked at the first number again.
Twenty percent?
Did that mean everything he had endured over the past month had only completed one-fifth of this process?

He had expected refining the dragon blood to increase the strength of his bones and the resistance of his skin and muscles, perhaps even raising his body’s quality beyond that of most Awakened in the First Evolution.
But the system’s explanation showed something much greater, the Indestructible Body was not simply a temporary enhancement.
His entire physical structure had changed, and it could even reach a point where it fully achieved an indestructible state.
He turned his attention toward his own body.
The flow of blood through his veins, the contraction of his muscles, and even the movement of mana along his internal pathways were clearer to him than before.
His bones could withstand greater pressure, his muscles could produce more force, and his internal organs were no longer as vulnerable to heavy blows as they had been before.
Even his body’s natural recovery had improved, although this did not mean that healing was free or unlimited, his body still needed energy to repair damaged tissues.
But his natural healing speed had increased by up to 250%.
His gaze moved to the description of physical damage reduction.
Twenty-five percent.
This effect was different from a direct increase in defense.
Even if an attack passed through his body’s natural defenses, part of its physical damage would still be reduced by his new body structure.
And when he considered this together with the 250% increase in defense...
His smile grew slightly wider.
He already had the World-Devourer Bastion, the Molten Bastion Body, and the Black Wing Armor.
Now, even his body without armor was much more durable, of course, this did not mean he could stand against every attack.
Lian still clearly remembered how the Essence of the End had destroyed part of his defensive structure without needing to overcome his usual resistance.
Powers of that kind would not become harmless just because he had a more durable body.
But against physical attacks? This was an incredible achievement.
However, the most important sentence in the description was still waiting for him.
Every 20% increase in completion multiplied the power of the Indestructible Body by ten.
If the description was correct, this structure had already reached such power at its current stage.
At forty percent, the power of the structure itself would increase tenfold.
Sixty percent? Another tenfold increase, and the same process would continue until it reached one hundred percent.
Lian slowly breathed out.
If he could really complete such a structure, his body would no longer be comparable to that of an ordinary human, even the word indestructible would no longer seem like much of an exaggeration.
"Of course, first I need to figure out how I’m supposed to complete the remaining eighty percent."
He checked the information once more, but the current description did not provide exact details about the resources required for the later stages.
It seemed the system had only identified the results of the refinement.
He closed the window.
Then he turned his attention to his second achievement.
[ Golden Nine-Dragon Soul ]
[ Completion: 20%. ]
[ Effects: Soul Attack Power Increased by 250%, Soul Defense Increased by 250%, Soul’s Natural Recovery Speed Against Soul Attacks Increased by 250% ]
[ The Nine Dragon Guardians are guardians responsible for protecting the main structure of the soul ]
[ All energy flows entering and leaving the soul are examined by the guardians, and when necessary, their paths are adjusted, guided, or redirected ]
[ Offensive Ability: The Nine Dragons can carry out a devastating and deadly soul attack against a target at their master’s command ]
[ Attack Power and Effectiveness depend on the master’s soul power, the target’s soul resistance, and the difference in rank between both sides ]
[ Every 20% increase in completion multiplies the power of the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul by ten ]
[ Final Evolution: Soul of the Nine Dragon Emperors ]
[ At full completion, the owner’s soul will gain near-absolute immunity to soul damage and soul attacks ]
[ The soul will become immortal, and nothing will be able to destroy your soul ]
This time, Lian looked at the window for a longer time, the 250% increase in both soul attack power and defense was already a major achievement.
But Nine Dragon Guardians? And they could examine the energy flows entering and leaving his soul?
This part seemed much more interesting.
He closed his eyes, separated his awareness from his surroundings, and directed it toward the depths of his own soul.
The sound of the river slowly faded away, and the pressure of the hot air in the hall also disappeared from his senses, and for a moment, everything was dark.
Then golden points appeared in the distance.
At first, there were only a few of them, but gradually, their numbers increased and filled the inner space of his soul with a soft light.
He raised his gaze.

At that moment, the sound of a deep roar echoed through the space, it was not like the roar of the Demon of End, but this one had a different feeling, heavy and powerful, yet without the familiar violence and hatred.
A huge shadow passed through the golden lights.
A large dragon covered in golden scales of light appeared before him.
Its body was long and powerful, and every time it moved, lines of soul energy remained along its flight path.
But before he could examine its structure carefully, another dragon emerged from the golden light.
Then a third, a fourth, and finally, nine huge golden dragons flew around the main structure of Lian’s soul.
For a few seconds, he simply watched the sight.

The dragons moved along different paths, but there were no collisions or disturbances between them. Each one covered a part of the space around his soul, and their movements were coordinated with those of the other eight dragons.
Golden light separated from their scales and then returned to the main structure of his soul.
Lian carefully examined one of them, but he could not sense any independent awareness, there was no separate will, nor was there a connection like the Hive Link.
These dragons were not living creatures, it could be said that they had now become part of his own soul.

chapters.title: Chapter 589: A New Body, A New Soul III
paragraphs: To test it, he sent a very small flow of ordinary, pure energy toward his soul.
Almost at the same moment, the dragon closest to its path changed direction. Golden light separated from its body and surrounded the flow.
Lian realized that the dragon was checking the quality of the energy and the path it followed, and more importantly, whether the energy posed any danger to his soul.
Then, since it found no problems, it allowed the energy to continue without making any changes.
He performed another test, this time deliberately moving the flow away from its normal path and sending it as an attack.
The two nearest dragons reacted. They opened their mouths at the same time, forming something like balls of fire, and fired them at the energy, destroying it in an instant.
Everything had happened without him giving them any direct commands.
Lian smiled. He could understand how important this ability was.
Soul attacks were often very different from physical attacks. Some of them could directly target the structure of a soul without damaging the skin or bones.
And when fighting enemies with powerful souls, even a fraction of a second’s delay in detecting an incoming attack could be dangerous.
But now? Nine guardians were always present around his soul.
Of course, it was still unclear how well they could resist a real soul attack from a much more powerful being.
But this was only their defensive ability.
He moved his gaze across the nine dragons.
According to the system’s explanation, if he gave the command, all of them could launch a coordinated soul attack.
A direct attack on an enemy’s soul.
This essentially worked like a powerful soul attack skill.
Lian wanted to test its power, but he quickly gave up on the idea. To use such an attack in a real situation, he needed a suitable target.
He looked at the dragons again.
For a moment, he imagined what would happen if these nine guardians reached their final stage in the future.
The Soul of the Nine Dragon Emperors.
Even its name sounded much more impressive than its current form. If it could have such an effect on his soul at only twenty percent completion, how powerful would it become at one hundred percent?
He could not find an exact answer, but he had reached one conclusion.
These two achievements had far more room for growth than his current rank could make use of.

Considering the resources needed for completion and the tenfold increase in power at each stage, it was unlikely that he would be able to unlock their full potential during his first or even second evolution.
Perhaps their true value would only become clear when he reached the Celestial rank himself.

At that stage, the amount of power his body and soul could withstand would become much more important. He even had a feeling that once he became a Celestial, these two achievements might help him become the strongest Celestial in the world.
Then he withdrew his consciousness from the inner space of his soul.
When he opened his eyes again, the Dragon Blood River was still flowing around his body.
But its pressure was no longer the same as before.
Lian raised his right hand and looked at the muscles of his forearm. There were no exaggerated changes in his body’s appearance.
His skin was still the same as before, and his body did not look unusual from the outside either, but he could feel his body’s newly gained strength.
And this was only twenty percent completion.
While he was thinking about this, the flow of mana in another part of the river changed.
He turned his head.
Several dozen meters away, Seris had also opened her eyes.
Her wet silver hair fell over her shoulders, and the Ancestral Mark on the back of her right hand was glowing with a soft light.
But what caught Lian’s attention was the quality of the mana around her.
One month ago, Seris had made incredible progress after her first evolution.
Now? Her mana was much denser, and more importantly, he could feel that the energy inside her body was moving in a different and more organized way.
She stared at a window in front of her for several seconds. It was clear that she had also gained something.
Then she looked away from the window and raised her right hand. At first, only the Ancestral Mark on her skin was glowing.
But a few moments later, very thin lines of golden and silver light appeared beneath the skin of her wrist.
The lines moved along her forearm and then reached her shoulder. Within a few seconds, other parts of her body began to respond to the same light.
Deep within Seris’s soul, structures connected to those same lines began to glow. For a moment, a faint image of the Ancestral Dragon appeared behind her.
But unlike the offensive and defensive blessings of her Mark, this time the dragon did not launch any attacks. It was only there for a brief moment before disappearing.
The young Pendragon looked at the glowing lines on her hand for several seconds, then reduced the flow of her mana. The lights slowly disappeared.
She still did not know all the abilities of [Dragon Veins].
But she could feel that this achievement was connected to her body and soul on a much deeper level than an ordinary skill.
And that would be very valuable for her future path.
Some time later, Lian stood up. Dark red blood slowly ran down his clothes and flowed back into the river.
He climbed onto the stone platform and ran his hand through his wet hair.
One month of continuous training had finally come to an end.
He felt that if he had to sit there for a few more days, even his [Indestructible Body] would not save him from getting bored.
At that moment, he heard footsteps coming from the other side of the platform.
Seris had also climbed out of the river.
He raised his head.

The girl pushed her wet silver hair away from the side of her face. Several strands of hair stuck to her neck and shoulders, and her wet clothes clearly showed the graceful lines of her well-shaped figure.
The red light of the river fell on her fair skin, and small drops of water fell from the ends of her hair. Since her clothes were wet, the shape of her beautiful figure was clearly visible.
Lian kept his eyes on her for a moment.
Seris noticed.
"What?"
He gave her a small smile.
"Nothing. Looks like that month of training did you a lot of good."
She looked at him, then her eyes rested on Lian’s upper body for a fraction of a second.
His black clothes were also sticking to his shoulders and chest, showing the muscles that had become more defined and dense after a month of refinement.
Her gaze moved slightly lower, but she quickly looked back at his face. A very faint red color appeared on her cheeks, so slight that even Lian did not notice it.
"You too."
"Me too, what?
She moved her wet hair away from the front of her shoulder.
"You’ve become stronger."
Lian laughed.
"Yeah, but I think we should find some dry clothes."
She glanced at her own clothes, and that was when she realized that she had not even noticed how completely wet they were or how clearly they showed her figure.
The red color appeared on her cheeks again. Even for someone with her personality, this was the first time she had been in such a situation in front of a man.
She glanced at Lian from the corner of her eyes... Well, since it was him, was it really a problem...?
If it had been any other man, she would have definitely summoned her sword by now and made sure he could not see her like this.
But she did not know why... She felt that since it was Lian, it was not a problem...
However, she suddenly shook her head and pushed all those thoughts out of her mind. What kind of thoughts were these?
"Let’s go." She did not want to stay in those wet clothes for even another moment.
When they passed through the gate, several Pendragon servants were waiting for them.
One of the women bowed as soon as she saw Seris.
"Lady Seris, Sir Lian, the Patriarch has requested that you visit him after your training is complete."
Lian looked at his own wet clothes, then at Seris.
"I think we should change our clothes first."
The servant replied,
"The baths and fresh clothes are ready. You may use them whenever you wish."
"Great." He smiled.
The two separated at the intersection of the hallway.
Lian headed toward the guest quarters, while Seris made her way to her private rooms. After a month of refinement, a warm bath and dry clothes were pleasant even for them.
About an hour later, they arrived almost at the same time in front of Rhaenar Pendragon’s private office.
The young Vorhelm was wearing fresh black clothes, and his hair was neat again. She was also wearing a white and dark-colored outfit.
Then the office door opened, and they both entered.
Rhaenar Pendragon was sitting behind his desk.

Several reports were placed on the desk, and the evening sunlight came through the large window behind him. Unlike during the crisis at the ceremony, there were no guards constantly coming and going, and no elders from the family were gathered outside his office.
When the two entered, the Patriarch raised his head from the report. He looked at his daughter first, then his gaze settled on Lian.
He said nothing for several seconds.
Lian felt that the man’s gaze was not limited to his face or clothes.
Even though Rhaenar had not released any pressure, he seemed able to recognize the changes in the quality of their bodies and souls.

Of course, the young Vorhelm saw no sign that the Patriarch had discovered the nature of his cores or his Ruined Heart. What was clear was that the quality of their very existence had changed compared to one month ago.
The man finally smiled.
"Congratulations."

chapters.title: Chapter 590: Dragon Body
paragraphs: "Apparently, you made good use of the river."
"Thank you, Father." Seris lowered her head slightly.
Rhaenar turned his gaze to Lian.
"Well, how did a month of training feel?"
Lian thought for a moment, then gave a slight shrug.
"It was boring, but the results weren’t bad."

"You spent an entire month in one of my family’s most valuable training resources, and the best thing you can say about it is that the results weren’t bad?"
He then leaned back in his chair and turned his gaze to his daughter.
"And you?"
"I’m satisfied." Seris replied.
Rhaenar raised an eyebrow.
"That’s all?"
"Yes."
"You spent thirty days training in Dragon Blood, and your father gave you access to one of the family’s most valuable rewards, yet all I hear is that you’re satisfied?"
She looked at him for a few seconds.
"I’m very satisfied."
Lian couldn’t hide his laughter.
Rhaenar let out a dramatic sigh.

For a while, their conversation continued with simple topics. He asked about the pressure of the river and how much his daughter could withstand, and Seris explained that during the first few weeks, she had been forced to reduce the speed at which she absorbed energy several times.
When Lian mentioned that his body had also reacted strongly to the blood during the first few days, Rhaenar nodded with satisfaction.
"Good. That means you allowed your bodies to adapt to the energy instead of destroying yourselves by rushing."
The young Vorhelm looked at him.
"I don’t think anyone wants their body to fall apart in the middle of training."
"Believe me, some of the young members of my family are willing to take that risk just to become stronger faster." Rhaenar gave Seris a meaningful look.
But the girl seemed indifferent.
Lian gave a faint smile. Apparently, the Patriarch had a lot of experience dealing with children who were too obsessed with power.
However, after a few minutes, Rhaenar closed the report on his desk. His expression became a little more serious.
"Now that both of you have Ancestral Marks, there’s something you should know before you leave."
"Do you know why none of the Pendragon Enlightened have Dragon Marks?"
The Enlightened were Awakened who had completed three evolutions.
He asked the question calmly.
Lian glanced at the Mark on the back of his hand for a moment.
As far as he knew, the Pendragons could use the Mark’s blessing until their third evolution, then consume it to form a Dragon Body.
But the details of this process were still not completely clear to him.
"To form a Dragon Body." Seris answered.
"Correct. But that’s only the visible result."
He raised his right hand. A very weak flow of mana moved across his fingers, then disappeared without him activating any special skill.

"Most people think a Dragon Body means a stronger body, stronger muscles, or better compatibility with different types of energy, these are all part of the result, but they’re not the most important part."
His gaze settled on Lian’s Mark.
"The Mark gives you a blessing that you can use as long as the structure of the Mark exists, but that power hasn’t fully become a part of your own existence yet."
Lian remembered the two black wings behind him. Until now, whenever he had activated the blessing, his Ancestral Mark had responded to it.
But in the end, those wings did not truly belong to him.
Rhaenar continued,
"When you form a Dragon Body, you’re not simply creating a new body, you have to connect the nature of the blessing to your body and soul, so that it no longer depends on the existence of the Mark."
"Does that mean the blessing becomes an innate ability?" The young Vorhelm thought for a moment before asking.
"Exactly."
The Patriarch smiled.
"The wings you’ve gained will no longer be something you simply summon from your Mark, they’ll become part of your own structure, and after that, they’ll continue to grow along with you."
This answer was very interesting to Lian.
The Wings of God already allowed him to fly at an incredible speed, create armor, and release an extremely powerful tornado.

If he could turn such power into a true part of his own existence, its future would no longer depend entirely on the survival of the Mark, especially since he had to remember that these Marks could be destroyed.
Rhaenar looked at Seris.
"The same applies to your Ancestral Dragon manifestation. Once you properly form your Dragon Body, that manifestation will no longer be just a temporary blessing."
"But I doubt forming this [Dragon Body] will be easy." The young Vorhelm added.
"That’s right, and that brings us to the difficult part."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"I guess you’re not going to tell us to just sit around and wait until our third evolution."
Rhaenar laughed.
"No, unfortunately, I can’t make this one easy for you."
[Heavenly Dragon Marrow]
He stated the name with emphasis.
"You need this material to form a Dragon Body."
Lian repeated the name in his mind, Heavenly Dragon Marrow. He didn’t even know such a material existed.
The Patriarch explained,

"This material can be found in certain areas of the Heavenly Realm, places where the remains of powerful ancient dragons exist. Not all samples have the same quality or nature, and not every material is suitable for every Mark."
He then pointed at the Mark on Lian’s hand.

"For example, the structure of your wings is different from Seris’s dragon manifestation. If both of you use an unsuitable sample, you might not be able to fully stabilize your blessings inside your bodies.
"Doesn’t the Pendragon Family have a supply of it?" Lian asked after thinking for a moment.
Rhaenar smiled.
"Even if we did, I wouldn’t simply give it to you."
He looked at him and continued,

"Anyone who wants to form a Dragon Body must find suitable material for themselves in the Heavenly Realm. This isn’t just a family rule, searching for, choosing, and obtaining that material are all part of the preparation for the final process."
Seris nodded without objecting, and Lian also kept this information in mind.
Entering the Heavenly Realm was impossible before reaching level sixty.
On the other hand, this was only one of the reasons he now had for entering that world.
Training resources for the Indestructible Body, resources for the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul, and Heavenly Dragon Marrow.
And perhaps answers to some of the mysteries he still had about Demons and beings above them.
He gave a faint smile.
After finishing his explanation, Rhaenar turned his gaze to his daughter.

"By the way, I have another piece of news for you. Our forces found a hidden area near one of the bases in the Ruined Realm, and the investigation teams still haven’t been able to identify every part of it. Its structure is different from the surrounding areas."
"Does it have powerful monsters?" Seris asked.
Rhaenar looked at her for a moment, then laughed.
"Of course, we still don’t know what’s inside, and that’s one of the reasons we’ve restricted large-scale entry."
He then leaned forward slightly.
"Now that your refinement is complete, I think it’s time for you to return to the Ruined Realm. It might be a good idea for you to take a look at that area yourself."
The young Pendragon nodded without hesitation.
"Okay."
Her father smiled and looked at Lian.
"You can go with her if you want."
"I don’t think I can go with her. There’s somewhere I need to be." Lian answered without thinking. It was almost time for him to head to the Land of First Dawn.
Rhaenar looked at him for a few moments, then nodded. The young Vorhelm took the opportunity to change the subject.
"By the way, I wanted to ask about what happened during this past month."
"You mean the Silver Elves?"
"More than anything, yes, but I have other questions too."
The Patriarch nodded.
"I thought you’d ask about this."
His expression slowly became more serious.

"We decided to start with a few limited operations. The goal was to identify the facilities connected to the infiltration of Earth and make it clear to the Elves that such an act wouldn’t go unanswered."
"But apparently, the results weren’t exactly what you expected." Hearing his tone, Lian could figure out at least that much.
