chapters.title: Chapter 591: The Cost of Conquest
paragraphs: "But apparently, the results weren’t exactly what you expected."
Rhaenar nodded.
"The Elves were prepared."
He paused.

"In some areas, they had even changed their defensive positions before our forces arrived. Several attacks succeeded in destroying their target facilities, but some operations turned into long and costly battles."
"So they already knew where we would attack?" Lian narrowed his eyes slightly.
It wasn’t strange that the Elves knew they would be attacked. The Silver Elves had carried out a sabotage operation in their world, and it was obvious that they would face a response.
The interesting part was that they even knew where the targets would be.
But after thinking about it for a moment, perhaps predicting this wasn’t difficult for a race that had almost caused a world war in their world.
"It’s likely, but that doesn’t mean they knew every detail of our plans."
Rhaenar placed his hand on the desk.

"When a sabotage operation on Earth fails and evidence of those responsible is left behind, expecting a retaliatory attack isn’t difficult. Especially for a race that is highly skilled at analyzing information and mana structures."
This answer made sense.
Lian had also learned during his battle with the Silver Elf just how patient that creature was when it came to planning.
If they had really spent fifteen years preparing for the operation in Verendal, it was unlikely that they hadn’t considered the possibility of failure and a human response.
The Patriarch continued,

"The problem isn’t just a few military defeats. Some native governments near the Elves’ territory are also watching the situation now. If we expand our attacks without thinking carefully, we might turn several separate enemies into one large alliance."
The young Vorhelm thought about this. The Silver Elves were only one of the native races in the Heavenly Realm.
And humans were not the only military power in that world.
"So you don’t want to start an all-out war."
"Not until we’re sure who we’re dealing with."
Rhaenar glanced briefly at the window.

"Not all Silver Elves were necessarily involved in that operation. If we attack all their territories without identifying those truly responsible, we might create enemies for ourselves who had no interest in fighting Earth before."
Lian nodded. This part of the Patriarch’s decision was understandable. Punishing the group responsible was very different from starting a war against an entire race.
But in the Heavenly Realm, this difference could determine whether a military operation remained limited or turned into a war that lasted for years.
Rhaenar continued slowly,
"The Heavenly Realm isn’t what many young Awakened think it is."
"What do you mean?" The young Vorhelm asked quietly.
"Some people think it’s a world full of resources and monsters, where all you have to do is defeat stronger enemies and collect more resources as you go further."
He shook his head.
"But that world has governments and borders, and there are races with thousands of years of history. Some of them were already fighting each other long before humans entered that world."
He explained that, despite its name, the Heavenly Realm was not one unified land under a single government.
Different regions were controlled by races, native families, independent governments, and alliances whose relationships were always changing.
Some traded with humans, while others had agreements to share routes or resources.
But there were also groups that saw the human presence as nothing more than an occupation of their lands.
"Even the natives don’t all agree with each other. One government might allow us to pass through its territory, while its neighbor might consider the same action a betrayal of the native races."
Lian listened in silence. Rhaenar also mentioned the conflicts of interest among human forces.
The Twelve Ancient Guilds controlled a large part of the trade routes and access to important resources in the Heavenly Realm.
The Six Great Families also had their own bases, territories of influence, and independent forces.
The Federation tried to coordinate the security of certain routes and shared interests, but no power was willing to hand over all its authority to another.
"Taking over a region might take a few days, but holding it could require years of troops and resources."
"Because of attacks from the natives?"

"That’s not the only reason. You need supply routes. You need to collect resources, transport them, and protect them. If you build a base in the middle of enemy territory, all its supply routes can become targets."
He then gave a slight smile.
"And even if you solve all those problems, another guild might claim that a trade route in the region passes through territory under its control and demand a share of the profits."
Lian also gave a faint smile.
"So even after defeating your enemies, you still have to deal with other humans."
Rhaenar laughed.
"Usually, the second part causes more trouble."
This answer didn’t surprise Lian much. During the short time he had spent in Verendal, he had nearly witnessed a war between Earth’s greatest powers.
And all because of a few attacks with forged signatures.
If such conflicts already existed on Earth, it was natural that they would become even more complicated in the Heavenly Realm, where resources and territories were far more valuable.
But something still remained in his mind, something Rhaenar’s explanation had not fully clarified.
"One more question."
Rhaenar looked at him.
"Go ahead."
The young Vorhelm leaned forward slightly.
"Why are humans so determined to conquer the Heavenly Realm?"
Silence fell for a moment, but the Patriarch’s expression did not change.
"What do you mean?"
"I understand that there are many resources there, vast lands, ancient treasures, training materials, and anything else that can help humans become stronger."

"But even with all that, maintaining occupied regions costs a lot. If we were only after resources, trading or controlling a few important trade routes might be more profitable than fighting a war that could last for decades."
Rhaenar remained silent.
Lian continued,
"Even so, Earth’s major powers are willing to suffer heavy losses, spend resources for years, and even risk conflicts with native governments."
His gaze remained fixed on the Patriarch.
"So there must be something there that is far more valuable than ordinary resources."
For a few seconds, the only sound was the faint movement of the papers on the desk.
Then Rhaenar gave a very faint smile.
"Your reasoning isn’t bad."
Lian waited, but the Patriarch did not continue immediately. Instead, he stood up and walked a few steps toward the window.
"The Heavenly Realm is a vast world, Lian. There are things there that remain poorly understood even after decades of human presence."
"That’s not the answer to my question." He narrowed his eyes.
Rhaenar glanced at him.

"I know. Some things will make more sense once you enter that world yourself. For now, just understand that the reasons humans are in the Heavenly Realm aren’t limited to what they write in public reports."
Then he returned to his desk without offering any further explanation.
Lian watched him in silence. So there really was something there. Perhaps a resource related to the theory of going beyond the fifth evolution, at least that was his guess.
Public knowledge said that the fifth evolution was the final one, and an Awakened who reached level 100 could no longer level up.
But what if that wasn’t true? There was a theory that levels above 100 existed, and that Gods stood at that level.
But no one knew how to break through the level 100 barrier and go beyond it.
He suspected that the Celestials might have found a way, and whatever it was, it was hidden in the Heavenly Realm.
Rhaenar clearly had no intention of giving him the full answer either.
Lian decided not to continue the discussion for now.
However, he was now certain that the Heavenly Realm was hiding much greater secrets than he had imagined.
This time, Seris joined the conversation.
"Father."
Rhaenar looked at her.
"Yes?"
"Why don’t the Celestials attack together? In one large, coordinated attack."
The young Vorhelm also looked at her. It was a good question.
If all human Celestials took part in a joint operation, Earth’s military power in the target area would increase greatly.
Such a force could probably conquer even large parts of the territories controlled by the natives.
But Rhaenar began his answer in a serious tone.
"Because the Heavenly Realm isn’t weak."
He placed his hands behind his back.
"We aren’t the only powerful beings in these worlds. The natives of the Heavenly Realm also have forces capable of fighting the most powerful human Awakened."
Seris listened quietly.

"If we gather all Earth’s Celestials for one large attack, we might be able to take over many regions in a short time, but doing so could unite governments that are currently at odds with each other against us."
"And if all of us are there, who will protect Earth?"
Lian thought about the Ruined Realm.
The Rifts.
And even the dangers that might not have been discovered yet.
Leaving Earth without its most powerful defenders just to fight a war in another world could be an extremely dangerous decision.
But Rhaenar had not finished speaking.
"Of course, there’s another problem as well."
"What is it?" The young Pendragon asked.
"If all human Celestials were willing to take part in a joint operation, the chances of success would be much higher."
The Patriarch fell silent for a moment.
"But there’s one person who isn’t willing to take part in such a plan." He looked directly at Lian as he said this.

Perhaps a resource related to the theory of going beyond the fifth evolution, at least that was his guess.
Public knowledge said that the fifth evolution was the final one, and an Awakened who reached level 100 could no longer level up.
But what if that wasn’t true?
There was a theory that levels above 100 existed, and that Gods stood at that level.
But no one knew how to break through the level 100 barrier and go beyond it.
He suspected that the Celestials might have found a way, and whatever it was, it was hidden in the Heavenly Realm.
Rhaenar clearly had no intention of giving him the full answer either.
Lian decided not to continue the discussion for now.
However, he was now certain that the Heavenly Realm was hiding much greater secrets than he had imagined.
This time, Seris joined the conversation.
"Father."
Rhaenar looked at her.
"Yes?"
"Why don’t the Celestials attack together?
In one large, coordinated attack."
The young Vorhelm also looked at her.
It was a good question.
If all human Celestials took part in a joint operation, Earth’s military power in the target area would increase greatly.
Such a force could probably conquer even large parts of the territories controlled by the natives.
But Rhaenar began his answer in a serious tone.
"Because the Heavenly Realm isn’t weak."
He placed his hands behind his back.
"We aren’t the only powerful beings in these worlds.
The natives of the Heavenly Realm also have forces capable of fighting the most powerful human Awakened."
Seris listened quietly.

"If we gather all Earth’s Celestials for one large attack, we might be able to take over many regions in a short time, but doing so could unite governments that are currently at odds with each other against us."
"And if all of us are there, who will protect Earth?"
Lian thought about the Ruined Realm.
The Rifts.
And even the dangers that might not have been discovered yet.
Leaving Earth without its most powerful defenders just to fight a war in another world could be an extremely dangerous decision.
But Rhaenar had not finished speaking.
"Of course, there’s another problem as well."
"What is it?" The young Pendragon asked.
"If all human Celestials were willing to take part in a joint operation, the chances of success would be much higher."
The Patriarch fell silent for a moment.
"But there’s one person who isn’t willing to take part in such a plan." He looked directly at Lian as he said this.

chapters.title: Chapter 592: A Threat to the Celestials
paragraphs: Lian said nothing for a few seconds, but he quickly understood what Rhaenar meant.
His father.
The patriarch of the Vorhelm Family.
The man who was supposed to return to the center of the family’s power soon, after being absent for a long time.
He frowned slightly, as this was strange. If his father was truly against launching a large-scale attack on the Heavenly Realm, he probably had a serious reason.
But what reason could that be? Did he know something about the native forces that the others did not?
Or was he pursuing a completely different goal?
Lian opened his mouth.
"Before you ask, I don’t know the reason either." Rhaenar spoke first, then added after a short pause,
"When you see your father, ask him yourself."
Lian nodded, although he was still unsure whether he even wanted to see his father.
Silence fell between them for a while, and he looked at the Ancestral Mark on the back of his hand.
He had learned a lot about the Heavenly Realm during their conversation, but his most important questions remained unanswered.
On the other hand, there was something Rhaenar might be able to explain in more detail.
He raised his head.
"I have another question."
"It seems your questions never end." The patriarch looked at him.
"After all, I don’t get the chance to talk to a Celestial every day." The young Vorhelm replied calmly.
"You’re making good use of this opportunity."
Rhaenar sat down again.
"Ask."
Lian paused for a moment.
"What do you know about the Indestructible Body and the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul?"
This time, he expected to see at least a small change in the patriarch’s expression, but Rhaenar neither looked surprised nor even raised his eyebrows.
He simply looked at Lian for a few seconds before slowly nodding.
"So my guess was correct. You managed to form both of them."
"You know about them?"
"Of course, and I suspected that you had obtained them. The structure of your body and soul shows it."
Rhaenar gave his answer so naturally that it sounded as if Lian had asked him about an ordinary skill.
But then he continued,
"However, knowing about a structure is different from seeing someone who has actually formed it. Even among the great families, achievements like these are uncommon."
His gaze remained on Lian for a moment.
"What percentage of completion have you reached?"
"Twenty percent for both."
"Then you’re still at the very beginning." The man gave a small smile.
Lian nodded.
"The system says that every twenty percent increase in completion makes the structure ten times stronger."
"That’s correct, but you need to understand exactly what that means."
The patriarch placed his hand on the table.

"Most Awakened believe that when their attributes increase, all their actual power grows by the same amount. This is somewhat true during the lower evolutions, but the higher you go, the more important the limits of your body and soul become."

"Imagine two people with the same physical strength attribute. One has an ordinary body, while the other’s muscles, bones, and force-transfer pathways have been refined. What do you think would happen if they collided directly?"
"The second person would probably transfer more force and put less pressure on his own body."
"Exactly."
Rhaenar nodded.
"The Indestructible Body takes this concept to a much higher level."
He explained that Lian’s body was no longer just a collection of strengthened organs. Every part of his body had reached a higher and more balanced level of quality through the refinement process.
His muscles could produce more force, while his bones and internal organs could withstand greater pressure.
"At full completion, the physical quality of such a body can be compared to that of the most powerful monster races."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Even the World Devourer Giants?" As far as he knew, that race was considered to have the strongest physical bodies among all monsters.
Even his Ancient-rank armor had been made from the corpse of a monster belonging to that same race.
"Yes. Of course, there are many differences within that monster race itself, but you can understand the level I’m talking about."
Rhaenar paused.
"At one hundred percent completion, the Indestructible Body makes physical invulnerability almost a reality. But that doesn’t mean you become immune to every power in the world."
Lian nodded, as he understood the difference between physical durability and dealing with a power like the Essence of the End.
The patriarch continued,
"There are powers that don’t even need to overcome your body’s normal resistance. Some target the soul, some destroy the mana structure, and others can even affect deeper concepts."
His expression became slightly more serious.
"So never assume that you can directly withstand every attack just because your body has become more durable."
"I learned that one already." Lian gave a faint smile.
Rhaenar did not ask anything, but he seemed to understand that this statement was probably related to what had happened in the prison.
"What about the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul?" Lian asked.
Rhaenar clasped his fingers together.

"That one might become even more valuable than the Indestructible Body in the future. The souls of most Awakened grow stronger as their Soul attribute increases, but the basic structure of their souls still has its own limits, just like their bodies."
"The Golden Nine-Dragon Soul doesn’t just increase your defense. It changes the structure of your soul and creates nine dragon guardians formed from your original soul."
Lian nodded.
"I’ve seen them."
Rhaenar smiled.
"Then you probably realized that they aren’t separate creatures."
"Yeah. Each one is a part of my soul."
"Correct, and that’s what makes them important."
Rhaenar explained that the nine guardians could examine the energy flows entering and leaving Lian’s soul and adjust them when necessary.
At the lower stages, this ability mainly increased stability and resistance to soul damage.
However, at higher stages, when soul powers became more complex and dangerous, having such a structure could make the difference between maintaining control and having one’s soul collapse.
Lian remembered the nine enormous golden dragons flying around the main structure of his soul.
"They can attack, too."
Rhaenar nodded.

"And that ability also grows as the completion percentage increases. But remember that the power of a soul attack doesn’t depend only on the amount of energy. The quality of your enemy’s soul, their resistance, and the difference between your levels also matter."
He leaned forward slightly.

"When completion reaches one hundred percent, the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul will become the Soul of the Nine Dragon Emperors. That stage cannot be compared to what you have now. At that point, your soul will become completely immortal."
Lian remained silent for a few seconds.
The Soul of the Nine Dragon Emperors.
"Then how do I increase the completion percentage?"

"For the Indestructible Body, you need to improve the quality of your body step by step. Ordinary energy isn’t enough. You need suitable resources for refinement, deeper refinement, and materials whose quality is higher than that of your body’s current structure."
Rhaenar raised one finger.

"But the strength of the resource isn’t the only thing that matters. Compatibility is also important. If you absorb energy that your body’s structure cannot properly adapt to, you might suffer serious damage instead of increasing your completion."

"The dragon blood was an example of that. Your body was compatible with it, and it was a very valuable refinement resource. You need something of at least equal value, or something even more valuable."
Something even more valuable than the blood of a Demon?
Where was he supposed to find something like that, especially at his current level?
"The same applies to the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul. You need to find soul resources of higher quality."
Lian listened carefully, but he did not look happy.
Finding resources as valuable as the blood of a Demon would not be easy even for a Celestial, let alone someone like him who had only completed his First Evolution.
"And can I find these resources in the Ruined Realm?"
Rhaenar shook his head.
"Maybe some of them, but for the higher stages? That’s unlikely."
He paused.
"Sooner or later, you’ll have to enter the Heavenly Realm."
He let out a quiet breath.
The Heavenly Realm again. It seemed that no matter which path he considered, he always ended up at the same world.
Rhaenar continued,
"The true value of these two structures will become clear when you reach the Celestial level."
"Because at that point, the quality of your body and soul will greatly affect how much power you can control and release."
"Two Celestials might have very different energy reserves, but the one with a superior body and soul can use his power at a much higher level and for a much longer time."
"And if you have completed both the Indestructible Body and the Soul of the Nine Dragon Emperors by then... no other Celestial will be able to stand against you."
A calm smile appeared on his face.
"But no one has ever reached that level. Anyone who has managed to obtain even one of these two structures has been killed without difficulty."
"The Celestials won’t allow such a threat to grow."

chapters.title: Chapter 593: The Patriarch’s Warning
paragraphs: These two structures had not been created just to make a level twenty-nine Awakened stronger, they were the foundation of a power that could make a huge difference at much higher levels.
But what exactly did this man mean when he said the Celestials would kill him?
Lian stared at the patriarch with a confused expression, and the man simply laughed in response.
"Don’t worry, since I know about your relationship with my daughter, I won’t try to kill you like the others would, but my warning still stands, be careful around the other Celestials."
He paused for a moment before adding,
"If they find out, they won’t leave you alone, no one wants the balance of power to change."
Lian remained silent, as he fully understood the situation, however, he had never expected to suddenly become a threat to the most powerful beings in the world.
And he doubted that hiding himself from them would be easy.

"They won’t notice that you’ve obtained these two structures the way I did, I guessed because it was obvious, being able to hold your own against a Demon at your age is proof of your talent, and with talent like yours, it’s easy to figure out."
"Then I don’t need to find a way to hide them?" The young Vorhelm asked after thinking for a moment.
"I doubt you’ll be unlucky enough to encounter the other Celestials again so soon."
Lian nodded, as he had received an answer to some extent.
"Father." Seris, who had mostly been listening until now, raised her right hand.
Rhaenar looked at her.
"Yes?"
"Dragon Veins."
With a gentle flow of mana, thin golden and silver lines appeared beneath the skin of the girl’s wrist.
The lights moved along her forearm, and for a moment, a faint glow could even be seen beneath the clothes on her shoulder.
Then they slowly faded away.
Rhaenar looked at his daughter’s hand for a few seconds.
"So you have an achievement of your own, too."
Seris nodded.
"How should I complete them?"
The patriarch gave a small smile.
"Dragon Veins have become part of your body’s and soul’s structure, and they can be a great help to you in the future, as you know, they allow you to use the power of a dragon."

"As your veins grow, the connection between your body, soul, and Ancestral Mark will become stronger. This structure can become especially important when you reach the stage of forming a Dragon Body."
"Do they require special resources?"

"Yes. You need suitable resources related to dragon races and gradual refinement. Heavenly Dragon Marrow can also help you in the later stages, but you don’t need to focus all your attention on that for now."
Seris glanced at her wrist for a moment.
Rhaenar continued,
"The most important thing is that you don’t try to force your Dragon Veins to grow too quickly. Your body and soul must be ready at the same time."
Then he gave a small smile.
"Knowing you, that was probably the first thing you wanted to do."
The young Pendragon said nothing, she simply lowered her hand.
Lian glanced at her face from the side, and it seemed that the patriarch had guessed correctly.
He gave a faint smile.
"I think that warning was meant more for you."
Seeing the two of them, Rhaenar slightly shook his head, but unlike a few minutes ago, there was something different in his eyes this time.
For a moment, he looked between Lian and his daughter, then asked very casually,
"By the way, where exactly is the relationship between you two supposed to go?"
For a moment, Lian thought he had misheard, and Seris also turned her head toward her father.
Just a few seconds ago, they had been talking about legendary refinement structures, Celestials, and resources from the Heavenly Realm.
And now?
Rhaenar seemed to have brought up another completely ordinary topic.
The young Vorhelm raised his eyebrows.
"Excuse me?"
The patriarch continued without the slightest change in his expression.
"You two have been spending more time together lately, so I thought it wouldn’t hurt to know what your plans are."
Seris continued looking at her father, while the fingers of her right hand slowly curled around the armrest of her chair.
Lian thought for a few seconds before answering,
"For now, our plan is to become stronger."
Rhaenar looked at him.
"That’s all?"
"For now."
Silence fell for a moment, and then the patriarch gave a very small smile.
"Then I should make one thing clear from the beginning."
Lian felt the man’s tone change, it was not threatening, but it became much more serious than before.
"As long as you’re a Vorhelm, you won’t be allowed to marry my daughter."
He did not answer for several seconds, marriage? When had the conversation even reached marriage?
He had not even made a clear decision about his own feelings toward Seris yet.
He enjoyed being by her side, trusted her, and had come to value her presence in battle.
But Rhaenar was talking about marriage as if the ceremony were going to happen tomorrow.
Lian let out a quiet breath.
"I don’t think we’ve reached that stage yet."
"I know."
Rhaenar continued looking at him calmly.
"That’s why I’m telling you now, before it’s too late."
Seris wanted to say something for a moment, but her father continued.
"I have no personal problem with you, Lian, you’ve already understood that."
His smile slowly disappeared.
"But I don’t trust the Vorhelms."
Lian’s expression became more serious, the rivalry between the two families was nothing new, but Rhaenar’s tone made it clear that this was more than just a political disagreement or an old rivalry.
"The Vorhelms bring misfortune."
The man remained silent for a moment, his gaze moved away from Lian and settled on an unclear point beside the window.
"I don’t want what happened to my sister to happen to my daughter, too."
The young Vorhelm was no longer smiling.
Rhaenar’s sister? Until now, he had never heard anything about what had happened to the patriarch’s sister.
Even the information he had about the rivalry between the Pendragons and the Vorhelms contained no clear mention of such an event.
However, from the way Rhaenar spoke, it was clear that this matter held deep personal meaning for him.
Lian was about to ask a question, but before he could say anything...
"Father!"
Seris’s voice rose, this time it was not cold and brief like her usual replies, but firm and clearly full of protest.
Rhaenar turned his gaze toward his daughter, and for a moment, their eyes met.
She had tightened her fingers around the armrest of the chair.
From her expression, it was clear that she wanted to object, but the patriarch did not even allow the conversation to turn into a long argument.
He calmly shook his head.
"Anyway, enough being lazy."
Lian blinked.
Lazy?
"You’ve spent an entire month resting, it’s time to start working hard again."
For a moment, he genuinely did not know whether to laugh or protest.
He had spent a month under pressure in the Dragon Blood River that even his monster-like body could barely endure.
His bones and muscles had been refined again and again, his soul had gained a completely new structure, and now Rhaenar was calling that entire month a rest?
But before he could say anything, the patriarch continued,
"Reach your Third Evolution as soon as possible.
His gaze moved between the two of them this time.
"You might be the strongest among humans of your generation, but don’t forget that your greatest enemies and rivals are in the Heavenly Realm."
Seris was still unhappy about the earlier topic, but Rhaenar clearly had no intention of discussing marriage again.
He raised his hand.
"You can leave for now."
Lian felt the change in space before the movement was complete, the distance between the desk and the door became strange for a moment.
Seris also noticed the change, but neither of them had a chance to react.
Rhaenar simply moved his hand slightly, and then both of them disappeared from in front of the desk, appearing in the hallway outside the office a moment later.
The huge wooden door closed behind them.
He looked at it for a few seconds before letting out a quiet breath.
"Your father is a strange man... Ah, my father is the same."
Seris gave no reply, and Lian glanced at her briefly, the girl was silent, and her gaze remained fixed on the stone floor of the hallway for a moment.
It seemed that she was still thinking about her father’s words.
At first, she had intended to apologize to Lian for Rhaenar’s behavior.
But just before she opened her mouth, another thought came to her mind.
Why should I apologize? Her father had said he would not allow Lian to marry her.
So why did those words bother her so much? Was she planning to marry Lian?
She glanced at the young man beside her for a moment.
Lian was still standing calmly, and it seemed that the sudden change of topic by Rhaenar was stranger to him than the marriage discussion itself.
Marriage...? The word repeated in Seris’s mind for a moment.
She liked being with Lian, and she enjoyed training and fighting alongside him.
She wanted to become stronger so she could stay by his side in future battles.
When Lian was away from her, she sometimes thought about his return more than she expected.
But marriage? The young Pendragon had never made a decision about such a thing.
She did not even have a clear idea of what their relationship would become in the future.
Then why did hearing her father’s objection make her feel as if someone wanted to take something away from her?
The girl looked away from Lian, and a very faint color appeared on her cheeks, so slight that it was almost impossible to notice in the soft light of the hallway.
Do I really want to marry him? For a moment, Seris felt that it would be better to stop thinking about this.
At least for now.
But just as she was trying to sort out her thoughts, Lian’s voice rang out.
"By the way, do you want to return to the Ruined Realm?"
Seris raised her head, and for a moment, her gaze rested on his face.
Then she nodded.
"Yeah."
The young Vorhelm gave a small smile.
"Good. Because I have a suggestion."
Seris waited.
"Before we check out that hidden area, how about we settle an old debt?"
The girl fell silent for a moment.
An old debt?
Her gaze remained fixed on Lian’s face, and she quickly understood what he meant, the creature they had both decided to return to someday.
The monster whose memory was still unpleasant for her.
And now, after a month of refinement in the Dragon Blood River, they had an excellent chance to test their new powers.
Her eyes narrowed slightly, and her lips slowly moved.
"The Dreadmaw Sovereign?"

"Then I don’t need to find a way to hide them?" The young Vorhelm asked after thinking for a moment.
"I doubt you’ll be unlucky enough to encounter the other Celestials again so soon."
Lian nodded, as he had received an answer to some extent.
"Father." Seris, who had mostly been listening until now, raised her right hand.
Rhaenar looked at her.
"Yes?"
"Dragon Veins."
With a gentle flow of mana, thin golden and silver lines appeared beneath the skin of the girl’s wrist.
The lights moved along her forearm, and for a moment, a faint glow could even be seen beneath the clothes on her shoulder.
Then they slowly faded away.
Rhaenar looked at his daughter’s hand for a few seconds.
"So you have an achievement of your own, too."
Seris nodded.
"How should I complete them?"
The patriarch gave a small smile.
"Dragon Veins have become part of your body’s and soul’s structure, and they can be a great help to you in the future, as you know, they allow you to use the power of a dragon."
"As your veins grow, the connection between your body, soul, and Ancestral Mark will become stronger.
This structure can become especially important when you reach the stage of forming a Dragon Body."
"Do they require special resources?"
"Yes.
You need suitable resources related to dragon races and gradual refinement.
Heavenly Dragon Marrow can also help you in the later stages, but you don’t need to focus all your attention on that for now."
Seris glanced at her wrist for a moment.
Rhaenar continued,
"The most important thing is that you don’t try to force your Dragon Veins to grow too quickly.
Your body and soul must be ready at the same time."
Then he gave a small smile.
"Knowing you, that was probably the first thing you wanted to do."
The young Pendragon said nothing, she simply lowered her hand.
Lian glanced at her face from the side, and it seemed that the patriarch had guessed correctly.
He gave a faint smile.
"I think that warning was meant more for you."
Seeing the two of them, Rhaenar slightly shook his head, but unlike a few minutes ago, there was something different in his eyes this time.
For a moment, he looked between Lian and his daughter, then asked very casually,
"By the way, where exactly is the relationship between you two supposed to go?"
For a moment, Lian thought he had misheard, and Seris also turned her head toward her father.
Just a few seconds ago, they had been talking about legendary refinement structures, Celestials, and resources from the Heavenly Realm.
And now?
Rhaenar seemed to have brought up another completely ordinary topic.
The young Vorhelm raised his eyebrows.
"Excuse me?"
The patriarch continued without the slightest change in his expression.
"You two have been spending more time together lately, so I thought it wouldn’t hurt to know what your plans are."
Seris continued looking at her father, while the fingers of her right hand slowly curled around the armrest of her chair.
Lian thought for a few seconds before answering,
"For now, our plan is to become stronger."
Rhaenar looked at him.
"That’s all?"
"For now."
Silence fell for a moment, and then the patriarch gave a very small smile.
"Then I should make one thing clear from the beginning."
Lian felt the man’s tone change, it was not threatening, but it became much more serious than before.
"As long as you’re a Vorhelm, you won’t be allowed to marry my daughter."
He did not answer for several seconds, marriage?
When had the conversation even reached marriage?
He had not even made a clear decision about his own feelings toward Seris yet.
He enjoyed being by her side, trusted her, and had come to value her presence in battle.
But Rhaenar was talking about marriage as if the ceremony were going to happen tomorrow.
Lian let out a quiet breath.
"I don’t think we’ve reached that stage yet."
"I know."
Rhaenar continued looking at him calmly.
"That’s why I’m telling you now, before it’s too late."
Seris wanted to say something for a moment, but her father continued.
"I have no personal problem with you, Lian, you’ve already understood that."
His smile slowly disappeared.
"But I don’t trust the Vorhelms."
Lian’s expression became more serious, the rivalry between the two families was nothing new, but Rhaenar’s tone made it clear that this was more than just a political disagreement or an old rivalry.
"The Vorhelms bring misfortune."
The man remained silent for a moment, his gaze moved away from Lian and settled on an unclear point beside the window.
"I don’t want what happened to my sister to happen to my daughter, too."
The young Vorhelm was no longer smiling.
Rhaenar’s sister?
Until now, he had never heard anything about what had happened to the patriarch’s sister.
Even the information he had about the rivalry between the Pendragons and the Vorhelms contained no clear mention of such an event.
However, from the way Rhaenar spoke, it was clear that this matter held deep personal meaning for him.
Lian was about to ask a question, but before he could say anything...
"Father!"
Seris’s voice rose, this time it was not cold and brief like her usual replies, but firm and clearly full of protest.
Rhaenar turned his gaze toward his daughter, and for a moment, their eyes met.
She had tightened her fingers around the armrest of the chair.
From her expression, it was clear that she wanted to object, but the patriarch did not even allow the conversation to turn into a long argument.
He calmly shook his head.
"Anyway, enough being lazy."
Lian blinked.
Lazy?
"You’ve spent an entire month resting, it’s time to start working hard again."
For a moment, he genuinely did not know whether to laugh or protest.
He had spent a month under pressure in the Dragon Blood River that even his monster-like body could barely endure.
His bones and muscles had been refined again and again, his soul had gained a completely new structure, and now Rhaenar was calling that entire month a rest?
But before he could say anything, the patriarch continued,
"Reach your Third Evolution as soon as possible.
His gaze moved between the two of them this time.
"You might be the strongest among humans of your generation, but don’t forget that your greatest enemies and rivals are in the Heavenly Realm."
Seris was still unhappy about the earlier topic, but Rhaenar clearly had no intention of discussing marriage again.
He raised his hand.
"You can leave for now."
Lian felt the change in space before the movement was complete, the distance between the desk and the door became strange for a moment.
Seris also noticed the change, but neither of them had a chance to react.
Rhaenar simply moved his hand slightly, and then both of them disappeared from in front of the desk, appearing in the hallway outside the office a moment later.
The huge wooden door closed behind them.
He looked at it for a few seconds before letting out a quiet breath.
"Your father is a strange man...
Ah, my father is the same."
Seris gave no reply, and Lian glanced at her briefly, the girl was silent, and her gaze remained fixed on the stone floor of the hallway for a moment.
It seemed that she was still thinking about her father’s words.
At first, she had intended to apologize to Lian for Rhaenar’s behavior.
But just before she opened her mouth, another thought came to her mind.
Why should I apologize?
Her father had said he would not allow Lian to marry her.
So why did those words bother her so much?
Was she planning to marry Lian?
She glanced at the young man beside her for a moment.
Lian was still standing calmly, and it seemed that the sudden change of topic by Rhaenar was stranger to him than the marriage discussion itself.
Marriage...?
The word repeated in Seris’s mind for a moment.
She liked being with Lian, and she enjoyed training and fighting alongside him.
She wanted to become stronger so she could stay by his side in future battles.
When Lian was away from her, she sometimes thought about his return more than she expected.
But marriage?
The young Pendragon had never made a decision about such a thing.
She did not even have a clear idea of what their relationship would become in the future.
Then why did hearing her father’s objection make her feel as if someone wanted to take something away from her?
The girl looked away from Lian, and a very faint color appeared on her cheeks, so slight that it was almost impossible to notice in the soft light of the hallway.
Do I really want to marry him?
For a moment, Seris felt that it would be better to stop thinking about this.
At least for now.
But just as she was trying to sort out her thoughts, Lian’s voice rang out.
"By the way, do you want to return to the Ruined Realm?"
Seris raised her head, and for a moment, her gaze rested on his face.
Then she nodded.
"Yeah."
The young Vorhelm gave a small smile.
"Good.
Because I have a suggestion."
Seris waited.
"Before we check out that hidden area, how about we settle an old debt?"
The girl fell silent for a moment.
An old debt?
Her gaze remained fixed on Lian’s face, and she quickly understood what he meant, the creature they had both decided to return to someday.
The monster whose memory was still unpleasant for her.
And now, after a month of refinement in the Dragon Blood River, they had an excellent chance to test their new powers.
Her eyes narrowed slightly, and her lips slowly moved.
"The Dreadmaw Sovereign?"

chapters.title: Chapter 594: Time to Settle an Old Debt
paragraphs: A cold wind passed between the snow-covered rocks.
The sky was red, and heavy clouds covered a large part of the distant peaks.
Along the mountainside, tall trees could be seen, their branches bending under the force of the wind, while the snow piled on them slowly fell to the ground.
In the middle of this cold and quiet landscape, a blue light appeared.
A few seconds later, Lian stepped out of the light, his feet landing on the snow-covered ground.
He looked around for a moment, this was the same mountain range that held some unpleasant memories for him.
After finishing their conversation with Rhaenar, he and Seris had decided to return to one of the old areas of the Ruined Realm before going their separate ways.

Fortunately, both of them had already registered return points in this area, so they did not need to travel through the long mountain path from the beginning again, not to mention that they had no idea how they would even find their way here without those points.
Lian had simply selected the point he wanted, and his special travel ability for the Ruined Realm had brought him here.
A few moments later, another blue light appeared a short distance away from him.
Seris appeared.
The girl took a step onto the snow, and her silver hair moved slightly in the wind as her cold gaze immediately turned toward the mountain peak.
The young Vorhelm looked in the same direction, but after a few seconds, his eyebrows drew together slightly.
Something was wrong.
"Seris."
The girl looked at him.
Lian pointed toward the mountains.
"Do you remember what this place looked like last time?"
Seris looked at the distant slopes for a few seconds before slowly nodding.
"Yeah."

Back then, the mountains had been covered in green plants, with tall rocks rising from the ground. A small village stood among the slopes, and narrow paths led from it toward a cave where the Dreadmaw Sovereign lived.
But now? A large part of the northern slope was gone.

The place where the cave entrance had once been was now a huge, black crack, the surrounding rocks had collapsed, and deep marks stretched from near the peak down toward the lower parts of the mountain.
Even the surrounding forests had been damaged.
Some trees had been pulled out by their roots, while others had been reduced to nothing but broken, blackened trunks.
Lian examined the scene for a few seconds before giving a low whistle.
"Wow."
The young Pendragon looked at him.
"What?"
"Looks like someone got really angry after we left."
The girl looked at the mountains again, and the corner of her mouth lifted slightly.
"Very angry."
Lian laughed, but when his gaze fell on the ruined slope, his smile slowly disappeared.
That creature had truly destroyed the entire area.
After its thirty-year plan had failed, it had probably had nothing left to control its anger.
"I never thought I’d willingly come back here one day." He muttered softly.
Seris looked at him.
"I wanted to come back and kill it."
Silence fell for a few moments, then Lian asked with a faint smile,
"Do you still remember the hit you took last time?
For a moment, Seris looked at her left leg, the same leg that had been broken during their first battle against the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"Yeah."
Her gaze returned to the mountains.
"But this time is different."
"Very different." He nodded.
They both started moving.
At first, their path passed through a forest where only scattered parts remained undamaged.
Snow covered the broken trunks, and some rocks had burn marks or signs of powerful impacts on their surfaces.
However, the closer they got to the mountains, the worse the destruction became.
Lian sometimes looked at the deep cracks that ran through the ground, some of them were several meters wide and stretched over long distances.
Based on the direction of the broken rocks, it was possible to guess that a huge force had been released from the upper part of the mountains toward the slopes.
And apparently, this had happened more than once.
"Do you think it’s still here?" Seris asked, seeing what the creature had done to this place out of anger. It was possible that it had already left the mountain by now.
He shook his head.
"There’s a good chance it is."
"Why?"
"If it could leave this place, it probably would have done so years ago."
Lian looked toward the peak.
"That creature needed a human body to enter human Regions, so it’s unlikely that it managed to leave the mountains without achieving its goal."
She nodded, the reasoning made sense.
But Lian was also considering another possibility.
Perhaps, after its plan had failed, the Dreadmaw Sovereign had finally found a new way to evolve.
If that had happened, they might be facing a creature far stronger than before, though this possibility did not worry him too much.
Not after everything he had experienced over the past few months.
Some time later, they reached the area near the old village... or more accurately, what remained of it.
Lian stopped on a small hill, from there, he could see the former location of the village.
The wooden houses had been almost completely destroyed, some were buried beneath piles of rocks, while others had nothing left but broken foundations sticking out of the snow.
The village’s central square was also buried beneath a thick layer of dirt and stone, and there was no longer any sign of the narrow paths between the houses.
Seris stood beside him.
Neither of them spoke for a few moments, but this time, the silence felt different.
He remembered the day they had entered this same village, the seemingly kind people, the village chief who spoke about the Mountain God.
And the three young people who had believed they had finally found a way to return home.
Aria.
Alisa.
Ryan.
Aria’s face appeared in his mind for a moment, the girl who had tried to protect the person she loved until the very end.
And that same person had ripped her heart out of her chest.
Lian still remembered the girl’s disbelieving expression, and even Alisa’s cries had not faded from his memories.
The sound that had echoed through the stone hall that day, while the Dreadmaw Sovereign watched everything from its throne.
He let out a quiet breath.
"I still remember."
Seris looked at him, there was no need to ask what he was talking about.
"Me too."
For a moment, the girl looked at the remains of the village.
"That creature..."
She did not finish her sentence, but Lian understood what she meant, the Dreadmaw Sovereign was not just a powerful monster.
It was a creature that nurtured human emotions to achieve its goals, only to destroy them at the worst possible moment.
To it, love, hope, and sorrow were nothing more than tools for its experiments.
He looked toward the mountains again.
"Let’s go."
She nodded.
They both walked down the hill and left the ruined village behind, the higher they climbed, the more difficult the path became.
But it was not because of the cold or the steep mountain slopes, a large part of the old paths no longer existed.
Where a narrow road had once passed between the rocks, there was now a deep cliff, while in another area, a huge pile of broken stones blocked the path.
Lian passed through the obstacles without difficulty, and Seris stayed close behind him.
Over the past few months, they had both grown strong enough that such obstacles no longer mattered much to them.
However, halfway along the path, he suddenly stopped, and his eyes narrowed slightly.
She stopped at the same moment, both of them had sensed something at the same time.
A very weak flow of energy was moving down from the cracks in the upper mountains, the energy was dark and heavy, but familiar to them.
Unlike the scattered energy of ordinary monsters, it had a clear and concentrated structure.
Lian looked toward the highest part of the mountains, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
"We found it."
Seris followed his gaze, in the distance, a huge shadow could be seen among the mist and floating dust.
But before they could make out its exact shape... BOOM!
A deep sound came from the top of the mountains, like a heavy strike against a huge bell.
A few seconds later, a wave of pressure passed through the rocky gaps and sent the snow on the slopes flying into the air.
Both of them remained still.
A second sound rang out, this time closer.
Then, a deep voice spread across the entire area from the top of the mountains.
The wind stopped for a moment.
"Dares to set foot in my territory?"
Lian raised his head, his smile grew slightly wider, and he said mockingly,
"Looks like it’s still just as welcoming."

chapters.title: Chapter 595: The Tables Have Turned
paragraphs: They covered the remaining distance at a faster speed.
When they reached the area near the former cave, the scene before them was even more destroyed than what they had seen from below.
The cave no longer existed, the massive stone ceiling that had once covered the hall of the Dreadmaw Sovereign had completely collapsed.
A large part of the mountain wall had also split open, turning the inside of the cave into an open area.
At the center of this area was a huge pit, surrounded by broken pillars, black rocks, and the remains of bones.
The cold wind passed freely through the ruins, and the gray sky could be seen directly above the area.
However, at the far end of the area, a creature was sitting on a black stone pillar that remained among the ruins of the old throne.
It had a massive, red body, and twisted horns like the dry branches of trees that grew out from both sides of its head.
Its mouth was wide and unnatural, looking like a permanent smile even when closed, and its two black eyes were buried deep in its face.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign.
Lian looked at the creature for a few seconds.
[ Name: Dreadmaw Sovereign ]
[ Level: 20 ]
[ Rank: Unholy ]
For a moment, his gaze remained fixed on the number twenty, it was still the same level and still had not undergone its first evolution.
He tilted his head slightly.
So you really couldn’t make any more progress.
Of all the things he had expected to see, this was almost disappointing, while the Dreadmaw Sovereign continued to keep its eyes on them.
At first, it only saw two humans who had entered its ruined territory without permission, but when its gaze settled on Lian’s face, its fingers stopped moving.
A few seconds passed.
Then it leaned its head forward slightly, its gaze moving from Lian’s face to Seris and then back again.
Its permanent smile was still there, but its shape slowly began to change.
Its voice came from between its large teeth.
"You two..."
For a moment, silence filled the area. Then the creature suddenly stood up in anger.
"You two damn humans!"
Its voice echoed throughout the open area.
"I’m glad you still remember us." He looked at it calmly.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign clenched its claws, and the remains of the black throne beneath its feet began to crack.
"How dare you come back here again?!"
Its gaze briefly stopped on Lian’s unharmed body.
It clearly remembered what it had done to this human.
It had destroyed his left eye and crushed his bones. It had destroyed almost all of his internal organs.
Even in his final moments, when the young man’s body looked more like a piece of bloody meat, it had still believed his death was certain.
But now? Not only was he alive, there was not even the slightest trace of those injuries on his body.
The monster narrowed its eyes.
So he had healed.
It did not like this.
However, what truly bothered it was their return, the two humans who had destroyed all its plans were now standing before it of their own free will.
The Sovereign spoke in a rough voice.
"Thirty years..."
Its claws slowly tightened.
"I spent thirty years preparing for that day."
Its gaze fell to its empty neck, where the golden key was no longer present, the same key that had once kept the energy flow of its core going almost without stopping.
The key that those three humans had activated while escaping, taking it out of its reach.
"You destroyed my heart, took my key away, and ruined all my efforts!"
The smile on its face grew wider, but this time, it was because of its anger.
"And now you’ve come back on your own just to die?!"
Lian glanced at Seris, the girl was looking at the monster with her usual calm expression, then he turned back to the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"Honestly, we came to see if you had finally managed to evolve."
Silence filled the area for a moment.
"But it seems you’re still level twenty, that’s disappointing."
The Sovereign’s black eyes remained still for a moment.
The same words, the same old insult, even back then, this weak human had dared to point out its failures.
And now, once again... in its own territory... he was standing before it and insulting it.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign lowered its head slightly, and the air around it grew heavier.
"This time..."
Its voice was low and slow.
"I’ll make you wish you had died last time."
"Try it." Lian only smiled.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign raised its right index finger, making a small movement, the same movement that Lian still remembered clearly.

During their first meeting, the monster had released a red beam with nothing more than a movement of one finger, without even getting up from its throne, the result had been the destruction of a large part of the hall, the burning of Lian’s face, and the loss of his left eye.
Seris had also been badly injured in that attack.
But now, when red light gathered at the tip of the monster’s finger, neither of them stepped back.
[ Crimson Decree ]
The red energy was compressed with a sharp sound and then a thick beam shot directly toward him.
The distance between them was less than thirty meters, and the beam crossed that distance in a fraction of a second, melting a layer of stone along its path.
But just before it hit, Seris took one step forward, and a sword appeared in her hand as she swung it only once.
Shiiing!
A silver crescent separated from the edge of the blade.
The two attacks met a few meters apart, but contrary to the Sovereign’s expectations, their collision did not end in a huge explosion.
The silver crescent passed through the center of the beam.
The red energy split into two parts and moved along two different paths toward the rocks behind Lian.
A moment later, two explosions sounded from opposite sides of the area, on the right side, part of the rocky wall split open, and a stream of molten rock flowed down.

Seris also lowered her sword, and for a few seconds, the Dreadmaw Sovereign did not move at all, its gaze first fell on its own finger.
Then it looked at the grooves on the rocks and finally at the silver-haired girl standing before it.
"What...?" The sound barely came out of its mouth.
It knew this attack, it knew very well how much power it contained, last time, this same attack had been enough to bring those two humans to the edge of death.
But now, the girl had split it apart with a single sword swing.
She had not used any powerful skill, nor had she even pushed her mana to its limit, it had been nothing more than a simple slash.
What exactly had happened? Was it seeing things? Or had it finally gone crazy?
How could a lowly human block its attack so easily?
The Sovereign unconsciously curled the fingers of its right hand.
’Maybe I didn’t use enough power?’
This explanation seemed more reasonable than any other possibility.
Humans could become stronger, and they might even have evolved during this time, but it was impossible for the difference in power between them to have changed this much.
The monster let out a heavy breath.
Even if the girl had survived its long-range attack, that did not mean she could withstand its physical strength.
Its claws opened, and then its entire body moved forward.
The stone beneath its feet broke.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign jumped down from the remaining pillar of the throne and charged straight at Seris.
Despite its three-meter-tall body, it moved extremely fast, its right arm pulled back, and thick black claws extended from its fingers.
But before it could reach the girl, Lian stepped into its path and, without activating any defensive skill, simply raised his right hand.
Thud!
A dull impact echoed through the area.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign’s claws stopped a short distance from the young Vorhelm’s face.

For a moment, the monster did not understand what had happened, then its gaze moved down, the fingers of that human were wrapped around its massive wrist, the Sovereign let out a short growl and tried to pull its hand back.
But its wrist did not move... it applied more force... this time, the muscles in its shoulder and arm swelled, and the stones beneath its feet cracked, yet Lian did not even take a single step back.
What exactly was happening???
The Sovereign stared at the young man’s face, its permanent smile no longer looked anything like it had a few moments ago.
"I remember you did the same thing to me last time." Lian tilted his head slightly, his gaze briefly stopping on the monster’s fingers.
"Of course, back then, you crushed my hand."
Then he clenched his left fist.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign saw his movement and tried to defend itself with its free hand, but before its arm could reach the right position...
BOOM!
The human’s fist struck its stomach.
No special offensive skill had been activated, and there was no Eclipse Energy or End Energy in the punch.
It was only Lian’s physical strength, a strength that now also benefited from the structure of his Indestructible Body.
The force of the punch first sank into the monster’s stomach, and then its massive body was lifted off the ground... and thrown backward at high speed.
The Sovereign passed by the remains of the throne and crashed into one of the half-broken pillars, smashing it in half.
It then fell to the ground and slid several meters across the rocks.
When it finally stopped, dark blood flowed from its mouth.
For a few seconds, it could not breathe, the pain spreading through its stomach could not be compared to any of the blows it remembered receiving from those two humans.
The monster raised its head with difficulty.
In the distance, Lian was still standing in the same place, even his expression had not changed.
Why did it feel as if their positions had been switched? It was supposed to be the terrifying, invincible monster!
But why did it seem like this human was the real monster noew?
Wthat the fuck?

Its permanent smile was still there, but its shape slowly began to change.

But now?

The monster narrowed its eyes.

Its claws slowly tightened.
"I spent thirty years preparing for that day."

chapters.title: Chapter 596: The Sovereign’s Desperate Struggle
paragraphs: The monster looked down at its own stomach, the red skin in that area had split open, and something beneath the point of impact was hurting badly.
Impossible!
It was a creature of the Unholy rank.
Even without its first evolution, its physical structure was far beyond that of ordinary monsters and Fallen monsters.
But this human... had injured it with a simple punch...?
The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth.
How did they become so strong?
The monster slowly stood up from among the broken rocks, dark blood dripping from the corner of its mouth, but it no longer intended to look at its opponents with the same contempt as before.
The two humans in front of it had changed, this was now clear, so it had to treat them as real enemies.
The Sovereign placed both hands on the ground, and black energy flowed from between its fingers into the rocks.
[ Ossuary Gravefield ]
The sounds of repeated cracking came from beneath the ground.
Ten meters away from Lian, a huge pillar of black bone emerged from between the rocks.
Then came a second pillar, a third, and in less than a few seconds, dozens of bone spears and pillars rose from different points across the area.
Some of them were several meters tall, and their sharp tips curved upward.
The Sovereign did not intend to injure them with this attack alone, the pillars blocked their paths of movement.
By creating a gap between the two humans, it could separate them and put more pressure on the weaker target.
But Lian noticed its intention before the bone formation was complete, and his gaze fell on the paths where the pillars were growing.
It was easy to understand that the monster’s goal was to separate them from each other.
The first pillar emerged from beneath his feet, but he only raised his right foot and slammed it down.
CRAAACK!
The tip of the pillar shattered before it could emerge from the ground, and a deep crack spread along its structure.
The second pillar bent toward his side from the left, Lian struck it with his elbow, and pieces of bone scattered in every direction.
He caught the third pillar with his hand and pushed it away from its path, the bone root emerged from between the rocks and broke against the ground.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign did not move for a moment, these pillars had been created by it.
They were not supposed to break like dry tree branches.
But that human was destroying them one after another without using a skill.
On the other side, Seris passed between two pillars with a short movement.
Her sword drew a silver crescent through the air and cut through the four bone spears that had risen around her.
The broken pieces fell to the ground, she did not even slow down and briefly looked at the Sovereign.
"That’s it?" The girl’s voice was calm.
But to the monster, it felt heavier than any insult.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign let out an angry roar, this time, its twisted horns began to shake.
A deep, drawn-out sound came from them, a sound that first resembled the howl of the wind at night, but soon turned into a sound with several layers.
[ Litany of Silent Hearts ]
The air grew heavier, and faint whispers could be heard among the sound of the wind.
Human voices.
Crying.
Begging.
And screams that seemed to come from a very distant place.
The Young Pendragon stopped moving for a moment, she heard a familiar voice among the whispers.
"Sister..."
For a fraction of a second, the image of Aria appeared in her mind, the young girl who had looked at Ryan’s bloody hand in disbelief.
But Seris quickly realized that what she was hearing was not Aria’s real voice, this was only a recreation of the emotions and voices that the Sovereign had recorded from its victims over the years.
Even after their deaths, the monster was still using the traces of their suffering to attack.
Her gaze grew colder.
At the same time, something else happened deep within Lian’s soul, the nine golden dragons moving around his main soul raised their heads almost at the same time.
The invading force was detected by the guardians before it reached the central part of his soul, and two dragons blocked its path.
Three other dragons spread its unstable energy throughout their defensive structure, while the remaining guardians covered the other paths.
The soul pressure that was supposed to trap his mind in painful memories lost much of its effect before reaching its main target.

Lian paid attention to this reaction for a moment, then gave a small smile, he had finally gotten the chance to test the Golden Nine-Dragon Soul against a real attack, and the result was very satisfying.
In contrast, the Dreadmaw Sovereign looked at him in disbelief.
Why isn’t it having any effect?
It knew that [ Litany of Silent Hearts ] could even cause some enemies of the same level to suffer from mental confusion for a short time.
But this human seemed to have heard nothing more than an unpleasant sound.
Lian looked at the monster.
"You know... using the voices of your victims is just as disgusting as I expected." His smile disappeared.
The Sovereign gritted its teeth.
But before it could reply, the human continued.
"I think it’s time to end this show."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign stepped back, not out of fear, at least, it was not willing to admit that to itself yet.
But it had now understood that a direct fight with Lian would lead nowhere, so it had to change its approach.
Its gaze settled on the female human, despite her high swordsmanship, the girl was still smaller than the monster in terms of physical size.
If it could catch her off guard from a suitable angle, perhaps it would find a chance to change the situation.
The monster spread both hands, and seven black and red rings formed in the sky above the area.
Inside each ring, long and uneven teeth appeared, then the edges split open, and seven huge mouths, each with rows of bone teeth, emerged from the rings.
[ Feast of Seven Maws ]
The jaws spread out around Seris, two in front, two on the sides, one above her head, and the remaining two positioned along her escape routes.
The monster had carefully chosen its attack angles.
If the Young Pendragon moved backward, she would be caught from behind, if she moved to either side, her path was already blocked.
And if she only defended herself from the front, the upper jaw could crush her from head to toe.
Seris raised her head, looked at the positions of the seven mouths for a moment, and then calmly held her sword in front of her body.
A silver crescent appeared behind her.
[ Moon Manifestation ]
The silver light around her sword grew stronger, and then seven smaller crescents formed around her.
[ Seven-Crescent Orbit ]
The Dreadmaw Sovereign let out a roar, and all seven jaws moved at the same time.
But she did not even step back, the first crescent struck the jaw on the right and forced it off its path.
The second crescent split the mouth in front of her through its upper teeth.
The third and fourth crescents spun in two different directions and destroyed the jaws that had blocked her escape routes.
The fifth jaw came down from above, and Seris only took one step forward, the huge teeth struck the ground a short distance behind her and split another part of the area.
At the same moment, the sixth crescent moved upward from below.
The upper jaw split in half, and only the final mouth remained.
But it did not even get a chance to attack, her sword passed in front of it with a short movement.
SHRAAK!
The two halves of the jaw separated in the air and turned into mana particles before reaching the ground.
The entire attack ended in less than a few seconds, and Seris lowered her sword, her gaze fixed on the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
The creature still had its hands spread out, but nothing remained in the sky.
Not one of the seven jaws and not even the slightest sign of the pressure from the encirclement, the monster forgot to breathe for a moment.
Where did they go? The Seven Hungry Jaws were one of its most powerful abilities, a skill designed to surround and destroy fast enemies.
But the girl had destroyed all of them without even needing to put up a serious defense.
The monster looked at Lian, the young man was standing farther away and calmly watching the fight.
It seemed that he did not even think there was a need to help Seris.
At that moment, an unpleasant thought formed in the Sovereign’s mind.
Could... this girl defeat me on her own, too?
Seris moved, this time, she closed the distance, the Dreadmaw Sovereign immediately jumped backward, but the girl’s sword passed by its shoulder.
Dark blood splashed across the rocks.
The monster let out a short roar and tried to attack from the left, but she changed her position before it could complete its movement.
The second strike hit its right arm, and the third slash landed along its side.
The Sovereign angrily tried to create some distance, but every time it took a step, one of the silver crescents limited its path.
After several exchanges, it finally understood the pattern of Seris’s movements.
The girl did not want to kill it immediately, she was testing its defensive abilities and reaction speed.
This was even more humiliating than the wounds themselves.

chapters.title: Chapter 597: The Unholy Last Blood
paragraphs: The Dreadmaw Sovereign let out a loud roar and slammed its claws into the ground, the dark blood flowing from its wounds spread through the cracks in the stone.
But instead of continuing along its natural path, it began to move in specific directions.
Six red lines spread out from the monster’s body, each reaching a different point in the area, where signs made of dark mana began to form.
[ Inverted Blood Altar ]
Lian felt the change in the mana from a distance.
He narrowed his eyes, six connection points and a central structure, along with streams of energy that were trying to pull the surrounding energy toward the Sovereign’s body.
So it wanted to strengthen itself while weakening its enemies.
The Inverted Blood Altar was not just a defensive field, if it was completed, it could use the energy in the area to strengthen the monster’s injured body.
And the longer the battle continued, the more valuable this advantage could become.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign was also counting on exactly this, it no longer intended to win with a single attack.
If it could keep its opponents inside the field, perhaps it could slowly find a chance to change the situation, but just as the altar’s six connection points lit up, Lian raised his right hand.
Five extremely thin strands of corrupted light containing Eclipse energy formed between his fingers.
Daylight shone through the broken clouds onto the snow-covered rocks.
He used those same paths of light to guide the strands, and five black lines moved along the reflections of the light.
They reached five of the altar’s connection points almost at the same time.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign had not even realized what was happening when the mana structures around the connection points began to break down.
It let out a short roar.
"What?!"
The five strands had not attacked its body, but the Eclipse energy was destroying the altar’s structure.
Five points collapsed one after another.
The final point was still intact, and the monster tried to transfer all its remaining energy into it.
But Seris had already raised her sword, a silver crescent separated from the blade and split the rock holding the final connection point.
CRAAACK!
The central structure of the altar lost its balance.
The streams of red and black blood energy flowed backward for a moment and then spread across the broken stones.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign looked around in disbelief.
It had used various skills and attacks, but none of them had even managed to put these two humans in real trouble.
At that moment, Seris appeared in front of it.
Her sword came down, but this time, the edge of the blade did not strike the monster’s neck directly, it created a deep cut along its shoulder and upper chest.
The Sovereign lost its balance.
When it tried to attack the girl with its claws, a heavy pressure fell upon its body.
[ Sovereign Judgment ]
Its knees bent.
Not because Seris had used up all her mana.
But because the difference in their power had now become so great that even part of the skill’s pressure was enough to hold it down.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign struck the ground with one knee, and the stone beneath it cracked.
She held her sword a short distance from its neck, the girl’s cold eyes fixed on the monster’s face.
"It’s over."
The monster raised its head with broken breaths, its gaze remained on the silver sword for a moment.
Then it looked at Lian.
The young man was still standing a short distance away, without needing to release his true power.
The Sovereign could no longer understand the situation.
How was this possible?
The two humans who once could not even breathe properly under the pressure of its presence had now brought it to its knees.
In the past, it had nearly killed both of them with a single movement of its finger, but now, even all its skills were not enough.
Lian took a few steps closer and looked at Seris.
"That’s enough."
The girl looked at him for a moment, then reduced the pressure of her skill and moved her sword back slightly.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign tried to get up from the ground, but its deep wounds and the blow it had received from Lian would not allow it.
Dark blood flowed from its mouth, its breathing had become irregular, and for a moment, it lowered its head.
Was it really going to die at the hands of these two humans?
At that very moment, something moved deep inside the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s body.
At first, it was very weak, like a heartbeat coming from somewhere farther away than the main heart in its body.
Then... THUMP!
The second beat was much heavier.
The Sovereign remained still for a moment, deep within its existence, a stream of dark energy began to move.
It was something that even the monster itself had never fully activated until that moment.
Lian felt the change in pressure and narrowed his eyes.
[ Warning: Rank Trait Awakened. ]
[ Unholy Last Blood ]
The moment death approaches, the blood of an Unholy begins to react.
The life force buried deep within its existence is released, forcing its dying body to continue fighting even after suffering injuries that should have ended its life.
Crushed organs, broken bones, and damaged muscles are no longer enough to stop it.
Its wounds begin to close as its remaining life force burns away, while its physical strength rises far beyond its previous limits.
The closer it gets to death, the more violently its Unholy nature awakens.
For a short time, even an Unholy that is almost at the edge of death can release power beyond its normal limits, turning every remaining moment of its life into a dangerous and desperate fight.
In addition, all its stats receive a monstrous boost.
But this power comes at a terrible cost.
Every second it spends fighting consumes part of its remaining life force, and with each passing moment, more of its existence is lost.
When this force finally runs out, nothing will remain to sustain its body.
And unlike evolution, this transformation brings no permanent improvement.
It is simply the final resistance of an Unholy that refuses to accept its own death.
Lian looked at the information for a moment.
Then he gave a faint smile.
He had always known that Unholy monsters were far more powerful than Fallen and ordinary monsters, in fact, everyone knew that.
But part of this difference was not just related to their base stats or the number of cores they could form after evolution.
Even before evolution, an Unholy monster possessed a deep reserve of life force that was released when it came close to death.
For an ordinary creature, the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s current injuries could have marked the end of the battle.
But an Unholy monster? It still had another stage, and this ability could completely change the outcome when fighting much stronger enemies.
This could be considered a Rank Trait, and only Unholy monsters and those of higher ranks possessed it.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign raised its head, the black blood flowing from its wounds stopped for a moment.
Then strands of dark energy emerged from the cracks in its skin, and the muscles throughout its body contracted violently.
Its twisted horns cracked and parts of them broke off, but a darker and harder layer was revealed underneath.
Its huge mouth opened, and a sound rose from deep in its throat that no longer resembled an ordinary roar.
GRRRRAAAAAAH!
A wave of pressure spread throughout the area, broken stones were thrown in every direction, and part of the remaining bone pillars collapsed.
Seris took a few steps back to create a suitable distance.
Lian also looked at the monster without any hurry.
The creature slowly rose from the ground, its shoulder wound was still there, but the bleeding had stopped.
Some of its internal injuries had also apparently been suppressed by the consumption of its stored life force.
Its black eyes now glowed with red lines running through them.
The Sovereign took a heavy breath.
Then it looked at Lian, its permanent smile widened again.
"You thought..."
Its claws opened.
"You could kill me this easily?"
Lian gave a slight shrug.
"Don’t you think it’s a little too early for you to start hallucinating?"
Silence filled the area for a moment.
"I WILL KILL YOU, HUMAN!" The Dreadmaw Sovereign let out an angry roar, it no longer intended to hold back its power.
The life force stored within its Unholy nature was being consumed, and it could also feel that it did not have much time left.
But this short amount of time might be enough to kill those two humans, it gathered all its remaining strength into its legs.
And charged toward Lian.
This time, it was faster.
The force of its movement crushed the stones beneath its feet, and its right claw moved toward the young man’s neck at a sharp angle.
But the young Vorhelm did not even try to retreat and raised his right arm.
The Sovereign’s claw struck his forearm.
THUD!
A heavy impact rang out, and for a moment, the force of the blow traveled along Lian’s arm.
His skin was scratched by the monster’s sharp claws, but his bones and muscles held firm.
He only lowered his arm by a few centimeters.
That was all.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign stopped moving, its gaze fixed on the human’s forearm, the wound was very shallow.
Even with the increased power from Unholy Last Blood, an attack that could have torn the bodies of many Awakened apart had only left a scratch on this human’s skin.
The monster felt something inside its chest collapse.
What kind of body is this?
Lian looked at the scratch for a moment and then raised his head.
"Now it’s my turn."
Two enormous black wings spread open behind him.
[ Wings of God ]
