chapters.title: Chapter 598: Serve Me or Die ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: A strong wind moved around him.
The monster instinctively raised its head, those two black wings cast a huge shadow over the ground beneath the red sky above the mountains.
But before the monster could react properly, Lian left the ground and, with a single flap of his wings, rose several meters into the air.
The Sovereign tried to follow his movement by turning its body, but Lian was moving faster than its eyes could follow.
A moment later, a shadow passed over its head.
And then
BOOOOM!
Lian’s foot struck the Sovereign’s shoulder, and the monster’s huge body was slammed into the ground.
The rocks around the impact point sank, and a large crack formed beneath its chest.
The monster let out a painful roar and tried to get back up.
But another force pressed down on its body from the opposite side.
[ Sovereign Judgment ]
Seris held her sword at a short distance, this time using only part of her own mana to restrain the target.
Even so, the skill’s pressure was enough for a creature that was still suffering from serious injuries despite activating Unholy Last Blood.
The Sovereign’s knees bent again.
Lian landed in front of it, and the Wings of God settled quietly behind him.
For a moment, his gaze remained fixed on the creature that had once called itself the god of the mountains.
The monster tried to roar, but its voice turned into a rough cough, and dark blood came out of its mouth.
Its stored life force was rapidly running out.
And this time, there was nothing left to save it.
The young Vorhelm clenched his right hand, his fingers slowly forming a fist.
When the Dreadmaw Sovereign saw that movement, it held its breath for a moment, it knew what the next punch would mean.
In its current condition, even one more hit could end its life.
There was no altar left, no life force left to use with Unholy Last Blood, no way to escape, and not even any hope of defeating these two humans.
This time, it was truly dying.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign took short, broken breaths.
Whenever it tried to move its body, intense pain passed through its shoulder and chest.
The energy of Unholy Last Blood was still flowing inside it, but it could barely suppress its injuries anymore.
Even after activating that innate power, it had failed to push the two humans in front of it back.
Its gaze remained fixed on Lian’s hand, the same hand that had crushed its bones in the past.
Now, if that fist came down, it probably would not get another chance to stand up.
But Lian did not strike, instead, he lowered his hand.
"I have a proposal."
The monster raised its head for a moment.
"What...?"
He glanced at Seris, and the girl reduced the pressure of Sovereign Judgment, but she remained ready to react if it made any suspicious move.
"To be honest, I didn’t come back just to kill you."
The monster gave a bloody smile.
"Then... why did you come back?"
Lian thought for a few seconds before answering.
"To see whether you’re worth keeping alive or not."
The Sovereign narrowed its eyes.
"You’re an Unholy monster, you’re intelligent, you can learn from your experiences, and even though you haven’t undergone your first evolution yet, you’re incredibly powerful."
His gaze briefly fell on the remains of the Inverted Blood Altar.
"If you hadn’t spent all this time experimenting on humans, you would probably have evolved a long time ago.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth, those words hurt more than any other insult.
It had spent thirty years working toward its goal.
It had experimented with different hearts and searched for various ways to become human.
But in the end, everything had failed.
And now, the creature that had destroyed all its efforts was standing in front of it, talking about its wasted talent.
"Shut up..."
"Even so, you still have a chance." Lian showed no reaction.
"Serve me."
For several seconds, complete silence filled the area.
Even the cold wind passing between the rocks could not remove the weight of that moment.
Then, the Dreadmaw Sovereign laughed.
It was a short, rough laugh that quickly turned into a bloody cough.
"A slave?"
Its gaze remained fixed on Lian’s face.
"You want me... the Sovereign of these mountains... to become a subordinate of a human?"
Lian nodded.
"Exactly."
The monster laughed again, this time, its laughter came more from hatred than anything else.
"I hate humans!"
Its claws scraped against the rocks.
"Your race destroyed my entire family, slaughtered the creatures I belonged to, and took our lands."
Its gaze briefly shifted toward the ruined village below the mountains.
"I spent thirty years trying to find a way into human territory. Thirty years searching for a body that could withstand my power."
Its smile disappeared.
"And now you want me to serve a human?"
Lian said nothing, and the Sovereign continued in a firmer voice.
"I would rather die!"
The young Vorhelm looked at it for a few seconds, then nodded very naturally.
"Alright."
That was all.
He did not try to convince it, make any promises, or even explain the benefits of joining the colony.
He simply raised his right hand again, and the Dreadmaw Sovereign fell silent for a moment, it had not expected this reaction.
It had imagined that if this human truly wanted to make it serve him, he would try to convince it.
Perhaps he would threaten it, or perhaps he would promise it more power, but apparently, Lian was truly ready to respect its choice.
And kill it.
The young man’s fingers slowly closed into a fist.
The Sovereign looked at his hand, its entire body was still in pain from the previous punch, and even the thought of being struck by that fist again made its injured muscles tense up instinctively.
Lian took a step closer, but just before he could strike
"Lian."
Seris’s voice rang out, he turned his head toward the girl, and she kept her gaze on the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"Do you really want to keep it?"
Lian remained silent for a moment, then nodded.
"If it agrees."
Seris turned her gaze toward him.
"Aria."
Just one word, but its meaning was completely clear to both of them.
He turned his gaze back to the monster.
"I haven’t forgotten, I haven’t forgotten Aria or the other people it killed."
He remained silent for a few seconds.
"But its death won’t bring them back, if I can keep all its abilities under control, it won’t be able to do those things again."
Seris said nothing.
"An Unholy monster with this much intelligence and growth potential could be a valuable member, especially if I force it to use all its abilities for a different purpose."
Then he looked at the Sovereign.
"Of course, it only gets one chance."
The young Pendragon looked at him for a few moments, she still hated that creature.
But she knew how useful it could be to have a monster as a subordinate.
One and Two could no longer act against Lian’s main commands after accepting the bond.
If this creature really joined the colony, it would no longer have the freedom it once had either.
In that case, even the monster itself might be of much greater help than its corpse.
Seris finally gave a small nod.
"Alright."
However, it still had no intention of giving in, it struggled to raise its head.
"I said... I’d rather die!"
Lian let out a short sigh.
"Fine."
This time, he truly prepared to bring his fist down, but at that very moment, an idea crossed his mind, and his gaze remained on the monster’s face for a moment.
A creature that had spent thirty years trying to use a human body without losing its own monster power.
A creature that believed no ordinary human could withstand its existence energy.
He gave a faint smile.
’Maybe I should show it something interesting before it dies.’
"By the way, I have a question."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign looked at him with hatred.
"What?"
"You spent thirty years searching for a human body that could withstand the power of an Unholy monster, right?"
The monster frowned.
"So what?"
Lian did not answer.
Instead, he released a very small amount of Eclipse Energy from his Eclipse Core.
The faint light shining through the clouds and reaching the area changed around his right hand, and black lines appeared within the light.
Eclipse Energy moved along the paths of the light, and several thin strands of corrupted light formed around Lian’s fingers.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign did not move for a moment, its gaze fixed on the young man’s hand.
At first, it thought it was facing some kind of dark energy, but it soon realized that its nature was different from ordinary mana.
A deep pressure rose from within it.
Not because of the amount of energy, but because of its quality, the monster instinctively lowered its head.
This...
Its instincts had reacted, it felt as if a being of a much higher rank had entered its territory.
But this time, the pressure came from only a few tiny strands of energy.
"What is that...?"
Lian gave a small smile
"Something simple."
That answer did nothing to calm the monster, because it had recognized the energy, not its exact source, but it had recognized its rank, the energy belonged to a being of the Demon rank!
How could this human use something that belonged to a Demon?

He simply raised his right hand again, and the Dreadmaw Sovereign fell silent for a moment, it had not expected this reaction.
It had imagined that if this human truly wanted to make it serve him, he would try to convince it.
Perhaps he would threaten it, or perhaps he would promise it more power, but apparently, Lian was truly ready to respect its choice.
And kill it.
The young man’s fingers slowly closed into a fist.
The Sovereign looked at his hand, its entire body was still in pain from the previous punch, and even the thought of being struck by that fist again made its injured muscles tense up instinctively.
Lian took a step closer, but just before he could strike
"Lian."
Seris’s voice rang out, he turned his head toward the girl, and she kept her gaze on the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"Do you really want to keep it?"
Lian remained silent for a moment, then nodded.
"If it agrees."
Seris turned her gaze toward him.
"Aria."
Just one word, but its meaning was completely clear to both of them.
He turned his gaze back to the monster.
"I haven’t forgotten, I haven’t forgotten Aria or the other people it killed."
He remained silent for a few seconds.
"But its death won’t bring them back, if I can keep all its abilities under control, it won’t be able to do those things again."
Seris said nothing.
"An Unholy monster with this much intelligence and growth potential could be a valuable member, especially if I force it to use all its abilities for a different purpose."
Then he looked at the Sovereign.
"Of course, it only gets one chance."
The young Pendragon looked at him for a few moments, she still hated that creature.
But she knew how useful it could be to have a monster as a subordinate.
One and Two could no longer act against Lian’s main commands after accepting the bond.
If this creature really joined the colony, it would no longer have the freedom it once had either.
In that case, even the monster itself might be of much greater help than its corpse.
Seris finally gave a small nod.
"Alright."
However, it still had no intention of giving in, it struggled to raise its head.
"I said...
I’d rather die!"
Lian let out a short sigh.
"Fine."
This time, he truly prepared to bring his fist down, but at that very moment, an idea crossed his mind, and his gaze remained on the monster’s face for a moment.
A creature that had spent thirty years trying to use a human body without losing its own monster power.
A creature that believed no ordinary human could withstand its existence energy.
He gave a faint smile.
’Maybe I should show it something interesting before it dies.’
"By the way, I have a question."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign looked at him with hatred.
"What?"
"You spent thirty years searching for a human body that could withstand the power of an Unholy monster, right?"
The monster frowned.
"So what?"
Lian did not answer.
Instead, he released a very small amount of Eclipse Energy from his Eclipse Core.
The faint light shining through the clouds and reaching the area changed around his right hand, and black lines appeared within the light.
Eclipse Energy moved along the paths of the light, and several thin strands of corrupted light formed around Lian’s fingers.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign did not move for a moment, its gaze fixed on the young man’s hand.
At first, it thought it was facing some kind of dark energy, but it soon realized that its nature was different from ordinary mana.
A deep pressure rose from within it.
Not because of the amount of energy, but because of its quality, the monster instinctively lowered its head.
This...
Its instincts had reacted, it felt as if a being of a much higher rank had entered its territory.
But this time, the pressure came from only a few tiny strands of energy.
"What is that...?"
Lian gave a small smile
"Something simple."
That answer did nothing to calm the monster, because it had recognized the energy, not its exact source, but it had recognized its rank, the energy belonged to a being of the Demon rank!
How could this human use something that belonged to a Demon?

chapters.title: Chapter 599: The Three ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: For a moment, the Dreadmaw Sovereign felt as if all the blood in its body had turned cold.
How?
Why could a human keep a Demon’s energy inside his own body?
Had he found a treasure that belonged to a Demon?
Had he made a contract with a being of that rank?
Or did another thought cross its mind.
But before it could finish that thought, Lian raised his left hand as well.
Inside his body, the End Core reacted.
A very small amount of End Energy moved along his fingers.
Unlike Eclipse Energy, no black light formed around this hand.
Instead, part of the mana flowing out of the Sovereign’s body became disconnected for a moment as it approached Lian’s fingers.
A strand of red mana that still remained around the monster’s injured shoulder came into contact with that energy.
And then, without an explosion, without burning, and without even leaving scattered particles behind, the rest of its structure was cut off.
It was as if it was never supposed to exist beyond that point.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign held its breath, its gaze moving between the two hands of the young Vorhelm.
The energy in his right hand was wearing down the structure of mana.
But the energy in his left hand? That one was something completely different.
And even more terrifying.
Its instincts gave it the same warning again.
Another demonic nature, but not from the same source as the previous one, it was something else.
Two independent natures, two different sources, and both belonged to ranks far above its own existence.
The monster felt its spine turn cold.
Its voice barely came out.
"Impossible..."
Lian looked at it.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign instinctively moved backward, but its injured body did not allow it to move very far.
Its lips were trembling.
"You’re using the power of two Demons?!"
The young Vorhelm said nothing, but his silence felt heavier to the monster than any answer.
The Sovereign moved its gaze from the young man’s two hands to his face, it could no longer believe what it was seeing.
A human could not withstand two different demonic natures so easily.
Even many powerful monsters could damage their own existence structure and be destroyed if they absorbed incompatible energy from a Demon.

But this young man was not only alive, he was also controlling two different sources at the same time, without his body falling apart, without his mana going out of control, and without the slightest sign of pressure.
The monster slowly moved its head back, and a terrifying thought formed in its mind.
Perhaps...
Its gaze remained fixed on Lian’s human face... perhaps he was not human at all...!
It had spent thirty years searching for a human who could withstand its monster power, thirty years looking for a way to obtain human skin and enter the Seven Regions.
But now, a being stood in front of it who had a human appearance while keeping two different demonic powers inside his own body.
Could he be a Demon?
This possibility made all its pride collapse for a moment.
If the one standing before it was truly a Demon in human form, then it had never stood a chance of winning.
Even Unholy Last Blood would mean very little against a being of that rank.
"What... are you, really?" the Sovereign asked in a trembling voice.
"Someone who came to see you for the second time." Lian tilted his head slightly, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
That was all.
He gave no further explanation, revealed nothing about the origins of the Cores, and did not even try to correct the monster’s misunderstanding.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign remained motionless for several seconds, it still did not know the answer to its question, but for the first time, it felt that perhaps it was better not to know.
The young Vorhelm controlled the Eclipse Energy and End Energy, there was no reason to use any more of the energy stored in the two Cores.
That short display was enough.
He lowered his hands and stood in front of the Dreadmaw Sovereign again.
"Well, have you changed your mind?"
No answer came for a while.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign looked at the broken rocks around it, at the place it had once considered its sacred hall.
At the remains of its black throne, and at the cracks spread across the mountains after its thirty-year plan had been destroyed.
And finally, at the two humans standing in front of it.
Seris held her sword beside her body.
No pressure was coming from her skill anymore, but the monster knew that if it made even the slightest hostile move, the girl could react before its attack reached her.
Lian was also standing calmly, but it could no longer say with confidence that this young man was truly human.
Damn him.
How could everything have changed like this?
There had been a time when it was close to killing these two with a single movement of its finger.
Now, even after releasing all its abilities and activating Unholy Last Blood, it had failed to seriously injure them.
More importantly, the young man standing before it probably possessed the power of beings whose ranks were far above its own.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth, its hatred of humans was still there, and the same old anger remained deep inside it.
But now, another question occupied its mind.
If he really was a Demon...
Among monsters, differences in rank meant a great deal, serving a weak human was humiliating to it.
But serving a being of the Demon rank? That was completely different, even if that being had a human appearance.
It felt that the being standing in front of it only wore the appearance of a human, but was actually a Demon!
On the other hand, if it died now, all its efforts to evolve would also come to an end forever.
But if it survived, perhaps it would still have a chance to grow stronger.
Perhaps, under the command of this unknown being, it could reach a level it had only dreamed of before and take its revenge.
Of course, thinking this way did not mean its pride had disappeared.
It still hated surrendering, but death no longer seemed like an easy choice as it had a few minutes ago.
Besides, surrendering to a Demon... did not seem that humiliating, perhaps it could even be an honor?
"If I accept... what will happen?" the monster finally asked in a hoarse voice.
Lian gave a faint smile.
"You’ll obey my orders. You’re not allowed to harm innocent humans, take anyone’s heart for your experiments, or do the same things you were doing in these mountains again."
His gaze grew colder for a moment.
"And if you think I’m forgiving you for your past, you’re wrong, I’ve only decided to use your power instead of killing you, but this chance won’t last forever."
The monster slowly breathed out, and for a moment, its gaze fell on Seris.
The girl said nothing, she simply waited for its decision with the same cold gaze as always.
The Sovereign looked at Lian again.
"And what if I want to disobey you one day?"
"You can’t." The young Vorhelm replied, he did not explain the exact reason, but naturally, it was because the Colony would not allow such a thing.
Silence lasted for several seconds.
The monster could understand what this meant, if it accepted the bond, it would no longer be free as it had been before, and if it dared to disobey, this superior being, this Demon, would kill it.
Lian’s main commands would become binding on it, but in return, it would survive.
And perhaps it would have a chance to continue evolving.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign lowered its head.
For several seconds, the only sound was the cold wind passing through the mountain ruins.
Then, its large lips slowly moved.
"I accept."
"Good."
Without delay, he activated the [Colony Sovereign] Talent.
A flow of mana formed around the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s body.
The monster raised its head for a moment, it felt strange.
It was as if invisible threads were forming deep within its existence and connecting it to a point far beyond its physical body.
But unlike what it had expected, this force did not seem to be trying to erase its identity.
Its memories remained, and its hatred of humans did not disappear either, it was still itself, but a new bond was forming in the deepest part of its existence.
A bond that established Lian’s position as its ruler and god.
At that same moment, a blue window appeared in front of Lian.
[ Colony Sovereign Talent Activated ]
[ Target: Dreadmaw Sovereign ]
[ Level: 20 ]
[ Rank: Unholy ]
[ Target has accepted the special colony member bond ]
[ Current Special Member Capacity: 2/5 ]
[ Forming New Bond... ]
He waited for several seconds.
The mana around the monster grew denser, and the Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth.
A deep pressure passed through the structure of its existence, but this time, it did not try to resist.
It had made its own choice, and there was no longer any chance to change its decision.
[ Special Member Bond Successfully Established ]
[ Please assign a name to the new member ]
Lian looked at the kneeling creature, the Dreadmaw Sovereign, the monster that had considered itself the god of the mountains for thirty years.
The same monster that had once been so much stronger than him that he could not even resist a single movement of its finger.
But now?
That proud Sovereign was no longer even the master of its own fate.
Lian thought of the other two special members of the Colony.
One.
Two.
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"From now on... your name is Three."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign raised its head.
"Three...? This majesty is named what?"
But before it could protest, the system’s final window appeared.
[ Third Special Colony Member Registered ]
[ Name: Three ]
[ Special Colony Members: 3/5 ]

chapters.title: Chapter 600: One, Two, and... Three?!
paragraphs: "Three?"
The rough voice of the Dreadmaw Sovereign echoed through the mountain ruins.

The three-meter-tall monster was still on one knee, its red skin was split in several places, dark blood was flowing from its shoulder and side, and its heavy breathing showed that even though the battle was over, its physical condition was still far from good.
But at this moment, the pain from its wounds seemed to be the least of its concerns, all its attention was focused on what it had heard.
[ Name: Three ]
[ Special Colony Member: 3/5 ]
The Sovereign blinked several times.
Then it slowly raised its head and looked at the young man standing a short distance away.
"My name... is Three now?"
Lian, who was checking the status of the newly formed bond, answered without raising his head.
"Yeah."
"Three?!"
"I heard you."
The Sovereign kept its mouth open for a moment, then struggled to get up from the ground, although the severe pain in its side forced it to place a hand against one of the broken rocks.
"I am the Dreadmaw Sovereign! An Unholy creature that has ruled these mountains for thirty years! Even the powerful monsters in this region didn’t dare to enter my territory without permission!"
The young Vorhelm finally raised his gaze.

For a few seconds, he looked at the mountains, almost half of which had been destroyed by the Sovereign itself, collapsed rocks, destroyed trees, and the remains of the old cave were scattered across the slopes for a long distance.
Then he looked at the monster again.
"Well, there aren’t many creatures left around here now."
The corners of Seris’s lips, as she stood beside him, lifted slightly for a moment.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth.
"I mean, I deserve a better name!"
The young Vorhelm calmly nodded.
"Maybe, but the two previous members have similar names, if I make an exception for you, the others might get jealous."
The monster fell silent for a moment.
"The two previous members?"
"One and Two."
"What?"
"One and Two, I don’t think they’re that hard to remember."
The Sovereign stared at him in disbelief for several seconds.
It had expected that after accepting the bond, it might receive a title that matched its rank and greatness.
At the very least, it expected a name that reminded it of its former rule.
But this man hadn’t even bothered to come up with a proper name for it!
"So I’m an Unholy monster, and I come after two other creatures?"
Lian shrugged.
"In terms of membership order, yeah."
The Sovereign was about to make another complaint, but just as it opened its mouth, a brief pressure passed through its existence from the Colony Bond.
It wasn’t strong enough to cause pain, it was simply a clear reminder of its new position, it was no longer the independent ruler of these mountains.
And that truth bothered it even more than its new name.
After making sure the bond was stable, Lian lowered his hand.
"Well, now that we’ve finished talking about names, let’s make a few things clear."
The Sovereign looked at him with displeasure.
"I still—"
"First, you’re no longer allowed to hunt innocent humans, second, experimenting on the bodies and hearts of living creatures is forbidden."
His voice was still calm, but there was no sign of humor in it this time.

The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth for a moment, it was clearly unhappy with these restrictions, but the bond it had accepted itself would not allow it to ignore the Colony Master’s direct commands.
"And what if I want to evolve?" The monster raised its head.
"I still need resources for my first evolution."
"Hunt monsters, find other ways to grow stronger, you have plenty of options."
"Is it that simple?"
Lian gave a faint smile.
"After spending thirty years trying to create a human body, I expect you to be able to find other ways too.
The Sovereign said nothing.
Seris also looked at the wounded creature from beside him. She still hated it, but at least now she knew that the former ruler of the mountains no longer had the freedom it once enjoyed.
Lian’s gaze moved over the monster’s deep wounds.

"For now, you should rest too." He looked at the Sovereign’s deep wounds. "You still haven’t recovered a large part of your life force, and in this condition, you can’t fight properly even if you want to."
The monster raised its head with displeasure.
"Where?"
"The Colony House."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign wanted to ask about this place, but before it could say anything, Lian activated the [Hive Dominion] skill.
At that moment, a faint light came out of the monster’s body.
The Sovereign looked at its hands in disbelief. Its red skin was slowly breaking down into thousands of tiny particles of light.
The process caused no pain, but the feeling of its body slowly disappearing was not pleasant for a creature that had spent its entire life taking pride in its physical strength.
A few moments later, thousands of glowing points gathered together and all disappeared at once.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign vanished from the ruined mountain slope.
But Lian and Seris were still standing in the same place.
Inside the Colony House, thousands of particles of light appeared in an empty spot.
The particles slowly joined together, and after a few seconds, the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s huge, three-meter-tall body took shape again.
The monster cautiously took a step, first looking at its hands and then at the surroundings.
The cold mountain wind and broken rocks were gone, a wide and quiet space lay before it, with gentle energy flowing through it and areas set aside for the Colony members to rest and recover.
The Sovereign frowned.
So this was its new home?
Before it could take a closer look, a deep growl came from its right.
It turned its head, and a huge creature was not far away.
A giant ant with a hard, dark shell, old scars could be seen on parts of its body, and its large size and strong body structure immediately caught the eye.
One.
The ant had raised its head after sensing the arrival of a new member, its antennae moved slowly, and its gaze remained fixed on the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
Then another short growl came from its throat, this time, the sound was not entirely friendly.
For a few moments, the two monsters looked at each other.
Then the Dreadmaw Sovereign asked mockingly.
"What kind of creature are you?"
One only moved its antennae.
Then it shifted its huge body slightly and settled back into its resting place, although it still hadn’t completely taken its eyes off the new member.
Dreadmaw remained silent for several seconds.
An ant?
It had expected that after entering the Colony of a being who possessed the power of two Demons, it would encounter terrifying and strange monsters.
Of course, this ant was neither small nor weak.
But still, the first special member of the Colony was an ant?
The Dreadmaw Sovereign had not yet managed to accept this when another presence caught its attention.
A heavy pressure reached it from a more distant part of the Colony House, and the monster turned its head.
There, a huge wolf with a bony body was resting.
Two.
The Wolf of Eight Disasters opened its eyes after sensing the arrival of the new creature.
It gave the Sovereign a brief look, neither growling nor getting up, and it did not even show any interest in making contact.
But that brief look was enough for the Dreadmaw Sovereign to notice something unusual.
The dense energy inside the wolf’s body, the pressure of its presence, and the calmness that could only be seen in creatures that had survived many deadly battles.
This wolf...
The Sovereign narrowed its eyes.
Although it was an Unholy monster itself, it could clearly tell that the creature before it was no ordinary monster.
The wolf’s power was far beyond what its calm appearance suggested, and more importantly, it didn’t seem interested in showing off its strength.
After that brief look, Two placed its head back on its legs and closed its eyes.
Apparently, the new Colony member was not important enough to disturb its rest.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign remained motionless for several seconds, then shifted its gaze between the giant ant and the wolf.
So these two were really One and Two?
For a moment, it thought about the fact that it, an Unholy creature, had now become the third special member of a Colony whose two previous members were an ant and a wolf.
Of course, after sensing Two’s presence, it was no longer so sure that it should feel humiliated by this.
Even so, one thing still bothered it.
Three...
It gritted its teeth.
"I really hate this name."
One let out another short growl after hearing its voice.
The Sovereign looked at the ant.
"What? Do you have a problem?"
One moved its antennae and turned its huge body slightly toward it.
Dreadmaw only growled and ignored it, then walked toward an empty spot suitable for resting with a displeased look.

The Sovereign immediately raised its head.
"Wait! We still haven’t settled the matter of my name—"

Seris was standing beside him.

He nodded.
"Yeah. It’ll rest there for now."
The girl glanced at the place where the Dreadmaw Sovereign had disappeared a few moments earlier.
"What about One and Two?"
"They’re inside too, they’re still recovering from their previous injuries."
She nodded.
"Good."
Lian gave a small smile.
"Though I don’t think Three is very happy about meeting its new housemates."
The young Pendragon looked at him.
"Why?"
"Apparently, it still hasn’t accepted the fact that it joined the Colony after an ant and a wolf."
The corner of the girl’s mouth lifted slightly.
"It’ll get used to it."
"I think so too."
Then he looked toward the ruined peak, the same place where he had once nearly lost his life.
Now, not only had he survived that old battle and returned, but the creature he once couldn’t even resist had become the third special member of his Colony.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"Well, I think this one’s over too."
She nodded.
"Yeah."
Lian looked at the sky, then turned back to the girl beside him.
"I’m going back to the academy."
"The academy?"
"I have some unfinished business there, and I also need to prepare for a trip."
The girl remained silent for a few seconds.
"Where?"
Lian raised an eyebrow for a moment, only then realizing that he hadn’t told her about his plans for the trip.
"I’m going to the Land of First Dawn."

sentences.text: "Three?"
The rough voice of the Dreadmaw Sovereign echoed through the mountain ruins.

The three-meter-tall monster was still on one knee, its red skin was split in several places, dark blood was flowing from its shoulder and side, and its heavy breathing showed that even though the battle was over, its physical condition was still far from good.
But at this moment, the pain from its wounds seemed to be the least of its concerns, all its attention was focused on what it had heard.
[ Name: Three ]
[ Special Colony Member: 3/5 ]
The Sovereign blinked several times.
Then it slowly raised its head and looked at the young man standing a short distance away.
"My name... is Three now?"
Lian, who was checking the status of the newly formed bond, answered without raising his head.
"Yeah."
"Three?!"
"I heard you."
The Sovereign kept its mouth open for a moment, then struggled to get up from the ground, although the severe pain in its side forced it to place a hand against one of the broken rocks.
"I am the Dreadmaw Sovereign!
An Unholy creature that has ruled these mountains for thirty years!
Even the powerful monsters in this region didn’t dare to enter my territory without permission!"
The young Vorhelm finally raised his gaze.

For a few seconds, he looked at the mountains, almost half of which had been destroyed by the Sovereign itself, collapsed rocks, destroyed trees, and the remains of the old cave were scattered across the slopes for a long distance.
Then he looked at the monster again.
"Well, there aren’t many creatures left around here now."
The corners of Seris’s lips, as she stood beside him, lifted slightly for a moment.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth.
"I mean, I deserve a better name!"
The young Vorhelm calmly nodded.
"Maybe, but the two previous members have similar names, if I make an exception for you, the others might get jealous."
The monster fell silent for a moment.
"The two previous members?"
"One and Two."
"What?"
"One and Two, I don’t think they’re that hard to remember."
The Sovereign stared at him in disbelief for several seconds.
It had expected that after accepting the bond, it might receive a title that matched its rank and greatness.
At the very least, it expected a name that reminded it of its former rule.
But this man hadn’t even bothered to come up with a proper name for it!
"So I’m an Unholy monster, and I come after two other creatures?"
Lian shrugged.
"In terms of membership order, yeah."
The Sovereign was about to make another complaint, but just as it opened its mouth, a brief pressure passed through its existence from the Colony Bond.
It wasn’t strong enough to cause pain, it was simply a clear reminder of its new position, it was no longer the independent ruler of these mountains.
And that truth bothered it even more than its new name.
After making sure the bond was stable, Lian lowered his hand.
"Well, now that we’ve finished talking about names, let’s make a few things clear."
The Sovereign looked at him with displeasure.
"I still—"
"First, you’re no longer allowed to hunt innocent humans, second, experimenting on the bodies and hearts of living creatures is forbidden."
His voice was still calm, but there was no sign of humor in it this time.

The Dreadmaw Sovereign gritted its teeth for a moment, it was clearly unhappy with these restrictions, but the bond it had accepted itself would not allow it to ignore the Colony Master’s direct commands.
"And what if I want to evolve?" The monster raised its head.
"I still need resources for my first evolution."
"Hunt monsters, find other ways to grow stronger, you have plenty of options."
"Is it that simple?"
Lian gave a faint smile.
"After spending thirty years trying to create a human body, I expect you to be able to find other ways too.
The Sovereign said nothing.
Seris also looked at the wounded creature from beside him.
She still hated it, but at least now she knew that the former ruler of the mountains no longer had the freedom it once enjoyed.
Lian’s gaze moved over the monster’s deep wounds.
"For now, you should rest too." He looked at the Sovereign’s deep wounds.
"You still haven’t recovered a large part of your life force, and in this condition, you can’t fight properly even if you want to."
The monster raised its head with displeasure.
"Where?"
"The Colony House."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign wanted to ask about this place, but before it could say anything, Lian activated the [Hive Dominion] skill.
At that moment, a faint light came out of the monster’s body.
The Sovereign looked at its hands in disbelief.
Its red skin was slowly breaking down into thousands of tiny particles of light.
The process caused no pain, but the feeling of its body slowly disappearing was not pleasant for a creature that had spent its entire life taking pride in its physical strength.
A few moments later, thousands of glowing points gathered together and all disappeared at once.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign vanished from the ruined mountain slope.
But Lian and Seris were still standing in the same place.
Inside the Colony House, thousands of particles of light appeared in an empty spot.
The particles slowly joined together, and after a few seconds, the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s huge, three-meter-tall body took shape again.
The monster cautiously took a step, first looking at its hands and then at the surroundings.
The cold mountain wind and broken rocks were gone, a wide and quiet space lay before it, with gentle energy flowing through it and areas set aside for the Colony members to rest and recover.
The Sovereign frowned.
So this was its new home?
Before it could take a closer look, a deep growl came from its right.
It turned its head, and a huge creature was not far away.
A giant ant with a hard, dark shell, old scars could be seen on parts of its body, and its large size and strong body structure immediately caught the eye.
One.
The ant had raised its head after sensing the arrival of a new member, its antennae moved slowly, and its gaze remained fixed on the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
Then another short growl came from its throat, this time, the sound was not entirely friendly.
For a few moments, the two monsters looked at each other.
Then the Dreadmaw Sovereign asked mockingly.
"What kind of creature are you?"
One only moved its antennae.
Then it shifted its huge body slightly and settled back into its resting place, although it still hadn’t completely taken its eyes off the new member.
Dreadmaw remained silent for several seconds.
An ant?
It had expected that after entering the Colony of a being who possessed the power of two Demons, it would encounter terrifying and strange monsters.
Of course, this ant was neither small nor weak.
But still, the first special member of the Colony was an ant?
The Dreadmaw Sovereign had not yet managed to accept this when another presence caught its attention.
A heavy pressure reached it from a more distant part of the Colony House, and the monster turned its head.
There, a huge wolf with a bony body was resting.
Two.
The Wolf of Eight Disasters opened its eyes after sensing the arrival of the new creature.
It gave the Sovereign a brief look, neither growling nor getting up, and it did not even show any interest in making contact.
But that brief look was enough for the Dreadmaw Sovereign to notice something unusual.
The dense energy inside the wolf’s body, the pressure of its presence, and the calmness that could only be seen in creatures that had survived many deadly battles.
This wolf...
The Sovereign narrowed its eyes.
Although it was an Unholy monster itself, it could clearly tell that the creature before it was no ordinary monster.
The wolf’s power was far beyond what its calm appearance suggested, and more importantly, it didn’t seem interested in showing off its strength.
After that brief look, Two placed its head back on its legs and closed its eyes.
Apparently, the new Colony member was not important enough to disturb its rest.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign remained motionless for several seconds, then shifted its gaze between the giant ant and the wolf.
So these two were really One and Two?
For a moment, it thought about the fact that it, an Unholy creature, had now become the third special member of a Colony whose two previous members were an ant and a wolf.
Of course, after sensing Two’s presence, it was no longer so sure that it should feel humiliated by this.
Even so, one thing still bothered it.
Three...

"I really hate this name."
